A tool requiring human interaction belongs in the usability pilot, rather than being recorded as an unsupported unattended arm.

Declare which question is being tested:

  • Equal-budget comparison: match the available model family, reasoning, context, total inference allowance and task time across arms. Report where a workflow cannot meet those constraints.
  • Whole-workflow comparison: use each workflow's intended coder/reviewer configuration. Report extra model turns, time and measured expense alongside outcome. A four-turn team beating a one-turn baseline does not isolate an orchestration effect.

Run only after reviewing the commands and native profiles:

python3 scripts/compare-workflows.py --config /private/study/plan.json \
  --output /private/study/run-NEW --allow-models

--allow-models authorizes live arms and their potential charges. A fixture plan instead requires --fixtures; those modes cannot be combined. The declaration is an operator-controlled label, not an executable classifier or a sandbox. No provider calls are required to prepare the plan or run the offline controls.

For each repeat and task, the runner rotates arm order; alternate complete blocks reverse it. Use a multiple of twice the arm count for full position and direction balance. This deterministic ordering is recorded and reproducible; it is not randomized sampling. Run arms serially on otherwise comparable hosts and control caches, provider limits, previous conversation context and service changes. Do not silently rerun a failed attempt. Any replacement must retain the original and be reported as an additional declared run.

docs.title: Inspect evidence and its limits
docs.text:
The new output directory is mode 0700. It retains the configuration, its hash, source commit/content fingerprint, attempt repositories, actor/check logs, artifacts and comparison.json. A source snapshot accepts only regular tracked files; symlinks, submodules, ambiguous paths, trees over 10,000 files or 128 MiB are refused. Source Git reads disable optional locks, lazy fetching and inherited Git configuration, replacement objects and graft files. Only the pinned commit's tree is read, not a history traversal. Partial/promisor sources are refused, and Git transports are disabled, including on Git versions without the lazy-fetch guard. Source preparation and materialization share the overall deadline; each Git subprocess is additionally limited to 30 seconds. Each attempt gets its own initialized object store, with no worktree, alternates or source-object borrowing. Dirty, staged and untracked source files are not task inputs. Git configuration inherited by commands is also cleared so environment-based Git redirection cannot target the source.

Read completed, planned_attempts, each attempt's completed/passed, actor status and every independent check. Failed actors are graded too, preserving partial outcomes. A zero actor exit cannot override a failed check, and a good artifact cannot override a nonzero or timed-out actor. Missing/interrupted final evidence is not success. The runner's exit status is zero only if every planned attempt completes and passes; mixed success is normal study data and returns nonzero. Analyze all attempted outcomes, including setup failures, timeouts and incorrect patches, using the declared exclusion rules.

Elapsed wall time includes local command execution and process cleanup. Token usage and cost are explicitly unknown in this schema, even for successful attempts. Obtain independent provider receipts or native metering and bind them to attempt IDs before making cost claims; unknown is never zero. No aggregate score or product ranking is generated. Report per-task outcomes, uncertainty, sample sizes and configuration differences instead of treating a small average as a general winner.

The commands and checks are trusted local code. This runner is not a sandbox, disk quota or provider billing cap. The controller uses pinned Linux process identities to stop observed descendants when a command ends or times out. Very short-lived detached descendants can escape observation, and independent host services remain outside that boundary. For hostile code or strict process containment, run each entire attempt in a separately enforced disposable environment. Logs and repositories may contain prompts, credentials and proprietary code; review and redact evidence before publishing it.

docs.title: Summarize retained comparison evidence
docs.text:
The offline summary reads the frozen configuration and comparison.json from one evidence directory. It invokes no actor, grader, Git command or provider:

Run these commands from a source checkout or extract the scripts directory from the matching release archive. The binary installer installs only amx. Keep the extracted scripts together and use an absolute Python script path when running the report outside that directory.

python3 scripts/summarize-comparison.py /private/study/run-NEW
python3 scripts/summarize-comparison.py /private/study/run-NEW --json \
  > /private/study/comparison-summary.json

It checks the recorded configuration hash, source commit pin, planned order, attempt/check identities and verdict consistency before reporting. Inputs are limited to regular, non-symlink JSON files of 16 MiB each and 200 planned attempts. Invalid or contradictory evidence exits nonzero without echoing its paths or error contents. This is a consistency check of retained records; it does not rerun grading or authenticate the grader, logs or candidate bytes.

Per-arm totals keep planned, attempted, completed, passed, failed, incomplete and unstarted attempts separate. Actor/check timeouts and cleanup failures remain visible. cleanup_failures counts command records containing one or more cleanup errors, not individual errors or processes. A valid summary exits zero even when the recorded study contains failed attempts; that exit status does not change the runner's verdict.

Pairwise timing ratios use the same task and repeat, and include only pairs where both actors and all independent checks passed with known, positive, finite durations. Every other outcome remains in the paired counts. The number of usable timing pairs is explicit; a missing or zero duration does not become a measured speedup. Timings include actor execution and cleanup, excluding source preparation and independent grading.

The summary retains declared arm names and input/configuration hashes, while omitting source paths, prompts, argv, logs and raw errors. Review arm names before sharing. Human interventions, inference requests, tokens and cost remain null. Fixture runs are labeled not an AI benchmark. Repeated runs of one task are not independent task samples; no confidence interval, overall score or winner is inferred.

docs.title: Grade artifacts without revealing the arm
docs.text: Before collecting results, define a rubric for functional correctness, regressions, maintainability and unnecessary changes. Have a separate person export proposed file changes under neutral attempt IDs, remove tool-identifying metadata where feasible, and retain the mapping privately. Give graders the same pinned task, acceptance contract and development context, excluding arm names, transcripts and elapsed time. Do not label missing artifacts as missing data to be discarded: record the declared failure outcome. Two independent graders should score artifacts before discussing disagreements; record both scores, agreement and an adjudicated result. State where patch style or native metadata makes full blinding impossible. Functional checks complement grading; neither alone proves arbitrary task correctness.

docs.title: Run a small usability pilot
docs.text:
Recruit 6–8 developers who did not build Agentmux and represent its intended power-user audience. Include experienced CLI/tmux users and record prior familiarity with Agentmux and the comparison tool. Evaluate novices separately if making beginner-accessibility claims. Treat this as a qualitative pilot, not a statistically powered product ranking. Counterbalance the order of Agentmux and the selected alternative. Give each participant an equivalent disposable repository and the same tasks: install, resume a workspace, launch two agents, delegate a task, find an agent needing attention, inspect the exact delegated task, review/apply a change, revoke collaboration and recover an interrupted task. Predeclare task completion criteria and a time limit. Keep a facilitator script and separate unassisted performance from assistance.

Record successful completion, time, navigation mistakes, permission surprises, recovery failures and help needed. Ask participants to explain what they believe the controls allow before revealing the answer. Follow with a consistent short usability questionnaire and an interview. Retain failures and observations, then fix repeated problems and repeat the pilot with fresh participants. Never present these small-sample preferences as evidence of better coding quality.

docs.title: Evidence needed for a strong rating
docs.text:
A future 9/10 assessment needs delivered behavior and independent evidence, not a larger feature list or a self-assigned score. Set thresholds before collecting data and publish the failures as well as successes:

Dimension Evidence that would justify reconsidering a high rating First-run usability Fresh users complete the core journey without developer assistance; predefined completion/time thresholds hold across supported platforms. Reliability Repeated realistic native-provider runs, restart/credential-refresh faults and multi-day observation meet a declared failure/recovery target; no silently lost tasks or falsely passing evidence. Task value A representative, adequately sized matched study shows useful outcomes against single-agent and relevant competitor baselines, with blinded grading and uncertainty. Safety and authority Independent adversarial review confirms the declared boundaries and failure behavior; fixes are retained as regressions. Maintainability and distribution Released, reproducible install paths; tested upgrades; bounded compatibility support; independently reproduced fixes and contributions.

Agree on quantitative thresholds and sample-size justification for the target users before the study. An illustrative target is a high unassisted core-task completion rate with no serious permission misunderstanding, but a small pilot cannot establish that rate. Passing the evaluator or meeting one dimension's target does not automatically upgrade the overall rating. Public stars and downloads can describe reach; they do not establish correctness or superiority.

docs.title: Prepare a native-subscription pilot
docs.text:
The repository includes a small whole-workflow pilot, separate from a representative benchmark or human usability study. Three selected tasks use historical source d52e940c473be6a3b7d7983a704e2bac9547e6de: escaped native credential redaction, authenticated trace display during concurrent mutation, and a reusable worker credential-discovery refactor. A separate reviewer wrote external Go-overlay graders and checked that the historical source fails and the corrected implementation passes. These selected repository tasks do not establish general coding quality or productivity.

python3 scripts/test-subscription-pilot.py
python3 examples/evaluation/subscription-pilot.py prepare \
  --output /tmp/amx-subscription-pilot-NEW \
  --go /absolute/path/to/go --amx /absolute/path/to/pinned/amx
python3 examples/evaluation/subscription-pilot.py preflight \
  --manifest /tmp/amx-subscription-pilot-NEW/pilot.json

Preparation makes no model calls. It freezes private grader copies and records tool versions, executable/wrapper/grader hashes, model settings, native auth paths and the protocol. Preflight retains only the authentication route summary. It requires existing Codex ChatGPT authentication and Claude first-party Pro/Max authentication, refuses API/alternate-provider environment variables, and does not install tools or copy account credentials. Codex's authentication methods and forced login setting distinguish subscription access from API-key access. Model availability still depends on the account; an unavailable model is a retained setup failure.

Review plan.json, then explicitly start the six live attempts:

python3 scripts/compare-workflows.py \
  --config /tmp/amx-subscription-pilot-NEW/plan.json \
  --output /tmp/amx-subscription-pilot-NEW/results --allow-models

Each arm gets 480 seconds. The baseline permits one native Codex invocation; the original v0.13-era pinned pilot permits up to four native coder/reviewer invocations, one implementation attempt per phase and a 7m15s workflow deadline. Guided work in v0.14.0 can use two of those permitted turns after an exact initial approval, while still running final checks. Record actual executed and skipped phases for each pinned build; keep historical four-call route-smoke evidence unchanged. Neither a native CLI turn nor its allowance establishes the provider's inference-request count. Codex uses gpt-6.1-sol at medium reasoning; the Claude reviewer uses claude-sonnet-5-5 at medium effort, with no automatic model/provider fallback. The selected model pins can be changed explicitly when preparing a new study. Agentmux's retained plan can still name its sonnet profile alias; the pinned native wrapper supplies the recorded full reviewer model. This is a workflow comparison with different inference allowances, not an isolated orchestration experiment.

Failures and limit responses remain failures. No automatic paid fallback or retry is provided. Authentication status does not expose account billing or extra-usage entitlement, so these local controls do not establish a financial cap. Usage and cost remain unknown in the comparison schema. Native command output stays in private attempt files; review it before publishing. Changed pinned files invalidate the study: prepare a new directory, preserving existing records. Functional grading is external and frozen, but these trusted local arms can read host files; the graders are not hidden by an isolation boundary.

docs.title: Recorded exploratory pilot
docs.text:
The reviewed November 4 aggregate identifies the actual v0.14.0 controller, patched process tracker, frozen protocol and historical task seed. Native Codex passed 3/3 selected tasks; the Agentmux workflow passed 1/3. Its two failures hit the 180-second implementation profile limit before review/application, and the supervisor separately rejected observed background work. All tracked cleanup completed. The successful Agentmux arm used Codex plus Claude static review, then controller checks, external grading and fixture-only application.

Four earlier native admissions remain invalidated process-limit evidence; seven were admitted in the corrected frozen study. Comparable token usage, inference-request count, actual subscription cost and immutable served-model revisions remain unknown. No competitor UI or unaided human journey was included. Budget fixes and their later targeted validation are separate evidence, not replacements for these six original attempts or a basis to pool a better pass rate.

New comparison failures can retain at most 32 identity-checked background-process records with explicit omitted/unknown counts. Records contain safe executable basenames and numeric identity/group/session metadata, never argv, environment values or full paths. Diagnostic failure cannot replace the primary failure or skip cleanup. Review these private records before sharing them.

docs.title: Targeted regression validation
docs.text:
The separate November 4 regression record covers only credential redaction and authenticated trace display. Both passed 2/2 using the clean 0.15.0-rc1 source build 45ceb620…, not a published release archive, with the same historical seed and frozen primary graders. The v0.15.0 release's cmd and internal trees match that RC; the native runs still used the source build, rather than the published archive. Both roles had 435-second limits within a shared 435-second mission and a 480-second outer attempt. Each used Codex implementation and Claude static review, mandatory final checks and fixture-only application. Four additional native CLI admissions brought this private sequence to fifteen.

The redaction implementation's extra package race-test command encountered four Unix-socket permission errors inside the native sandbox; subsequent focused checks and the frozen contract passed. No full-suite success is claimed. The original native 3/3 versus Agentmux 1/3 remains unchanged: no baseline was rerun and no pass rates are pooled. Requested aliases remained the same; served model revisions remain unverified. These targeted rechecks establish no speedup or general competitive advantage.

docs.title: Add an operator trial with Agent Deck
docs.text:
Agent Deck's official CLI reference documents native session management and session send --wait --json. It has its own completion/confirmation semantics and native hook setup. An unattended adapter has not been validated here; its absence from the six attempts is not a failed competitor result.

For an operator comparison, pin the Agent Deck release/binary and use a private disposable profile, XDG directories and tmux socket. Give the operator the same source commit, task, model settings, development checks and eight-minute limit. Record setup separately from task time, capture every operator intervention, retain the native delivery/confirmation fields, then grade the resulting patch with the same frozen grader. Use its supported launch/send controls rather than equating an idle pane or zero command exit with task completion. Keep results separate until the adapter and supervision/cleanup have their own controls.

docs.title: Single-task experiment pilots
docs.text:
amx experiment runs finite, auditable comparisons on the managed runtime. It creates a fresh broker, credentials, workspaces, homes, and private/shared memory for every trial. Agents within a trial run concurrently; trials run serially. Tmux is not required.

Use this runner for a finite instruction/assertion matrix. Use amx research for repeated-round decisions, private observations, scarce resources, dynamic populations, declared behavioral outcomes, role/personality treatments and counterbalanced factorial designs. Those are distinct manifest schemas; research fields are not accepted by an experiment manifest.

For coding alternatives with retained patches and executable checks, use amx flow run or amx flow lab. For one implementation and fresh-review journey, use amx work. These coding workflows use separate plans and do not create experimental payoff observations.

The included command fixtures validate orchestration and scoring. They do not produce evidence about agent cooperation, competition, or personality.

go build -o /tmp/amx ./cmd/agentmux
/tmp/amx experiment plan examples/experiments/pilot.yaml
/tmp/amx experiment run examples/experiments/pilot.yaml --output /tmp/amx-pilot

Use a new, empty output directory. Existing output must be private (0700). Choose a short path: each trial's Unix socket path must fit within 100 bytes. The example uses only /bin/sh and makes no model calls.

docs.title: Observe a running pilot
docs.text:
Each new attempt prints its active state directory and exact dashboard, web and managed activity commands on stderr. Final stdout remains JSON. A private atomic OUTPUT/live.json records only kind, trial, attempt, state path, finite deadline and running/completed/interrupted state; completed cached trials do not pretend to launch another live attempt.

Open the printed owner console to inspect tasks, results, coordination, permissions and knowledge, or request task cancellation. Workers are headless single-task processes: there is no native tmux pane, and queued extra instructions are not guaranteed another worker turn. This legacy pilot has no phase pause or step control and does not independently classify pristine versus owner-assisted results. Owner broker mutations remain auditable, but manually steered outcomes should be treated as exploratory. Use the research runner for repeated phases, dynamic populations, explicit intervention accounting and automatic exclusion of assisted runs from default estimates.

docs.title: Manifest and execution
docs.text:
A manifest has version: 1, an id, a relative or absolute managed team YAML, trials (repetitions), seeds, randomization_seed, timeout_seconds, and max_concurrency: 1. Unknown fields and additional YAML documents are rejected. The matrix contains every condition/seed/repetition combination exactly once. Seed/repetition blocks and condition order are shuffled deterministically using randomization_seed. Planning performs no agent execution or provider calls.

Every condition supplies:

  • A unique id and an initial instructions entry for each configured agent.
  • visibility: board-only or direct.
  • reward_mode: shared, individual, or winner.
  • Optional reward_instructions describing the incentives to participants.
  • Optional assertions overriding the manifest's common owner-defined oracle.

board-only removes inter-agent direct message, ping, and instruction grants. Board ACLs continue to apply. direct preserves explicit configured grants and does not expand them. Both conditions retain the owner's initial task delivery. Dynamic spawning and team creation are disabled in this initial runner.

Each initial instruction is submitted by the authenticated owner. The managed worker adds the configured role, condition and seed, task/message provenance, and authenticated CLI instructions. Every task starts a fresh harness turn. There is no prescribed research leader unless one is present in the team roles. Original configured workdirs are replaced with empty, dedicated trial workspaces; source repositories and previous results are not copied in. Explicit read-only program dependencies remain configured and are captured as possible confounds.

Each agent receives AGENTMUX_EXPERIMENT_SEED and the seed in its role context. This seeds the runner's matrix and gives scenarios a reproducible input; it does not seed a model's sampling, tool behavior, or asynchronous message ordering. Model calls and live reruns can differ.

docs.title: Independent scoring and payoffs
docs.text:
An assertion has an agent, exactly one exact or nonempty contains string, and an optional positive weight (default one). It evaluates the published task result only after a successful submission. Failed/cancelled tasks score zero. Assertions and expected answers stay in the owner artifact directory; they are not inserted into participant prompts or mounted as broker state.

The objective score is the sum of that agent's passing assertion weights:

Reward mode Computed payoff shared Every agent receives the sum of all objective scores. individual Each agent receives its own objective score. winner One unit is split among agents tied for the highest positive score; all-zero outcomes pay zero.

These are deterministic, recorded post-run payoffs. There are no live transfers, scarce-resource game mechanics, or repeated-round payoff feedback in this initial runner. Merely naming a condition "competitive" does not establish a scientifically consequential competitive environment. The incentive framing and actual payoff rule are recorded separately.

An agent's initial task is verified only if all of its assertions pass. A submitted response, a completed model turn, or "I succeeded" does not count as independent verification. Result truncation and known-secret redaction occur in the worker before scoring and are part of the measurement process.

docs.title: Artifacts and resuming
docs.text:
All files are private to the owner (0600, directories 0700). They can contain private messages, task content, memory, and explicit configuration secrets. Do not publish an output directory without reviewing it.

The output contains the normalized manifest and SHA-256 digest, randomized plan, and aggregate results.json. Each trial attempt contains:

  • started.json, result.json, and the exact initial instructions.json.
  • config.json: full normalized resolved configuration and its SHA-256 digest.
  • preflight.json: model/harness identifiers, resolved executable hashes, and native CLI versions where a bounded --version probe succeeds. Owner-defined command fixtures are hashed and are not run just to guess a version.
  • runner-calls.jsonl: owner requests and responses issued by the runner.
  • coordination.jsonl: complete paginated broker records, including messages, memory, task state, and coordination events. Lease secrets and credential tables are excluded; process environment values in agent records are redacted.
  • state/: the trial's durable managed state and private agent workspaces.

This is a coordination trace. It does not capture every native harness prompt, hidden model context, tool invocation, retrieval/read observation, or compaction event. Tool actions outside the broker are not a complete system trace. Provider usage is retained only where the adapter reports it and is not a spending cap.

Running the same manifest and resolved team against the same output skips completed trials. A different manifest/config digest is rejected. A partial, failed-infrastructure, or interrupted attempt is never silently retried:

# First stop any processes left by the interrupted attempt.
/tmp/amx experiment run examples/experiments/pilot.yaml \
  --output /tmp/amx-pilot --rerun-interrupted

Explicit reruns create a new attempt and preserve the old state. An exclusive output lock prevents two runners from mutating the same experiment. A completed trial with failed oracle assertions is still a completed observation and is not automatically repeated.

docs.title: Using real models
docs.text:
Replace the command fixtures with supported managed harnesses and connections. run additionally requires --allow-models because it can incur provider charges. Declare native credential files or explicit API-key references; fresh trial homes intentionally do not inherit native login/history directories automatically. Authentication availability is validated before accepting tasks.

Use sandbox: bubblewrap for supported Linux filesystem/process isolation. Provider calls require an explicit network policy: network: host grants unrestricted network access, while supported Bubblewrap managed harnesses may use network: allowlist with exact allowed origins/IP pins. See managed runtime network boundaries. local remains a trusted host process. Separate state/homes in local mode do not prevent a hostile agent from reading other trials or other host files. Isolation and information boundaries must be part of the experiment's declared conditions.

Begin with neutral roles, objective tasks, fixed populations, and strong single-agent/independent-agent baselines. This runner does not infer traits, measure causal effects automatically, determine statistical power, or implement a resource-allocation environment. Repeated tasks, controlled observation scheduling, richer payoff feedback, and harness-level input capture require additional scenario work before making stronger research claims.

docs.title: Managed execution hardening
docs.text:
These controls are opt-in. They fail closed when the requested boundary cannot be established. sandbox: local remains a trusted host process; it cannot enforce the network or disk boundaries below.

Disk caps require Bubblewrap with working --size support (introduced in 0.7.0), plus permitted user namespaces and tmpfs mounts. A namespace-only check is insufficient. Preflight verifies an actual capped filesystem before claiming work; an unsupported host must be upgraded instead of falling back to uncapped storage. CI builds the checksum-pinned official 0.13.1 release in a private prefix, retaining the runner's host security policy.

docs.title: Exact network destinations
docs.text:
agents:
  reviewer:
    harness: pi
    sandbox: bubblewrap
    network: allowlist
    egress:
      allow:
        - origin: http://127.0.0.1:11434
        - origin: https://api.example.com
          ips: [192.0.2.10] # Example only: replace with owner-approved addresses.

Each origin grants an exact scheme, hostname, and port. Paths, credentials, queries, fragments, wildcards, and redirects to other origins are not grants. Connection base_url may still include /v1; an egress origin does not include that API path. The example addresses above are placeholders.

The worker starts a private host-side Unix HTTP proxy. Bubblewrap creates a network namespace with no host network route, exposes only that worker's proxy socket, and starts a namespace-local loopback relay. The relay replaces all case variants of HTTP/HTTPS/ALL proxy variables and removes NO_PROXY. Clients which ignore these proxy variables fail to connect; host networking is never substituted.

DNS is resolved once when the worker starts and the proxy dials only those pinned addresses. Implicit DNS answers pointing at private/local addresses are rejected; an owner must select a literal address or supply explicit ips for a private service. An IP-literal origin cannot pin another address. Explicit pins also avoid changes in DNS answers during the worker's lifetime.

This section describes managed-mode networking. Full work/flow isolation instead uses the inspecting proxy described in the workflow guide. It checks each HTTP/1.1 Host and HTTP/2 authority inside HTTPS using an ephemeral public CA; the managed proxy below keeps HTTPS opaque.

For HTTPS CONNECT, the managed-mode proxy checks the requested host/port and a bounded TLS ClientHello's SNI before opening the upstream. Other SNI names, non-TLS tunnels, and encrypted ClientHello are rejected. HTTP authority mismatches and proxy credentials forwarded to upstream services are rejected/removed. The proxy does not follow redirects; any client-followed redirect must pass its own destination check. Concurrent connections and request/tunnel sizes are bounded.

This is a network-destination boundary. Opaque HTTPS does not reveal URL paths or encrypted HTTP Host/:authority; those are not inspected. Shared-CDN tenant routing remains subject to that service's policy. It is not a TLS interception proxy or an application-layer URL allowlist. Certificate-pinned or non-proxy-aware clients may be incompatible and fail closed.

Agents cannot delegate broader networking through spawning. A none parent can spawn only none; an allowlist parent can spawn none or a subset of its origins and explicit IP pins. A child cannot discard pins or substitute pins for an unpinned DNS origin. The owner retains its explicit administrative authority to select approved templates.

docs.title: Aggregate admission budgets
docs.text:
budget:
  max_tokens: 1000000
  max_cost_microusd: 10000000 # $10 of declared reservations, not a bill cap.
agents:
  lead:
    budget:
      enforcement: reservation
      max_turn_tokens: 20000
      max_turn_cost_microusd: 1000000
      max_subtree_tokens: 300000
      max_subtree_cost_microusd: 5000000

Token and cost values are separate owner-declared admission allowances. Cost uses integer millionths of a US dollar. Every agent/template under a session ceiling must declare the corresponding nonzero per-turn allowance. A spawned child also needs a declaration whenever any ancestor limits that dimension.

Claiming a task atomically charges its full per-turn allowance against the session and each configured ancestor/subtree ceiling. Explicit instructions and observation wakes use the same claim path. An idempotent claim replay does not charge twice; retrying uncertain work charges a fresh allowance. Charges survive restarts, failed tasks, cancellation, and missing/untrusted usage reports. There is no automatic budget renewal or usage-based refund. budget.status exposes the caller's own subtree, or the full session to the owner.

The owner can update effective session/agent admission budgets with versioned capacity.update; readiness and transactional claims use the same effective limits. Edits cannot lower a ceiling below permanently reserved usage. A live admission deadline can only shorten the existing deadline and does not kill an already-running native process. These overlays survive restart without changing the launch definition. capacity.get reports current capacity without reserving it. See live admission controls for replacement semantics and CAS versions.

These limits bound declared admissions, not provider billing or actual native-model token generation. Native CLIs can make multiple requests, and their usage reports do not provide an authoritative pre-spend enforcement point. Configuration requesting enforcement: hard is rejected. A provider account's own spending controls, or a separately enforceable credential-holding gateway, are necessary for a hard external bill ceiling. Do not treat a reported usage observation or max_tokens on one request as a total-turn bill cap. Reservations govern managed and native bridge task claims in either local or isolated mode; human-driven inference inside an interactive native CLI does not claim broker tasks and is outside these turn allowances.

docs.title: Capped workspaces and history
docs.text:
agents:
  coder:
    sandbox: bubblewrap
    # Omit workdir: the controller creates state/workspaces/coder.
    disk:
      workspace_bytes: 67108864
      history_bytes: 33554432
      temp_bytes: 16777216
      max_entries: 10000

Every size is required, between 1 MiB and 1 TiB. Entry limits are 1–100000. Disk capsules apply to managed turns; interactive sessions reject this setting. Disk capsules require a canonical, private, state-owned workspace at exactly state/workspaces/<agent>. External/shared workdirs are rejected. Use scoped messages and explicit owner-controlled artifact handoffs between workspaces.

Workspace, the entire private HOME, and /tmp are separate sized tmpfs mounts. The kernel returns ENOSPC when each filesystem is full. There are no writable host workspace/history binds in this mode. The trusted inner shim imports a read-only snapshot, runs the native harness, and exports only the workspace and selected native transcript directory through a private checkpoint socket. Other home files and temporary data are discarded. Read-only credential files remain narrow snapshots; auth refresh still belongs to the external owner credential source.

The host accepts only bounded regular-file/directory archives into fresh private staging. It rejects traversal, absolute paths, implicit directories, symlinks, hardlinks, devices, FIFOs, duplicate entries, PAX metadata, over-sized files, and excess entries. Source trees with links are also rejected. Export currently uses USTAR-compatible paths; files which cannot be represented fail the checkpoint. Entry count limits apply to imported/checkpointed storage; tmpfs runtime inode exhaustion remains a kernel/resource limit.

The history byte/entry allowance includes previous conversation generations, so resetting a conversation does not create a new quota. Existing generations consume the allowance available to the current checkpoint. A workspace/history digest check prevents silently publishing over observed host edits. Publication finishes before the adapter verifies the native transcript. A journal and old snapshots are retained if publication is interrupted; uncertain work is not automatically repeated.

Successful staging is removed. Failed, cancelled, malformed, or conflicted checkpoints keep one bounded quarantine under state/capsules/<agent> and block another capsule for that agent. Recovery is an authenticated owner operation which also works with the broker offline:

amx managed capsule inspect --state /private/run --agent coder
amx managed capsule recover --state /private/run --agent coder \
  --action restore --expect DIGEST_FROM_INSPECT

Stop the worker first. Inspection/recovery hold the worker's exclusive lock and the capsule controller lock, preventing recovery during active or concurrently starting execution. Inspection returns digests, state, and safe available actions. Recovery requires that exact current digest. publish selects an accepted, validated checkpoint; restore selects the known previous snapshots; discard is allowed only when existing host snapshots match their baselines. Interrupted publications retain fsynced before/after hashes and old snapshots. A partial publish with the only old snapshot in previous-* cannot be blindly discarded. Changed owner files, unexpected snapshots, links, or changed other history generations fail closed for manual inspection.

Filesystem recovery does not certify native task success. Resolve uncertain task leases and conversation state separately before resuming agents.

The enforced quantities are tmpfs filesystem sizes, checkpoint file-content bytes, and checkpoint entry counts. This is not a host filesystem project quota for all controller logs, database storage, metadata blocks, or unrelated owner files. A checkpoint can temporarily retain both old and new snapshots; plan for up to twice the selected workspace/history content plus bounded metadata. Native process-tree memory limits are separately configurable and should account for tmpfs usage. No privileged host mounts, quota configuration, or policy changes are performed automatically.

docs.title: Check the boundaries
docs.text:
The local adversarial tests cover origin/Host/redirect/pin/SNI checks, ECH and non-TLS rejection, live-tunnel revocation, claim deduplication and uncertainty, ancestor/session budgets, bounded archives, history generations, cancellation, snapshot conflicts, quarantine, active-worker recovery denial, stale recovery digests, and restore/publish after interrupted multi-volume publication.

Opt-in integration tests exercise real Bubblewrap namespaces without model calls:

make build
AGENTMUX_INTEGRATION_BINARY="$PWD/bin/amx" go test ./internal/egress ./internal/capsule \
  -run 'TestRealNamespaceProxyCannotBypassAllowlist|TestRealCapsuleENOSPCAndHistoryCheckpoint' -count=1

The endpoint test proves allowed traffic succeeds through the proxy while a denied endpoint receives no request and direct/proxy-opt-out attempts fail. The disk test fills all three actual tmpfs mounts to ENOSPC, verifies read-only seed enforcement, and checks workspace/native-history publication. An enclosing container may deny namespaces; such a failure is not silently downgraded.

TestRealManagedHardeningWorkerAndIsolatedBroker additionally combines an isolated broker, allowlisted worker, capped capsule and session reservation in one actual managed task and checks rejection of a second task before any further endpoint request. These tests use local deterministic processes and do not measure model quality or provider billing.

docs.title: Pane harness integration
docs.text:
This page describes the original v1 provider: pane launcher. Current start/add sessions use v2 harness: configuration and the work-session workflow. Their local interactive mode preserves normal native configuration and approvals. It does not apply the v1 launcher or headless safe-mode flags described below to every native terminal.

For v2, Claude/Codex/Pi can receive appended coordination context; --native-only appends none. Native Antigravity requires --native-only, while its Pi bridge supports coordinated isolated work. Codex custom endpoints use Responses; Pi compatible endpoints use Chat Completions. See managed setup and provider compatibility for configuration and checks.

For managed identities, native-auth snapshots, separate agent/broker sandboxes, and an opt-in real Claude/Codex/local-Pi workflow, see mixed harness sandbox acceptance.

The provider field in the existing pane configuration selects a local agent harness. Each pane runs its own process. Model endpoints and credentials remain configured in the harness; a harness name is not a model-provider connection.

Configuration value Executable Role delivery Agentmux coordination claude claude Appended system prompt Per-session native MCP when supported; CLI bridge fallback codex codex Initial prompt Per-session native MCP when supported; CLI bridge fallback antigravity or agy agy Interactive initial prompt CLI bridge pi pi Appended system prompt CLI bridge gemini or gemini-cli gemini Workspace context artifact in native mode Native MCP when supported; CLI bridge fallback gptme gptme Initial prompt CLI bridge

Existing Gemini configurations continue to select the Gemini executable. They are not redirected to Antigravity, whose flags and configuration differ.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
Agentmux combines the persona file and operational coordination instructions into one --append-system-prompt argument. This preserves Claude Code's default instructions. Native MCP uses a per-session --mcp-config with --strict-mcp-config so other MCP configuration is excluded. Agentmux does not bypass Claude's tool permissions.

The official CLI reference documents these flags. The ordinary pane launcher remains an interactive terminal process; streaming input or interruption through the Agent SDK is a separate integration surface.

Managed turns use --safe-mode, structured print output, and --permission-mode dontAsk. A coding role therefore needs an owner-approved native tool allowlist; role text alone does not grant tool permissions. For example, command: [claude, --allowedTools, 'Read,Write,Edit,Bash'] enables those tools while retaining the managed adapter's safety flags. Narrow the Bash patterns for the task where practical. A structured permission denial fails the managed task even when the CLI exits zero. See the Claude/Codex example for trusted local login reuse and workspace setup. Local mode does not isolate those tools from host files.

docs.title: Antigravity
docs.text:
Use provider: antigravity or its agy alias. The launcher passes --prompt-interactive, optional --model, and optional --effort. Persona text and CLI bridge instructions become the initial user prompt. The supported effort values are low, medium, high, xhigh, and max; the selected model and installed harness can impose further restrictions.

Agentmux uses the CLI bridge even if Antigravity advertises MCP support. Its MCP documentation describes global and workspace files rather than a per-session configuration flag. Writing those files for several agents sharing a workspace could mix their identities. The launcher creates no MCP configuration and changes no Antigravity settings.

Antigravity's headless protocol supports structured streaming turns, but that is separate from this interactive pane launcher. In headless mode, tool permissions can deny an action while the overall run still exits successfully; a controller must inspect structured outcomes and denials.

docs.title: Pi
docs.text:
Use provider: pi. Agentmux appends the persona and coordination instructions using --append-system-prompt. Set model to the configured model identifier, including a provider prefix when needed. reasoning_effort maps to --thinking and accepts off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, or max; Pi adjusts reasoning to the selected model's capabilities.

The launcher does not install extensions, modify MCP configuration, or approve project resources automatically. Pi's CLI reference and RPC interface describe the separate interactive and structured control surfaces. Installed versions can differ; CLI preflight checks the flags the launcher requires.

For npm-installed Pi inside a managed bubblewrap sandbox, use an explicit Node executable and the real package entrypoint: command: [/absolute/node, /absolute/pi-package/dist/bundle/cli.js]. Declare that Node binary and the complete Pi package directory in read_only_paths. A host symlink such as ~/.local/bin/pi, when mounted as a standalone file and invoked through another wrapper, loses its package-relative module paths. Its version check can pass while CLI help and actual turns fail. Managed setup discovers the explicit entrypoint; it does not mount a whole host home or change global installations.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text: A pane launcher provides convenient startup and context delivery. It does not authenticate agents to a coordination service, provide sandbox isolation, or turn terminal input into reliable structured commands. Those guarantees require managed identities, an enforced policy service, sandbox backends, and structured harness adapters. Native harness permissions still apply to CLI bridge calls.

docs.title: Live permissions and resource controls
docs.text: A workspace combines immutable launch configuration, explicit owner overrides, owner collaboration groups and consented teams. boundaries.get is the current authority snapshot. control.get is stored owner intent and group membership; a stored true is never proof that required membership or ancestry still holds. Use the selected agent's credential for its own boundaries.get; only the owner may inspect another agent or read/update complete owner controls. Roles describe responsibilities and titles label sessions; neither adds a permission source.

docs.title: Independent group contributions
docs.text:
An active owner collaboration group contributes directed note/ping grants among its current members, and instruction grants only when commands: true. Its own board/memory require current membership. Disabling the group removes only that contribution. Another overlapping active group keeps its grants. Explicit owner edge/scope overrides win, including denies; configuration and parent delegation remain underlying sources. Therefore notes-only means this group grants no commands, rather than revoking a command grant supplied elsewhere.

boundaries.get target entries include allowed actions, per-action sources and denied_reasons. Scope entries include effective read/write, source, reason and optional stored_read/stored_write. The optional stored fields identify an override, not actual current access. suspended labels isolation. The terminal Connections and Memory views display these differences directly; o opens the complete owner snapshot.

To remove one explicit override rather than replace it with another allow/deny:

{"version": 7, "kind": "edge", "from": "alice", "to": "bob", "action": "instruct", "reset": true}

Submit it to control.update with the current boundary version. Board/memory resets use kind, agent, namespace, reset: true. Reset can clean an exact historical entry even after membership ended or an agent was revoked; it cannot grant membership. Terminal M/P/I reset the selected directed message/ping/ instruction override; Memory R resets its selected scope override. Ordinary lowercase keys still set explicit permissions. Team namespaces always follow consent and ancestry, regardless of an old stored namespace override.

docs.title: Isolation and reconnecting
docs.text:
Isolation adds source: "isolation" suspension overlays without overwriting the prior explicit owner intent. It removes current owner-group memberships and consented memberships, dissolves teams owned by the isolated agent, and blocks ambient spawning/team creation. Native terminals keep running and private memory remains private. Existing accepted tasks and already-read data remain.

Reconnecting selected agents removes their directed pair's isolation overlays, restores configured static scope intent and rejoins their selected group. It keeps unrelated isolated relationships blocked. An explicit owner deny survives reconnect. A new exact owner grant can deliberately replace its isolation overlay without restoring ambient team/spawn authority. Rejoining a consented team still requires an invitation and fresh participant consent.

Older state files did not distinguish generated controls from explicit owner edits. These groups have no contributions_version (zero); new/reviewed groups have version 1. Editing an old group fails closed with conflict, before any membership or control changes, until the owner explicitly chooses one policy:

  • legacy_policy: "preserve": keep historical pair overrides as direct owner intent, including their allows and denies. Disabling this group can therefore leave those deliberately preserved direct grants effective.
  • legacy_policy: "group": remove only untagged historical allow: true edges between distinct members of this exact original group, then apply its requested state. All denies, other pairs, labeled isolation overlays and stored namespace controls remain. Other new active groups still contribute their own grants.

Neither choice guesses which old allows were manually intended. Review control.get and the exact pair first. The choice, requested membership/state, control revision, event and receipt commit atomically; rejection changes nothing. An unreviewed legacy group adds no new implicit pair grants; its historical controls remain the authority until review. A stale permission revision cannot apply a migration choice against changed owner intent. For the everyday CLI:

amx collaborate alice bob --legacy-policy preserve --session work
amx collaborate alice bob --legacy-policy group --session work

The terminal Connections c opens a migration review for an exact two-agent legacy group. 1 selects preserve, 2 group, o reads the historical pair edges, Enter submits that explicit choice with the frozen original members and policy version, and Esc cancels. No policy is preselected. Larger legacy groups use the CLI or the web's explicit review. Current groups never manufacture global edge or namespace overrides. After review, exact overrides remain individually resettable without granting membership.

docs.title: Capacity and live admission budgets
docs.text:
capacity.get {"agent":"alice"} is owner-only when inspecting somebody else; participants inspect themselves. It reports resource version, remaining lifetime spawns/teams, remaining spawn depth, current team slots, delegated templates, blocking reasons and effective agent budget. Owner capacity.get {} also reports the effective session budget. budget.status returns effective limits and permanently charged usage. Read-only snapshots do not reserve future capacity.

Owners can atomically edit admission budgets with capacity.update:

{"version": 1, "agent": "alice", "agent_budget": {"max_turn_tokens": 10000, "max_turn_cost_microusd": 200000, "max_subtree_tokens": 100000, "max_subtree_cost_microusd": 2000000, "enforcement": "reservation"}}

Use the resource_version returned by capacity/budget inspection, which is separate from permission revisions. A supplied budget replaces that complete budget object; omitted budget objects remain unchanged. session_budget accepts max_tokens and max_cost_microusd. Zero means an unset reservation/ceiling. Invalid negative limits, missing required turn reservations, stale versions and ceilings below permanently reserved usage fail without changing anything. New session ceilings validate every current agent and spawn template. No edit refunds a failed, cancelled or uncertain attempt, and launch configuration stays immutable. The same effective limits govern readiness and transactional claims. The terminal Sessions view uses B for a four-field, reviewed agent-budget editor.

capacity.update {"version":2,"admission_seconds":300} can shorten admission runtime from now. It cannot extend the existing process/run deadline or a previous admission deadline. An admission deadline stops future broker admissions; it does not assert that an already-running native process was terminated. Process-tree resource caps remain enforced launch settings and are not silently weakened.

These controls bound conservative broker admissions, not hard external provider billing. Direct interactive CLI inference remains governed by that native CLI. Saved resource overlays use recovery digests; missing or damaged persisted state fails closed rather than restoring larger defaults.

Role changes use a separate owner agent.role {id,role,version} operation and role_version, rather than the resource or permission revision. They apply at the next managed claim or through a native session's broker notice. In native Review/Auto mode, a role/boundary notice can become an attributed native turn; Manual mode leaves it for explicit inbox access. They never grant additional permissions. See native collaboration and managed runtime.

docs.title: Managed teams and durable coordination
docs.text:
Agentmux supports opt-in managed teams alongside native tmux workspaces. Managed mode gives each logical agent a separate credential, enforces message and memory permissions in a coordination service, and stores durable tasks in SQLite.

The existing load, render, pane launchers, and v1 workspace YAML remain available. Managed configuration uses version: 2 and mode: managed; use amx managed up for automatic startup, or managed init for manual service control. Do not pass it to amx load.

For a single coding request with fresh reviews, executable checks and a retained patch, use amx work. For owner-authored comparisons, missions and handoffs, use amx flow. Those journeys have separate plans, result storage and isolation settings; starting a managed team does not enable workflow isolation.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Authenticated operations over a private Unix socket; agent identity comes from its credential rather than a caller-supplied name.
  • Shared boards with exact read/write ACLs, direct messages, stored pings, and separately authorized instructions.
  • Durable instruction tasks, versioned state changes, instance-bound leases, uncertain-delivery recovery, and explicit owner verification.
  • Private per-agent memory and named shared memory, with version checks on updates.
  • Serialized headless turns through Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Pi, or an owner-configured command; optional private persistent conversations for Claude, Codex and Pi in Bubblewrap.
  • Optional bubblewrap worker and broker isolation that fails closed when unavailable, plus explicitly trusted local execution.
  • One-command tmux startup, preflight diagnostics, an owner workbench, ordered shutdown, and explicit restart.
  • Bounded spawning from owner-approved sandbox templates and consent-based dynamic teams with private team boards/memory.
  • Audience-checked reply threads, live owner role updates, independently removable collaboration groups, and versioned admission controls.
  • Bounded local event traces and portable bundles verified against an explicitly pinned owner signing key.

Agents can run as native interactive terminals (interaction: interactive) or serialized managed task workers (the default). Human input and native approvals stay in tmux; broker inbox messages never inject keystrokes. See work sessions.

Interactive native_only: true sessions require an empty role and omit Agentmux prompt injection. They retain broker coordination access, but tasks and role-change notices never become native terminal input. Managed-only conversation leases, automatic wakeups, traces, disk capsules and allowlist egress are rejected for interactive agents.

Persistent conversations and bounded wakeups support multi-turn workflows from one goal. Notes and pings are observations unless an explicitly authorized instruct creates a command task. Configured subscriptions can wake workers without injecting text into an interactive terminal. The finite pilot runner and repeated-round research environment support controlled comparisons separately from tmux supervision. Coordination history and native transcripts are useful evidence, but do not constitute a complete immutable trace of every model-visible input and tool execution.

docs.title: Try it without a model
docs.text:
Run make build from the repository root, or build directly with go build -o bin/amx ./cmd/agentmux. These examples use ./bin/amx. No provider credentials or model calls are needed for the /bin/cat demo.

Check setup, then start the complete team detached:

./bin/amx managed doctor examples/managed/command-demo.yaml
./bin/amx managed up examples/managed/command-demo.yaml --state .agentmux-state/demo

up returns a dedicated tmux attach command. Add --attach to open it immediately, or run managed status --state .agentmux-state/demo --watch for a live terminal summary. The broker, supervisor, status view, and each worker have separate named windows. Submit an instruction using the lead's credential:

./bin/amx managed call instruct \
  --credential-file .agentmux-state/demo/credentials/lead.json \
  --request-id demo-instruction-1 \
  --json '{"to":["worker"],"text":"Echo this task input so I can inspect the handoff."}'


./bin/amx managed call task.list \
  --credential-file .agentmux-state/demo/owner.json \
  --json '{}'

The command harness receives the worker's prepared input on stdin, and /bin/cat returns that text as its result. The task becomes submitted; a successful process exit does not independently verify its work. Copy the task's id and current version from task.list to verify it explicitly:

./bin/amx managed call task.verify \
  --credential-file .agentmux-state/demo/owner.json \
  --json '{"id":"TASK_ID","version":CURRENT_VERSION}'

./bin/amx managed status --state .agentmux-state/demo

Replace TASK_ID and CURRENT_VERSION with the returned values before running verification. Workers started by up consume queued tasks automatically. Their windows show managed worker processes executing headless turns; persistent mode resumes an explicit native conversation between tasks. Inspect published results through the broker API.

Stop the run without deleting its tasks or memory:

./bin/amx managed down --state .agentmux-state/demo
# Explicitly start another runtime attempt using saved configuration:
./bin/amx managed restart --state .agentmux-state/demo

The example permits lead to instruct worker and lets the worker send notes or pings back. A worker attempting to instruct the lead receives forbidden, even if its role text describes it as a coordinator.

docs.title: CLI contract
docs.text:
amx managed up <config> [--state <directory>] [--broker-sandbox local|bubblewrap] [--attach]
amx managed down --state <directory>
amx managed restart --state <directory> [--broker-sandbox local|bubblewrap] [--attach]
amx managed doctor <config> [--state <directory>] [--broker-sandbox local|bubblewrap]
amx managed init <config> --state <directory>
amx managed serve --state <directory> [--sandbox local|bubblewrap]
amx managed call <operation> [--credential-file <file>] [--socket <path>]
    [--json <object> | --stdin] [--request-id <id>]
amx managed worker --state <directory> --agent <id> [--once]
amx managed status --state <directory> [--watch]
amx managed activity --state <directory> [--watch]
amx managed rotate --state <directory> --agent <id|'$owner'>

Flags can appear before or after positional arguments. call uses {} when no arguments are supplied. --stdin reads one JSON object with a bounded size. AGENTMUX_CREDENTIAL_FILE can supply the credential path, and AGENTMUX_SOCKET can override its socket path. An explicit flag takes precedence.

Command results and failures use a JSON envelope with schema_version, kind, operation, ok, and either result or error. API calls also report request_id. Installation tokens and credential contents are never printed. The service startup notice goes to stderr; serve stays active until interrupted. status --watch and up --attach deliberately use interactive terminal output.

The CLI generates a random request ID when one is omitted. Within the same authenticated credential instance, retrying a write with the same ID and arguments retrieves its durable result. The cache is scoped to both logical actor and credential instance, so rotation cannot replay an old instance's lease receipt. Reusing an ID for different arguments fails with conflict. A transport failure can mean that a write committed but its response was lost: retain the reported request ID and retry that exact call, rather than submitting a new instruction.

docs.title: Lifecycle, diagnostics, and tmux ownership
docs.text:
up runs preflight before creating managed state or starting processes. It checks configured binaries and supported flags, named credential variables, dependencies, local endpoint metadata, and requested sandbox support without generating model output. Cloud authentication or dependencies that cannot be verified are reported as warnings rather than represented as tested. doctor exposes the same report without starting a run.

When --state is omitted, up uses .agentmux-state/SESSION under the current directory. Choose a short explicit path if the Unix socket path would exceed 100 bytes. An existing state directory must contain identical saved configuration; use a different directory for a changed experiment or team definition.

Each run uses its own private STATE/tmux.sock, with an attempt ID on the session and tracked panes. It does not connect to the user's default tmux server. A supervisor watches the authenticated agent registry and adds windows for newly spawned agents. Worker or broker crashes are observed rather than automatically restarted. The owner workbench shows the roster, native terminal previews, coordination content, tasks, shared memory, and live permission controls. It is a content-sensitive owner surface; agents must not receive its credential. For a metadata summary, use amx observe --watch --state STATE; v0.14.0 adds fixed collection diagnostics and offline capture reports. managed status --watch retains the lower-level lifecycle view.

Use managed activity --state DIRECTORY for a content-sensitive owner JSON snapshot of recent messages, task results/failures, events, and reported usage. Add --watch for a bounded terminal view; model and message text is quoted to escape terminal controls and Unicode direction controls. This view always uses the state's owner credential, includes private coordination content, and is not an agent-facing API. The default workbench also uses the owner credential and displays coordination content. See interactive work sessions for its shortcuts and native terminal workflow.

Use amx tasks --state DIRECTORY for filtered, paginated retained task history, and amx task TASK_ID --state DIRECTORY for one exact record. Add --open to open that task directly in the workbench, including an older task or retired recipient. Opening changes no task state; recovery still needs an explicit review of the exact task/version. These shortcuts have been available since v0.13.0; managed call remains available.

down interrupts owned worker processes first, waits for their terminal processes to exit, and then stops the broker and supervisor. It removes only the attempt's tracked session. A stale stop request cannot stop a new attempt. Durable tasks and memory remain on disk. restart performs an explicit ordered stop/start; it does not silently retry uncertain deliveries or reset the persisted runtime budget. After a run's budget expires, start a new state directory for a new run.

If termination or ownership cannot be confirmed, shutdown fails. Inspect current status before assuming the broker or native terminals are available or stopped. The CLI retains its JSON fault and prints shell-quoted recovery commands for the exact state directory to stderr:

amx managed status --state DIRECTORY
amx attach --state DIRECTORY
# Finish or exit each affected owned native CLI normally, then:
amx managed down --state DIRECTORY

Detaching or closing the workbench does not exit a native CLI. Retry a failed restart only after shutdown succeeds.

For one exited workspace-owned interactive session, use amx relaunch AGENT_ID --state DIRECTORY. Healthy peers keep running and the stable agent identity is retained. The default starts a fresh native conversation; --resume last, --resume picker, or an explicit native ID selects history through the supported harness. A live or revoked session cannot be relaunched, and no deadline is renewed. Older running controllers require one deliberate workspace restart before individual relaunch is available. See recovery for the distinction from retrying a broker task.

The lower-level commands remain useful without automatic tmux management:

./bin/amx managed init examples/managed/command-demo.yaml --state .agentmux-state/manual
# One shell:
./bin/amx managed serve --state .agentmux-state/manual
# Another shell:
./bin/amx managed worker --state .agentmux-state/manual --agent worker

For a manual worker, --once handles one queued task or exits if none is waiting. Do not launch a second manual worker for an agent already supervised by up; its exclusive lock rejects duplicates.

docs.title: Boards, messages, instructions, and memory
docs.text:
Operation Typical arguments Authority identity {} Any authenticated actor board.post board, text Board writers message.list Optional board, after, limit Only messages visible to the caller message.send to array, text message.send grant for every recipient ping.send to array, text ping.send grant for every recipient instruct One recipient in to, text Separate instruct grant; creates a task task.list / task.get Optional state / task id Sender, recipient, or owner observation.get Optional limit (1–200) Owner only; body-free retained counts, attention and live lease metadata task.observe Exact task id, lease, cumulative event_count, fixed event_kind Current recipient worker only; exact instance/generation/lease, ephemeral check-in task.cancel Task id, current version Sender or owner task.verify Task id, current version Owner, after submission agent.role Agent id, role, current role version Owner only capacity.get / budget.status Optional agent Own capacity/usage, or owner inspection capacity.update Current resource version, budget/deadline fields Owner only memory.get namespace, key Namespace readers memory.list namespace Namespace readers memory.put namespace, key, value, version Namespace writers events / status {} or optional event limit Owner only

For example, publish a board note and create private memory:

export AGENTMUX_CREDENTIAL_FILE="$PWD/.agentmux-state/demo/credentials/lead.json"

./bin/amx managed call board.post \
  --json '{"board":"team","text":"Please post evidence with each result."}'

./bin/amx managed call memory.put \
  --json '{"namespace":"private","key":"next_step","value":"Review the worker result","version":0}'

./bin/amx managed call memory.put \
  --json '{"namespace":"project","key":"decision","value":"Require owner verification","version":0}'

private always means the authenticated agent's private namespace. Named shared namespaces use their configured ACLs. Version 0 creates an entry; subsequent updates require its current version. Memory values are strings; applications can store structured JSON as a string if needed. The broker owner remains trusted with access to the state directory, even though ordinary API access to private memory uses an agent credential.

Roles describe responsibilities. They grant no authority. Policy defaults to deny; explicit grants control messaging and instruction relationships, while board and memory ACLs are configured separately. A literal "*" covers configured agents only. It does not create identities or authorize future operation types.

agent.role updates a role with its own role_version compare-and-swap check. Roles accept up to 16384 UTF-8 bytes without Unicode control characters except newlines/tabs; an empty role clears it. Managed workers capture the current role at the next task claim; in-flight input stays unchanged. Native sessions receive an inbox notice and can read the current role through identity; no keystrokes are injected. A nonempty role is rejected for native_only sessions.

board.post, message.send, ping.send and instruct accept optional reply_to for a visible message or instruction task. The broker derives thread_id; callers cannot choose a root. A board reply retains the original board, while each direct recipient must already be able to read the referenced message. A reply adds no authority or ancestor access. task.list supports state, to, query, order, after and limit, with a returned has_more flag; use task.get for an exact task. Native provider-only chat turns are outside this broker history.

Since v0.13.0, workers publish metadata-only check-ins while a task is leased. task.observe does not change task state/version, renew a lease, consume a durable request receipt or prove model activity. Worker check-in and native event times are set separately by the broker. Owner task reads may include this ephemeral progress; a broker restart makes it unknown. See the observability guide for effective uncertainty, native readiness, capacity and safe evidence inspection.

Owner collaboration groups, explicit overrides and consented teams remain separate permission sources. See live permissions for overlapping groups, isolation overlays, explicit legacy-state review, reset semantics and live admission edits. Memory lifecycle covers retention, retrieval and archive provenance.

docs.title: Bounded spawning and dynamic teams
docs.text:
The bounded team example enables these features explicitly. It uses command harnesses, so inspecting the API makes no model calls. The command fixtures echo their instructions; they do not decide to spawn or cooperate by themselves.

./bin/amx managed up examples/managed/bounded-teams.yaml --state .agentmux-state/teams
./bin/amx managed call agent.spawn \
  --credential-file .agentmux-state/teams/credentials/lead.json \
  --json '{"template":"helper","capabilities":{"boards_read":["team"],"memory_read":["findings"],"join_teams":true}}'

The response contains a new agent ID, not its credential. The supervisor creates its worker window. Its immutable template chooses the harness, argv, network, and dependency mounts; the child receives a new private workspace and a separate bubblewrap sandbox. An agent cannot provide an arbitrary executable, mount, credential, or working directory in a spawn request. Native model templates need explicit provider networking and credentials; the example helper uses network: none.

Children receive only the requested capabilities that the parent may delegate. Static wildcard ACLs are not inherited. The parent gets a control edge to the child; the child gets a note/ping reply edge and cannot thereby command its parent. Delegable scopes include board/memory reads and writes, target-specific messaging/instruction edges, approved further spawn templates, and team creation. A child needs explicit join_teams: true to accept invitations, and its parent must currently belong to that team. Lifetime spawn count, depth, concurrent tasks, and the persisted run deadline bound expansion. Creating a new child does not renew the run's time budget.

Use agent.list with the owner credential to inspect registry metadata. agent.stop with {"id":"AGENT_ID"} revokes an agent and its descendants' credentials; the supervisor then interrupts their workers. Revocation itself returns process_stopped: false because authorization withdrawal is distinct from process termination. Exited workers are not automatically restarted.

Revocation fences tasks addressed to the revoked agents. Previously accepted instructions they issued to other active agents remain durable; cancel those tasks explicitly with task.cancel when withdrawing the work itself.

Team creation is separately enabled and restricted to configured creators or explicitly delegated child capabilities:

./bin/amx managed call team.create \
  --credential-file .agentmux-state/teams/credentials/lead.json \
  --json '{"name":"Review group"}'

Use the returned team ID and version for team.invite (id, agent, version). The invitee must accept through its own credential using team.join (id, version); membership is not silently forced. team.list supplies current versions. Members receive the team's dedicated board and shared-memory namespace named in its response. Team membership does not grant instruction authority or access to unrelated namespaces. Board history defaults to messages written since joining; teams.history: all explicitly enables earlier history. Shared memory contains current values rather than a history of messages. Leaving removes future access but cannot erase information already read. team.remove, team.leave, and owner/creator team.dissolve update versioned membership. Lifetime team and member counts are bounded. See the dynamic-team guide for complete commands and consent rules.

Managers can change team name/description and propose ownership transfer. Only the proposed owner can accept, under current delegated authority. team.move is a non-owner member's own consent to join a pending destination invitation and leave the source atomically; it requires both current team versions. team.list gives participants their own self_access explanation when ancestry or other current requirements block access.

docs.title: Model harnesses and local endpoints
docs.text:
Harness Managed transport Endpoint support Claude Code Streaming JSON print mode Existing login, or an Anthropic-compatible base URL and credential environment variable Codex exec --json Existing Codex authentication, or an explicitly configured custom Responses endpoint and selected API-key environment Antigravity Streaming JSON input/output Existing local agy authentication; arbitrary endpoint overrides are rejected Pi JSONL RPC Existing Pi configuration, or a private OpenAI-compatible chat-completions connection Command Literal owner-configured argv; prompt on stdin Defined by the command

The local setup was checked with Claude Code 2.1.316 and Pi 1.4.0 from the maintained npm package @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent. Installation does not imply login or account access. The deprecated @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent package is not the current package. Harness versions and supported flags should be checked when upgrading.

The examples include:

  • Mixed Claude/Codex/Antigravity/Pi team.
  • Claude coder and Codex reviewer, with an explicit Claude tool allowlist and Git workspace setup.
  • Pi with local Ollama, using exactly http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1.
  • Pi with vLLM, using exactly http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1.

Replace each model placeholder with a model already served by that endpoint. For an unauthenticated vLLM server, remove the example's api_key_env line. For an authenticated server, export the named variable in the worker's environment. Keep actual credentials out of YAML, argv, role text, and task messages.

Codex custom connections select protocol: openai-responses and the owner's explicit base_url. The adapter supplies a per-process native model-provider definition with wire_api: responses, disables implicit OpenAI login for that provider, and uses only the selected API-key environment when configured. It does not edit the owner's Codex files. This follows the official custom-provider configuration. Chat Completions endpoints, including many Ollama/vLLM deployments, use Pi's openai-compatible/ollama connection instead. A successful metadata probe or protocol fixture is distinct from a successful real model turn.

Claude managed turns retain --safe-mode and --permission-mode dontAsk. Configure an explicit owner-approved --allowedTools prefix for coding tools, as shown in the Claude/Codex example; a role description does not grant native permissions. Tool denials fail the task rather than count as successful submission. Codex exec requires its working directory to be a Git repository with the current adapter. Default managed workspaces start empty, so initialize the example's state and run git init in its workspaces before managed up. Startup queues no tasks and makes no model-generation call; submit a bounded instruction explicitly when ready.

The adapter uses the configured API base exactly; it does not append /v1 or switch to Ollama's /api/generate. See the official Ollama compatibility documentation and vLLM server documentation. Pi receives a private temporary models.json, rather than changes to the user's configuration. Setup and doctor perform bounded metadata discovery for explicitly configured local/private endpoints, including exact model records and Ollama /api/show metadata. Explicit model_metadata fields override discovery; setup saves the selection, while doctor leaves hand-authored YAML unchanged. Missing fields use conservative defaults, not a claim about the engine's actual capacity. See compatible endpoint metadata for context/output limits, capability declarations and validation scope.

docs.title: Isolation and state ownership
docs.text:
sandbox: local runs trusted processes as the current OS user. Separate workdirs and API credentials provide organization, but do not stop such a process reading host files or another agent's credentials. Use this mode for development and trusted workflows. API ACLs are meaningful only while the caller cannot bypass the API through host access.

sandbox: bubblewrap requests kernel-enforced worker isolation. It must not fall back to local execution when the executable, user namespaces, mounts, or network policy are unavailable. network: none isolates networking; network: host deliberately allows unrestricted host networking. network: allowlist supports exact approved HTTP/HTTPS origins through a private proxy and namespace-local relay, including explicitly approved local inference endpoints. Clients must support the supplied proxy settings; incompatible clients fail to connect without a host-network fallback. See exact network destinations for configuration, DNS/IP rules and protocol limits. Validate the complete isolation setup on each deployment machine before relying on it.

The broker is a separate process with a private state directory. Use amx managed serve --state DIRECTORY --sandbox bubblewrap to isolate the broker with a minimal environment, no network namespace access, its private state mounted for persistence, and the Agentmux binary mounted read-only. It fails when the requested kernel isolation is unavailable. Without that flag, the broker runs as a normal trusted host process. Do not expose its complete state directory, owner credential, host tmux socket, container-management socket, or peer home directories to an isolated agent. A Node-based harness may need an explicit Node executable/CLI path in command and narrowly selected package dependencies in read_only_paths; do not mount the whole host home merely to make a wrapper work.

Initialization creates private default workdirs beneath the state directory for agents without workdir. Explicit relative workdirs and read_only_paths resolve against the configuration file's directory. The state contains SQLite data and credential files; treat it as sensitive and keep it outside version control. .agentmux-state/ is ignored by this repository. Restart the service with the same directory to retain tasks and memory; initialization refuses to replace existing nonempty state.

docs.title: Selected native login files
docs.text:
Native subscription logins can be explicitly provisioned to Bubblewrap workers:

agents:
  coder:
    harness: claude
    command: [claude, --allowedTools, 'Read,Write,Edit,Bash']
    sandbox: bubblewrap
    network: host
    auth:
      file: ~/.claude/.credentials.json
    resources:
      memory_bytes: 2147483648
      cpu_percent: 100
      processes: 256
      open_files: 1024
