auth.file is an explicit owner choice, not automatic home-directory discovery. Claude selects only its OAuth credential object. Codex selects only the authentication fields from ~/.codex/auth.json. Pi additionally requires auth.provider and selects that one provider from a Pi-native auth.json; command-backed keys and credential environment overrides are excluded. Other native settings, histories, hooks, plugins, and provider entries are not copied. Pi subscription credentials are not translated from another harness's format.

The original must be a owned private regular file (0600 or 0400) without hardlinks or symlink components. Originals must stay outside every configured agent workspace, declared dependency mount, and default shared runtime mount. Relative paths resolve against the team YAML; ~/ expands in CLI configuration loading. Native auth cannot be combined with a connection credential or environment overrides that change its location or login method.

Each worker creates a filtered private temporary snapshot and mounts it read-only at its harness's fixed location inside the private home. The model can read its own credential; this feature separates workers and does not hide credentials from their owning model. Host settings and original credential files are not mounted. Snapshot values never enter normalized configuration or status. Exact known values are also redacted from worker-published results and usage on a best-effort basis.

Managed workers reload and replace their filtered snapshot between turns, before claiming new work. Refresh or sign in through the selected owner-side source; a healthy worker sees its next valid contents without a restart. Interactive sessions retain their prepared snapshot for that native process, so relaunch them after a source change when needed. Read-only snapshots cannot write a token refresh back to the source. Normal and handled-error cleanup removes snapshots; a hard kill or host crash can leave a private temporary directory for owner cleanup. An unavailable source prevents new managed claims rather than falling back to host access. managed doctor checks native readiness inside the actual filesystem boundary when initialized state and its broker socket are available, with provider networking disabled.

docs.title: Enforced worker resources
docs.text:
All resource fields are optional and require sandbox: bubblewrap. memory_bytes, cpu_percent, and processes use a transient systemd user cgroup for the entire turn's process tree. A CPU value of 100 allows one CPU's time; process counts include threads. Memory limits also disable swap for the group and group OOM termination prevents partial survivors. These controls require Linux cgroup v2, delegated controllers, and a recent reachable systemd user manager (including scope OOM policy and literal environment handling).

open_files, cpu_seconds, and address_space_bytes use inherited per-process prlimit bounds. CPU seconds are not an aggregate tree budget. Address-space limits default to unset because Go and Node/V8 reserve large virtual ranges. Values are validated, actual cgroup controls are checked before the sandbox starts, and unavailable enforcement fails without an unlimited fallback. The host user bus and cgroup filesystem are not mounted into the agent.

These are per-turn execution limits. They do not bound an external inference server, provider token charges, or a parent's aggregate spending across children. Provider networking with network: host remains unrestricted. Use network: allowlist with explicit egress.allow origins for the supported destination boundary; encrypted URL paths are outside that boundary. See hardening for network and aggregate admission controls.

Reproduce the real kernel resource tests with make test-resources on a supported host. They include aggregate multi-process memory exhaustion and termination of a descendant that creates a separate session.

docs.title: Codex inside an outer sandbox
docs.text:
Codex defaults to its native workspace-write command sandbox. Some hosts block nested user namespaces, even though Agentmux's outer Bubblewrap sandbox works. An owner may explicitly select codex_sandbox: external for a Codex agent already configured with sandbox: bubblewrap. The managed worker enforces that outer boundary and requires it to start successfully before execution. Local execution and other harnesses reject this setting; native failures never select it automatically.

In this mode the adapter passes Codex --sandbox danger-full-access: the accessible filesystem is the isolated Bubblewrap filesystem, including its own writable workspace and private home, while host state and peer credentials remain absent. It does not pass the approval-bypass flag or change host policy. This is an explicit execution choice for an externally isolated runner, as described in the official CLI reference. The lower-level harness library remains a trusted process API; an arbitrary caller-supplied wrapper function alone is not proof of isolation.

docs.title: Recovery, cancellation, and bounds
docs.text:
Task acceptance, dispatch, process completion, and verification are separate facts. Workers serialize turns per logical agent. Completion requires a valid instance-bound lease and the expected task version; credential rotation fences old instances. Rotate an agent credential with its ID, or quote the reserved owner identity:

./bin/amx managed rotate --state .agentmux-state/demo --agent worker
./bin/amx managed rotate --state .agentmux-state/demo --agent '$owner'

The worker should be stopped and restarted after rotation. The owner path is separate from the agent namespace, so an agent named owner remains a normal agent.

On broker restart, a turn that may already have reached a harness becomes uncertain; it is not silently resent. The owner can inspect the task and use task.resolve with its current version and resolution: "retry" or "fail". Before retrying uncertain work, stop any old worker/harness process and assess partial side effects. Cancellation similarly distinguishes a request to stop from confirmation that the process tree stopped; cancelled work must not become automatically retryable after a restart.

Configured limits bound message sizes, stored work, runtime, and durable storage/request counts. The defaults include 30000 durable records and 50000 cached requests. Capacity is reserved for active task completion, cancellation, stopped-process acknowledgements, agent revocation, and team membership cleanup, so ordinary writes cannot consume the slots needed to finish those transitions. They are not guaranteed provider-spend caps. Harness token and cost reports are observations with provider-specific coverage. API list/response limits can require narrower pages. When storage limits are reached, the owner should export/archive state or start a new session; the runtime does not silently delete the request records required for reliable retries.

docs.title: Verify a deployment
docs.text:
Start with model-free checks on a Linux host with working Bubblewrap and a built binary. These exercise actual broker/worker namespaces and coordination:

python3 scripts/smoke-managed.py --binary bin/amx
python3 scripts/smoke-managed-team.py --binary bin/amx

The handoff scenario checks board/memory exchange, instruction hierarchy, credential separation and independent task verification. The dynamic-team scenario adds a spawned worker, invitation consent, stale-version conflicts, since-join history, nonmember denials, removal/leave/dissolution, lifetime spawn limits and restart behavior.

Automated regressions use fake harness processes and local transports for protocol failures, permission denials, handoffs and recovery. Installed-Pi opt-ins can check RPC framing and sandbox writes against a fake local endpoint; these do not establish compatibility with a real model service.

To exercise real provider turns, follow the mixed-harness scenario or bounded autonomous workflow. They require explicit model opt-in and selected native authentication. Review each scenario's networking, tool permissions and resource requirements before starting. An inference service outside worker resource groups remains a separately trusted component.

See provider compatibility for supported routes, hardening for destination/resource controls and traces and recovery for audit limits. A successful scenario verifies its configured task and boundaries; it does not establish model quality, a provider spending cap or comprehensive sandbox security.

The opt-in real tmux lifecycle test also covers startup, a durable command task, ordered shutdown, idempotent shutdown, and another attempt preserving submitted work:

AGENTMUX_MANAGED_INTEGRATION=1 go test -race ./internal/managedlaunch

Run make build first, or set AGENTMUX_TEST_BINARY to an absolute built executable path. Add AGENTMUX_SANDBOX_INTEGRATION=1 to include the real spawned Bubblewrap worker test; it requires a host with usable user namespaces.

docs.title: Managed setup
docs.text:
amx managed setup --output team.yaml asks for each agent's role, harness, model, isolation and authentication choice. It discovers installed executables and code dependencies, runs bounded preflight checks, creates dedicated private workspaces, and writes a new mode-0600 validated YAML file. It refuses to overwrite an existing configuration. Setup never starts a model, logs in, prints credentials, or changes provider/global settings.

For reproducible setup, supply a JSON specification:

amx managed setup --spec examples/managed/setup-local-pi.json --output team.yaml
amx managed doctor team.yaml
amx managed up team.yaml --broker-sandbox bubblewrap

Edit the model ID and endpoint to match a running server first. A failed preflight creates no configuration or workspaces. The report keeps unchecked provider authentication and unsupported endpoint metadata visible as warnings. Namespace/resource requirements still fail closed when the selected backend is unavailable. The generated next commands retain the broker isolation choice, which belongs to the launcher rather than the agent YAML.

The specification has session, workspace_root, sandbox, broker_sandbox, shared_board, init_git, and an agents array. Agent fields include id, role, harness, model, optional binary, interaction, native_only, workdir, conversation, coding_tools, network, egress, codex_sandbox, and explicit authentication/endpoint fields. Relative workspace and executable selections resolve from the invocation directory. Native auth paths must reference private files; their contents are never embedded in YAML. Do not put literal credentials into role text or paths.

Authentication choices are explicit:

Choice Meaning file Select auth_file for a supported Bubblewrap worker. Pi also needs exact auth_provider. Only the selected filtered credentials reach its fresh home. api-env Select api_key_env, a variable name. Add base_url for a custom Pi/Claude endpoint or Codex Responses endpoint. Its value remains outside argv/YAML. native-local Explicitly reuse the native host login in trusted local mode. This does not isolate files, tools, or peer credentials. none No selected auth; useful for a private unauthenticated compatible endpoint. Native local harnesses require native-local because they may discover host login.

coding_tools: true gives Claude the explicit native Read,Write,Edit,Bash allowlist. It is broader than a task-specific Bash pattern; review the YAML before granting coding access. Bubblewrap Codex defaults to its native workspace sandbox. An explicit codex_sandbox: external relies on the required outer boundary when nested native user namespaces are unavailable. Setup never changes a host policy or silently falls back to this mode.

Choose interaction: interactive for a human-controlled native terminal, or omit it for a managed task worker. Interactive native_only: true requires an empty role and omits Agentmux prompt injection. Native approvals, customizations and history remain in the selected CLI; broker messages never become terminal keystrokes. Managed persistent conversations, wakeups, traces, disk capsules and allowlist egress are unavailable in interactive mode.

Preset setup is also available:

amx managed setup --preset coding --session work --project /path/to/project --output coding.yaml
amx managed setup --preset reviewer-pair --session review --output review.yaml
amx managed setup --preset research-team --session study --output study.yaml

coding creates native Claude/Codex terminals with peer/shared access disabled until the owner enables collaboration. reviewer-pair and research-team create idle managed workers with preset responsibilities; setup queues no task. Presets default to explicitly trusted local execution; --sandbox bubblewrap selects isolated agent and broker setup and requires its selected private auth files. Review the resulting paths, roles and permissions before starting.

For npm Pi, discovery writes a canonical Node executable plus real JavaScript entrypoint and explicit package/optional native dependency paths. For known Codex standalone packages it includes the code-mode host, packaged Bubblewrap, ripgrep, and public manifest. It never mounts an entire provider home. Native Claude is self-contained. See the official Codex CLI installation guide for supported installation methods; setup consumes the installed CLI.

init_git: true or --init-git initializes Git only in newly created agent workspaces, with global/system configuration and hooks excluded for that operation. Existing workspaces and repositories are preserved. Setup makes no commits and does not set a Git identity. To use an existing project, review workdir and dependency paths deliberately; avoid mounting coordination state or a whole home. In a multi-agent coding team, use separate checkouts/worktrees and an explicit integration process for changes.

Spec-based ACLs default to deny. With shared_board: true, the team board and project memory are shared read/write among the selected agents. Private memory remains scoped per agent. Setup does not grant cross-agent instructions, spawn rights, or autonomy implicitly; add reviewed hierarchy, wakeup and template settings using the managed runtime and dynamic team guide. The coding preset instead leaves those scopes ungranted until owner collaboration is enabled. Live role edits and live permissions/admission controls are separate versioned overlays; they do not rewrite the saved launch definition.

docs.title: Compatible endpoint metadata
docs.text:
Pi endpoints use the exact supplied API base, commonly /v1. Discovery sends metadata requests only to configured loopback/private destinations, pins DNS, ignores proxy settings, bounds response size/time, and never follows redirects. Generic/vLLM discovery reads exact model records from GET /models; vLLM's max_model_len field describes context length. protocol: ollama also tries the metadata-only POST /api/show at the corresponding server root and reads declared model context, runtime num_ctx/num_predict, and explicit capability metadata. It never calls generation endpoints during setup/preflight.

Discovery does not infer capabilities from model names. Missing fields retain 8192 context tokens, 2048 output tokens (reduced for smaller declared contexts), text input, and no declared reasoning support. Tool compatibility remains unverified when absent. The owner can override advertised metadata:

connections:
  local:
    protocol: openai-compatible
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
    model_metadata:
      context_window: 32768
      max_output: 4096
      input: [text]
      reasoning: false
      tools: true

The setup JSON accepts the same model_metadata object on each agent. Explicit fields, including false, override discovery. tools: false disables Pi tools; true describes expected transport support and grants no Agentmux permissions. These declarations map to Pi's supported model configuration, not guarantees that every advertised endpoint accepts each tool or modality. Doctor reports metadata without rewriting hand-authored YAML. Setup persists its discovered/overridden selection so ordinary turns do not renegotiate it. For handwritten YAML, doctor's discovery is advisory; runtime uses the configured metadata or its defaults. The 8,192-token fallback is not a claim about an unknown engine's real capacity: configure and verify that engine explicitly. Pi 1.4.0 reserves 4,096 context tokens before selecting output capacity. Doctor rejects a reported context of 4,096 or less; it never silently enlarges a known engine limit. Use a verified larger engine context or a compatible runtime.

docs.title: Provider coverage limits
docs.text:
Managed Claude, Codex and Pi support private persistent conversations through explicit native session references. Interactive sessions use provider-native history selection instead.

Direct managed Antigravity supports fresh trusted-local turns. Its authentication documentation uses the OS secure keyring/DBus for native login, while its conversation guide describes workspace scoping without an independent private storage-root contract that Agentmux can enforce. Setup rejects isolated native authentication and persistent conversation settings for that route. Direct interactive Antigravity requires native_only: true and an empty role because its native role-injection interface is unsupported.

For isolated persistent agents using Antigravity inference, choose harness: antigravity-bridge in setup and follow the authenticated local bridge guide. Pi provides isolated tools/history while native authentication remains in a separate owner-controlled host inference service.

Pi can connect to compatible Ollama/vLLM chat-completions endpoints. Configure the exact model ID, available context and expected tool support before running. Metadata and fake-endpoint tests verify configuration and protocol handling; only a real bounded provider task can check the chosen service/model. Setup never downloads model weights. See provider compatibility for the distinct startup, continuation and tool checks.

The real Ollama test is opt-in and expects an existing service/model:

AGENTMUX_OLLAMA_LIVE=1 AGENTMUX_OLLAMA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:14534/v1 \
AGENTMUX_OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen2.5:14b \
go test -race -v ./internal/harness -run TestPiRealOllamaPrivatePersistentTwoTurns

docs.title: Memory lifecycle and retrieval
docs.text:
Private memory belongs to one authenticated agent. Named shared memory retains exact namespace read/write ACLs; no retrieval or transfer operation adds access. Task/native conversation history and this explicit memory store are separate.

memory_policy:
  default_ttl_seconds: 86400
  max_ttl_seconds: 604800
  max_total_bytes: 67108864

Omit the default TTL for non-expiring memory. memory.put accepts namespace, key, value, the current CAS version, optional ttl_seconds, tags, and sources. Source references can identify a message/task the writer can see or an explicit external HTTP(S) URI plus optional SHA256. The broker never fetches external URIs and does not certify the truth of agent-authored claims. Created and updated times, author, content digest and previous digest record provenance.

Expired entries disappear from reads and retrieval immediately. memory.head returns their current version/state without returning expired content. Updates require that version; memory.delete and owner memory.prune retain versioned tombstones, preventing stale writers from recreating an earlier CAS version. Deletion/pruning clears stored payloads and historical idempotency-response payloads. This is logical retention, not physical secure erasure of SQLite pages/WAL, backups, exported archives, native histories or provider systems. The allocation ceiling bounds current serialized memory records, not the whole SQLite file or every copy of content elsewhere.

Use the agent's own credential for private memory. The owner's private namespace is separate; owner credentials do not impersonate an agent. The export/import/search/index/prune commands below use the live broker. Selecting --state STATE --agent coder loads that agent's credential from the owner-controlled state directory; it does not change its API permissions.

amx managed memory export --state STATE --agent coder \
  --namespace private --output /private/coder-memory.json
amx managed memory import --state NEW_STATE --agent coder \
  --namespace private --input /private/coder-memory.json
amx managed memory search --state NEW_STATE --agent coder \
  --namespace private --query 'parser architecture'
amx managed memory prune --state STATE

Exports are exclusive mode-0600 files, bounded to 64 MiB/10000 entries. Imports validate the archive and perform per-key CAS writes into an explicitly selected authorized namespace. Existing keys require --replace; conflict resolution is never implicit. Imports preserve remaining TTL, skip expired values, record an import source, and can resume safely after partial completion. They retain the destination writer's identity rather than impersonating the source author. Each imported entry carries structured sources claims: source_session, source_agent (the exporter), source_namespace, source_author (the original entry's writer), source_key, source_version, the complete archive_sha256 and the imported value's sha256. These remain available on the destination entry without the original archive. They are asserted source metadata, not an authenticated source identity or a grant of source-namespace access. Re-exporting the entry retains its source claims inside the archive; a subsequent import records that immediate archive's identities. Existing v1 import sources without the newer identity fields remain readable. An entry imported by an older version can be enriched by reimporting its original archive with --replace; enrichment still uses the destination's current CAS version rather than silently changing an existing entry. An archive checksum detects accidental content changes; it is not a signature establishing a trusted source. Protect archive files as private data.

Lexical/tag search is local and deterministic. Semantic retrieval is optional: memory.index stores a finite vector bound to the current content version and an exact embedding model ID. Changing content invalidates its index. Cosine search compares only matching model IDs and vector dimensions. The index and search paths enforce the same namespace ACLs as ordinary reads/writes.

amx managed memory index --state STATE --agent coder --namespace private \
  --embedding-base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 --embedding-model EXACT_MODEL \
  --allow-provider-calls --max-entries 100
amx managed memory search --state STATE --agent coder --namespace private \
  --query 'parser architecture' --embedding-base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 \
  --embedding-model EXACT_MODEL --allow-provider-calls

These owner-side commands send selected authorized text to the explicit embedding endpoint. Supply --api-key-env NAME when needed. No provider is selected or contacted implicitly; calls, body sizes, timeouts and vector dimensions are bounded. This is retrieval over explicit memory, not an automatic long-term summary of everything agents observe.

docs.title: Value-only edits and retrieval evidence
docs.text: Use memory.patch with namespace, key, value and expected version to change only a live value. It requires both read and write access and preserves sources, tags and exact absolute expiry. memory.put is full replacement and accepts an explicit expires_at; imports retain source deadlines and skip expired entries. Owner exposure.list queries retained authenticated retrieval metadata, including reader, namespace/key, version, digest, time and route. Owner inspection and forbidden attempts do not count as agent exposure. The bounded ledger records data returned to an agent, not whether a model understood it.

docs.title: Reproduce a mixed-harness sandbox scenario
docs.text:
This guide runs a three-worker integration scenario with explicit isolation and an independent artifact check. Check provider compatibility before starting provider turns. For everyday interactive sessions, start with work sessions.

scripts/smoke-managed-models.py runs one real Claude lead turn, one real Codex coding turn, and one Pi turn against an already running local model. The broker and all three workers use separate Bubblewrap sandboxes. The script creates a private temporary team and uses the normal managed supervisor and tmux panes. It never downloads a model or starts a model server.

This is an integration acceptance scenario, not a cooperation experiment or a model-quality benchmark. The lead uses a supplied coordination helper. Pi receives the submitted source and reported test evidence in its instruction and produces an analysis-only review; its tools are disabled. A nonempty Pi response establishes that the local inference path ran, not that its verdict was correct.

docs.title: Requirements and reproduction
docs.text:
Use Linux with working unprivileged Bubblewrap namespaces, tmux, Python 3.9+, Git, and an Agentmux binary built from the current source. Install Claude Code, Codex CLI, and the maintained @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent package. The installed CLIs must pass managed doctor capability checks. Claude needs the native Read,Write,Edit,Bash tool allowlist used by this task; the managed adapter retains its safety and permission flags.

This scenario explicitly sets the Codex agent's codex_sandbox: external. Codex then delegates native tool isolation to the enforced outer Bubblewrap namespace. This option requires the Codex harness, sandbox: bubblewrap, and a real wrapper; local workers cannot select it. The native CLI's --sandbox danger-full-access selects that external-boundary contract inside the already isolated process. It adds no approval-bypass flag and grants no access to unmounted host files or credentials. Ordinary Codex configurations retain native workspace-write sandboxing by default, with no automatic fallback. Use the external policy deliberately when the host cannot support Codex's nested native sandbox; it still requires a working outer boundary.

Claude and Codex need existing login credential files. By default the script uses ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.codex/auth.json. Each must be an owned regular private 0600 file, not a symlink. Managed workers receive a private read-only native-auth snapshot at the expected sandbox path; the original source and the rest of the host home are not mounted.

First exercise the independent verifier without any model calls:

python3 scripts/smoke-managed-models.py --check-fixtures

The verifier must reject the broken fixture and accept the reference. It runs submitted Python in a fresh network-disabled Bubblewrap sandbox without broker or native credentials. Its tests remain outside participant workspaces.

Start a local OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint separately. Confirm the exact model ID with its /v1/models response, then explicitly opt into the real turns. For an endpoint already listening on port 34501 with model ID cached-qwen-1.5b:

python3 scripts/smoke-managed-models.py \
  --binary ./bin/amx \
  --allow-models \
  --pi-base-url http://127.0.0.1:34501/v1 \
  --pi-model cached-qwen-1.5b \
  --bounded-resources \
  --keep-output

The URL and model name above are an example of an already running local service; the script does not provision that service. It rejects non-loopback endpoints. The local model must support Pi's text-output completion path. Tool calling is not required. Claude and Codex use their native remote services with explicit network: host; this is not an outbound network allowlist.

Use --claude-bin, --codex-bin, and --pi-bin for executable locations, and --claude-auth-file / --codex-auth-file for credential sources. Optional --claude-model and --codex-model select explicit native models. The script discovers standard executable symlinks, Node, installed package code, and npm optional dependencies without mounting a whole home directory. A Node-based Pi launcher uses the canonical Node binary and real package entrypoint so a sandbox file bind does not change package-relative module resolution. Native executable arguments also use their canonical paths. Standalone Codex receives only its specific sibling code-mode host, bundled Bubblewrap/ripgrep, and package metadata; the containing .codex directory is not exposed. Add an exact --dependency reviewer=/absolute/package/path (or lead= / coder=) when an installation needs additional read-only runtime code. Broad paths remain subject to managed boundary validation. The handwritten sandboxed coding example shows the equivalent owner-configured boundaries; its placeholder paths need replacement.

--bounded-resources requests per-worker 2 GiB memory, one CPU, 256 processes, 1,024 open files, and 120 CPU seconds. Memory/CPU/process-tree limits require a working delegated user-systemd cgroup scope; an unavailable enforcement path fails closed. --memory-mib, --cpu-percent, --processes, --open-files, and --cpu-seconds override individual values. The overall deadline defaults to 600 seconds (--timeout, range 60–1,200). Two cloud tasks describe the requested task count, not a token or monetary spending guarantee. Native harnesses can make multiple model requests within a turn. No model task is automatically retried.

docs.title: What a successful run establishes
docs.text:
1. An owner-submitted lead task remains pending with the same ID and version across a controlled isolated-broker restart before any worker claims it. The owner does not resubmit the instruction. Readiness uses an authenticated identity response, so a stale Unix socket is insufficient.
  2. The actual Claude lead invokes authenticated operations for the shared board, project memory, and subordinate instructions. The Codex coder edits a small Python function, runs development tests, and publishes its complete source, SHA-256 digest, and reported test evidence into a scoped memory handoff.
  3. Reverse coder-to-lead instruction and private-board access are denied. The local reviewer cannot read the handoff namespace directly. It receives the bounded artifact through the lead's authorized instruction instead.
  4. Before each real native turn, a trusted read-only launch helper checks the actual authenticated identity, private HOME/workspace, own bridge paths, hidden host sentinel/state/owner credential, hidden peer broker/native credentials, hidden original auth sources, omitted owner environment secret, and configured CPU-time/open-file limits. Nongenerative help/version/login metadata probes bypass this task-specific helper check.
  5. The owner separately runs immutable normalization, type-error, generator, nonmutation, and fresh-output checks over the submitted artifact in an additional, credential-free verifier sandbox. Only that oracle can mark the coder task verified. The review model's own claims do not determine acceptance.

docs.title: Reports and cleanup
docs.text:
Standard output is a JSON summary with task counts, boundary checks, resource requests, oracle outcomes, artifact/review digests and byte counts, and reported native usage when available. It excludes source code, raw model responses, raw native diagnostics, and credential contents. Reported usage is an observation, not a billing guarantee. Use --report /new/private/report.json to save a new 0600 summary file.

The private temporary directory contains the exact generated configuration, broker database, workspace files, model outputs in task records, private logs, and a 0600 owner-operation JSONL audit. Those artifacts are sensitive despite the sanitized summary; do not publish the directory. The audit captures broker coordination, not a complete native prompt/tool/network trace.

The finally cleanup stops the manually started broker and the managed supervisor. Successful artifacts are removed unless --keep-output is set. Failures or unconfirmed cleanup retain the private directory for inspection and print its location; no automatic rerun can duplicate uncertain model work. The already running local model server remains the owner's responsibility.

docs.title: Collaboration inside native terminals
docs.text:
Agentmux keeps two choices separate: who may send an instruction, and whether its recipient may receive an agent-authored native turn. Enabling Commands in Connections grants the first. It does not silently enable the second. Native delivery is off by default.

New integrated Claude, Codex and Pi launches include a per-session adapter. Your terminal remains the place to type, approve tools, interrupt work and use the provider's normal features. The adapter does not type tmux keys, transmit unsent drafts or edit your global configuration. Pi checks its local editor for an empty draft before dispatch. --native-only disables this integration.

docs.title: Pair two native agents for tasks
docs.text:
From v0.15.0, task pairing combines command authority, receiver mode and result-return setup:

amx pair claude codex --delivery auto --session collaboration-test
amx pair claude codex --delivery auto --apply --session collaboration-test
amx attach claude --session collaboration-test

The preview changes nothing. Each --apply call loads and prints the current review, then makes one atomic change: mutual Commands, both receiver modes and own-result delivery. In the workbench, Connections → Shift+C opens one review; 1 chooses Review, 2 chooses Auto and Enter applies the frozen action.

Ask Claude in its native conversation to delegate a task to Codex. Both can return task results without reverse Messages permission. Auto affects each receiver's eligible existing queue and future work from all permitted senders. The grants and results setting can make old items newly eligible, so displayed pre-change counts are not the future queue size. Choose Review for exact-item approval. Limits, spent turns, other subscriptions and shared scopes stay saved.

Pairing requires supported owned integrated native sessions. It refuses stale versions, changed native conversations, external/native-only sessions and isolation that must be reviewed separately. An old pinned controller needs an explicit upgrade or a fresh workspace. link still controls shared chat/memory; allow and delivery remain available for one-way or custom settings.

docs.title: Manual controls and an owner-authored probe
docs.text:
Start a new workspace with the current binary, then use a regular owner shell:

amx start --session collaboration-test --detach
amx collaborate claude codex --session collaboration-test
amx delivery codex review --session collaboration-test
amx send codex "Summarize the board proposal in two sentences." \
  --mode instruction --session collaboration-test
amx delivery codex --json --session collaboration-test

Read the complete pending item's text and copy its exact candidate ID from the last command:

amx delivery codex --approve CANDIDATE_ID --session collaboration-test
amx attach codex --session collaboration-test

Review approves one exact item under the current policy version. A changed policy invalidates earlier approvals. For an owner-authored test instruction, no peer command grant is needed. To let Claude instruct Codex, enable the direction Claude → Codex → Commands in Connections, then ask Claude to use instruct through its authenticated broker CLI.

Choose Auto explicitly to receive eligible turns without each approval:

amx delivery codex auto --max-turns 20 --max-hops 4 --cooldown 1 \
  --session collaboration-test
amx delivery claude auto --session collaboration-test

In terminal Connections, the displayed recipient has its own delivery summary, separate from the sender's Commands permission. Shift+D reviews that recipient's delivery settings; Shift+A opens its pending-item chooser in Review mode. These actions also appear in Ctrl+K Actions with the recipient's stable ID. They keep the sender selected. In Sessions, the same keys apply to the selected session. Web Connections already offers Inspect receiver delivery, leading to Session detail with the same settings and pending approvals. Sender grants, receiver mode, current scopes, adapter capability, readiness and budgets all have to allow delivery.

Choosing Auto can start already queued eligible items, including boundary notices, as well as future instructions. The terminal confirmation previews the known queue count and bounded kind/sender metadata; the queue can change. Choose Review first when you want to inspect and approve one exact item's complete text. Plain amx delivery ID auto changes only the mode: it keeps saved subscriptions, turn/hop limits and cooldown. It does not grant Commands or reset spent turns.

docs.title: Modes and observations
docs.text:
Mode Behavior Manual Keep using the native CLI normally; inspect broker coordination when requested. No new peer turn is dispatched. Review Queue eligible items until the owner approves each exact candidate. Auto Deliver eligible items when the adapter can safely accept them, within the configured limits.

Direct notes, pings, readable board updates and shared-memory updates are separate subscriptions; all start off. Results of this agent's own instructions are enabled by default. An observation is labeled as data, not an instruction grant. Subscriptions never grant board/memory access or authority to command a peer. Private memory is never broadcast. Current owner role and boundary notices are delivered in Review/Auto even when note subscriptions are off, so the agent learns its changed limits. This can include an initial boundary synchronization turn after enabling delivery; it counts toward the turn limit. Notices include incoming sender permissions as well as outgoing grants and namespace access. Editing an unrelated pair does not wake other sessions whose effective boundaries remain the same.

amx delivery codex auto --notes=true --pings=true --boards=true \
  --memory-updates=true --results=true --session collaboration-test
amx delivery codex manual --session collaboration-test

Returning to Manual stops future dispatch and requests safe cancellation of the active peer delivery where the provider supports it. It does not interrupt an unrelated human turn. Isolation revokes future peer access and delivery eligibility; data already read remains known. Inspect active tasks and cancellation status too.

An instruction result returns to its issuer through a correlated task/result channel; this needs no reverse message.send or Commands grant. A native result turn still requires the issuer's Returned results subscription, its own Review/Auto delivery policy and adapter readiness. In Manual, inspect the recorded result with amx task TASK_ID or the agent-authenticated task.get operation. Result notices do not recursively generate result notices. Native turns count toward a cumulative per-agent turn limit, causal hop limits and any configured broker admission budget. Raising max_turns explicitly permits more turns; changing modes does not reset it. These are admission controls, not hard caps on provider billing or human CLI use.

docs.title: What the status means
docs.text:
Phase Evidence Pending Current queue record; no new native turn is confirmed. Earlier attempts may have run: inspect receipts and history, especially after retry. Claimed / submitting One exact attempt is reserved. Submitted Transport accepted the message, or the inbox write completed; model execution is not yet confirmed. Running Correlated native events or an explicit receiver acknowledgment confirm this delivery started. Completed Correlated settlement or an explicit receiver completion includes the result. The broker task is submitted for owner verification. Failed / cancelled The adapter has evidence of failure or cancellation. Uncertain Outcome cannot be confirmed. Agentmux does not automatically resend it. Inspect the terminal and resolve the task before another turn.

Permission revocation is checked again when claiming and when the adapter checks active delivery. Cancellation cannot undo model context or tool effects already produced. A restarted broker never assumes an in-flight native turn is safe to retry.

A successful instruct call confirms broker admission. A proposed task or pending delivery confirms queueing, not execution; inspect correlated receipts and history, especially after retries because prior attempts may have run. It does not identify the receiver's mode or prove why dispatch is blocked. Agents can inspect only their own native.status. Ask the owner to inspect another recipient with amx delivery ID --json --state /exact/workspace/state. Integrated launch context includes these instructions and owner commands even when the project repository contains no Agentmux documentation. amx delivery --help is available anywhere.

docs.title: Adapter capabilities
docs.text:
Harness Native path Current boundaries Codex Private app-server and native queue, retaining the normal TUI Exact thread/turn correlation, queued deletion and peer-turn interruption. Owner developer instructions stay intact; Agentmux appends separate context to new, resumed and forked conversations. CLI profiles and preconfigured remote transports retain manual coordination. Pi One per-invocation extension Waits for idle, trusted project, empty editor and no approval/pending input; settles only on the correlated agent settlement. Claude Code Own-child SessionStart hook and native session inbox Inbox submission alone is unconfirmed. Injected content asks the receiver to acknowledge and finish the exact delivery through its scoped CLI. A model may fail to do so. Already queued messages cannot be retracted; draft/approval preservation remains explicitly unverified in capability status. Requires a supported native inbox and enabled hooks. Antigravity / arbitrary commands Manual coordination No verified idle-wakeup adapter. Antigravity can instead be used through Pi's provider bridge.

Codex refreshes its separate Agentmux developer-context entry once per selected native conversation per bridge invocation; that entry persists in native history. Unsupported native transports keep the owner's configuration and terminal; Agentmux role-context append is unavailable in that fallback.

When human input steers a Codex peer turn, answers its native question, or joins Pi's settled activity, Agentmux returns an explicit withheld-result notice instead of sharing output that may answer the human's private input. Unsent drafts do not suppress normal results. Claude's completion remains an explicit receiver acknowledgment rather than automatic native event correlation.

In an all-native interactive workspace, the supervisor keeps healthy terminals open through a broker outage and recovers only its owned broker with bounded backoff. Sandboxed native workers use a private stable socket relay so a replaced broker socket remains reachable. In-flight work stays uncertain until explicit owner resolution; it is never replayed automatically. Managed/mixed workspaces retain their existing fail-closed shutdown behavior. Owner shutdown and configured runtime deadlines still take precedence over recovery.

docs.title: Check native delivery
docs.text:
Installed native TUI tests use loopback/offline fake providers to exercise draft preservation, idle wakeup, permissions and completion receipts. Pi requires the agent_settled lifecycle event; older or unverifiable Pi versions keep the original native invocation with manual coordination. Inspect the adapter's reported capabilities for your installed CLI.

These checks make no paid model requests. They verify the selected native integration, not every provider/account configuration. Delivery status does not show that a model understood an instruction or that its result is correct.

make build
AGENTMUX_INTEGRATION_BINARY="$PWD/bin/amx" \
  AGENTMUX_CODEX_NATIVE_INTEGRATION=1 go test -race ./internal/nativebridge/codex
AGENTMUX_CLAUDE_NATIVE_INTEGRATION=1 go test -race ./internal/nativebridge/claude
AGENTMUX_PI_NATIVE_LIVE=1 go test -race ./internal/nativebridge/pi
python3 internal/nativebridge/pi/testdata/native_broker.py --binary bin/amx
python3 internal/nativebridge/pi/testdata/native_broker.py --binary bin/amx --sandbox bubblewrap
python3 internal/nativebridge/pi/testdata/native_broker.py --binary bin/amx --sandbox bubblewrap --recovery

These require their installed CLIs. The full Pi workflow uses isolated profiles and an offline in-process provider; its sandbox fixture explicitly permits host networking but makes no external model request.

docs.title: Existing sessions and upgrades
docs.text:
An existing external session can join broker communication through connect, but that does not retrofit a native transport into its running CLI. An older owned session needs an explicit relaunch with the updated controller. Installing Agentmux does not replace a running pinned controller or restart your agents.

For a first trial, use the separate collaboration-test workspace above. When ready to upgrade an older workspace, finish or preserve its native work, inspect uncertain tasks, and deliberately restart it with amx managed restart --state /absolute/workspace/state. Whole-workspace restart stops its owned sessions; choose history through explicit per-agent relaunch when resumption is needed. Never start a second worker against the same conversation.

Launch YAML can preconfigure the initial delivery policy:

agents:
  reviewer:
    harness: pi
    interaction: interactive
    sandbox: local
    native_delivery:
      mode: review
      max_turns: 20
      max_hops: 4
      cooldown_seconds: 1
      notes: false
      pings: false
      boards: false
      memory_updates: false
      results: true

Live owner edits overlay this policy without rewriting the saved launch definition. When supplying native_delivery explicitly in YAML, set results: true if you want returned results; omitted boolean fields in that object are false. Agent-only bridge operations are native.register, native.peek, native.claim and native.event. Owner controls are native.configure and native.approve; native.status exposes scoped evidence without credentials or task leases.

Human-steered Codex turns continue when delivery is changed to Manual; the terminal remains the place to interrupt them explicitly. Cancellation of an untouched peer turn retains its original thread/turn identity after a native conversation switch. The control center provides exact-version uncertain-task fail/retry reviews; a retry is a new execution. External manual bridges do not become native delivery adapters through relaunch.

Pi can remain submitting if a draft appears before injection. A preexisting draft blocks readiness before submission begins. submitted is recorded only after the native transport accepts the message; receipt retries never inject it again. These phases describe transport evidence, not whether the model understood or completed the instruction.

docs.title: Observe running work
docs.text:
Start with one operational view, then inspect the exact task that needs attention:

amx context --session work
amx observe --session work
amx task TASK_ID --session work
amx task TASK_ID --open --session work

Replace TASK_ID with the printed task_… identity. observe prints commands containing the exact state directory so a later inspection cannot silently target another workspace. All four commands are read-only. Opening a task does not retry it or resolve its delivery.

amx observe, live managed-turn progress and the reporting timestamps on this page were introduced in v0.13.0. Upgrade an older workspace's controller and workers explicitly; installing a new CLI does not replace a running controller. An older controller can report this operation as unsupported. The output records observer_version and the pinned controller path separately; installing a new observer does not prove that an existing workspace upgraded its controller. Agentmux v0.15.0 includes structured collection diagnostics and the offline summary described below. Older v0.13.0 schema-1 captures remain readable; missing diagnostic timings stay unknown.

The capture uses disposable command-only fixtures. The running worker reports a check-in and zero native model events; stopped delivery remains uncertain.

docs.title: Read the evidence separately
docs.text:
Observation What it establishes What it does not establish Broker connected, with observation time The owner received a current broker response A worker or model is alive Observed worker pane The ownership-checked tmux inventory reports that pane's process state Useful model progress or successful work Live execution lease This retained task has a running dispatch whose lease has not expired Its process is responding or its outcome is known Worker check-in The exact leased worker recently reported to the broker The model produced a new event Native event time, count and kind The adapter observed that many JSON events for this attempt Useful reasoning, a complete transcript, or task correctness Native adapter readiness This registered adapter reported readiness; connection becomes stale after ten seconds without reporting A retained running receipt is current or completed Submitted result The worker submitted an outcome Independent verification or owner approval Verified result or trace The recorded verification or authenticated adapter evidence passed its stated checks Universal correctness or complete hidden provider activity

The terminal and web workbenches show their last successful snapshot time. An offline view retains its previous evidence and disables changes. Component errors remain separate: a reachable broker cannot turn unavailable worker inspection into confirmed liveness.

docs.title: Use attention without losing old failures
docs.text:
observe counts the entire retained task history. It reports both recorded delivery and effective delivery. An expired dispatch can therefore remain recorded as dispatching while its effective delivery is uncertain. Inspection does not rewrite that record, its version or its lease.

Attention takes one item from each populated category in rounds: recovery, recorded failure, submitted result awaiting verification, then pending work. It takes a second item from a category only after giving the other categories representation. Historical failures therefore cannot hide every new review request. Healthy live execution leases have a separate list. Each list defaults to 25 items; --limit 1..200 changes the bound. Counts remain complete when a list is truncated, and the output labels that truncation. Older tasks and retired recipients still contribute to the totals.

Retained capacity shows records, idempotency receipts, messages and tasks against their configured ceilings. Reported headroom does not guarantee admission: some capacity is reserved for shutdown/recovery and other limits still apply. The CLI also samples database, WAL and shared-memory file sizes outside the broker lock. It never follows file links or recursively walks traces and workspaces; unknown file sizes remain unknown. These byte counts are observations, not disk quotas.

amx observe --session work --limit 100
amx tasks --session work --status running
amx tasks --session work --status failed --limit 100
amx task TASK_ID --open --session work

Use the task history's printed continuation command for further pages. In the workbenches, Tasks for selected session opens the recipient's retained history. The exact task view separates instruction/result, task version, recorded delivery, native receipt, trace metadata and current recovery actions.

docs.title: Watch reporting
docs.text:
amx observe --session work --watch
amx observe --session work --watch --interval 2s --json

--watch --json emits JSONL: one complete JSON object per observation, with schema_version: 1. The interval is a delay after collection, not a promise that samples arrive at that frequency. Collection has a finite deadline; --interval accepts 250ms through one minute and requires --watch.

For a private capture, choose a new output path:

umask 077
amx observe --session work --watch --json > /private/new-observations.jsonl

Stop with Ctrl+C. Watching continues through unavailable components and emits their errors; interruption exits successfully. For automation, a one-shot partial observation emits its available JSON and exits nonzero:

amx observe --session work --json

Check complete, broker_error, runtime_error, native_error and each storage.files entry's state/problem before treating a sample as available. An unsafe or unreadable storage file makes the collection partial; an absent WAL/shared-memory file is reported separately and is not an error. complete means component observations were available; inspect attention_more, active_more and native_more for bounded inventories. The top-level collection time, broker snapshot time, worker check-in, native event time and readiness time describe different observations. They are not one atomic snapshot of every process.

These metadata snapshots and JSONL are the supported integration surface. Agentmux has no bundled OTLP/Prometheus exporter or cross-workspace trend database. Preserve sample timestamps, complete and component errors in any external aggregation; unavailable samples do not mean zero work.

docs.title: Structured collection diagnostics
docs.text:
Agentmux v0.14.0 adds diagnostics without changing observation schema version 1 or the existing human output and complete behavior:

Field Meaning diagnostics.collection_duration_ms Local elapsed collection time, including acquisition and decoding; excludes the watch delay and final output formatting diagnostics.components.broker Owner credential loading and the broker observation read diagnostics.components.runtime Ownership-checked runtime inspection; not_recorded is a legitimate headless workspace diagnostics.components.native Native summary read after a successful broker observation; not_attempted has null duration and error code diagnostics.components.storage Metadata inspection of the three known database files

Every component has state, error_code, nullable reason_code and duration_ms. observed means the collection succeeded, including a known unavailable runtime or absent storage file; it does not assert worker health. Component errors use unavailable with one of these fixed codes: credential_unavailable, unauthenticated, forbidden, timeout, canceled, transport, unsupported, invalid_response, unavailable, metadata_unavailable or unknown. Successful components have a null error code. Local call deadlines and cancellation are classified from their context; a server cancellation can also produce canceled. Unknown causes remain unknown instead of being guessed from error prose. Existing free-form component errors remain separate.

Updated controllers refine broker/native operational-read failures with three fixed reason codes: operational_read_busy means another operational read already owns the single read slot; query_budget_exhausted means the server's 250 ms query budget expired; shutdown means the Store is closed or its lifetime ended during collection. Existing error codes and human errors stay unchanged. A shorter caller deadline does not claim a server query-budget expiry. Legacy controllers and unrecognized causes leave the reason null; null never means healthy. New clients opt into the wire field so older clients continue receiving the original fault shape.

Durations use the local monotonic clock. Parallel components overlap, so their durations must not be added. Broker and native reads retain their existing three-second call limits within the collection's four-second context. These measurements describe local collection, not model latency, task completion or an uptime guarantee.

The native inventory is a fast reporting/receipt summary. It deliberately does not evaluate all queued admission candidates; native[].pending_count is null when not computed. Use amx delivery ID and the exact task view to inspect current admission policy and queued native work. Metadata indexes keep large task bodies out of operational counts and ranking. These projections use a separate read-only database snapshot, outside the worker coordination lock. The query budget remains 250 ms; slow query cancellation cannot hold the worker's connection or its unchanged 500 ms lease monitor.

One operational read runs at a time. Overlapping observations return unavailable; a watch collects again on its next tick. An unfinished query reports unavailable evidence. Credentials are rechecked before a completed sample is published.

The output omits task/result bodies, raw native events, provider usage bodies and credentials. It still contains local paths, task/session identities, timestamps and authenticated trace metadata. Keep captures private and review them before sharing. This is an operational record, not a credential bundle or an immutable execution attestation.

docs.title: Summarize a private capture offline
docs.text:
Stop the capture with Ctrl+C, then run the dependency-free Python reporter. Release archives include scripts/summarize-observations.py; the binary installer installs amx only. Extract the scripts/ folder from the archive matching your observer version, or use the corresponding source checkout. Run from that archive/checkout directory as below, or pass its absolute script path to python3 from any directory. Choose a gap threshold appropriate to your capture interval:

python3 scripts/summarize-observations.py /private/new-observations.jsonl --max-gap 5s
python3 scripts/summarize-observations.py /private/new-observations.jsonl --max-gap 5s \
  --json > /private/new-observation-report.json

The command also accepts - for standard input. It makes no provider calls, does not open the workspace and does not write the input capture. A successful report records the SHA256 of every original input byte. That hash identifies the consumed capture; it does not authenticate who produced it.

The report includes sample count, first/last timestamps, observed time span, forward gaps above the chosen threshold and backward/repeated timestamps. First and last follow file order; span means maximum minus minimum timestamp. It counts reported completeness and component availability at samples, with bounded gap and availability-transition examples. These counts do not estimate uptime between samples or establish task quality.

Retained tasks, task states, recorded/effective delivery, recovery eligibility, attention and live leases remain gauges. Their first, last and known peaks are not completed-task throughput or success rates. Capacity ratios use each sample's own ceiling; changing ceilings remain visible. Database, WAL and shared-memory sizes distinguish absent zero-byte files from unknown sizes. Adjacent size decreases can reflect checkpointing or replacement. Observed runtime attempt-identity changes count adjacent known samples, not actual restarts. Missing samples break those comparisons; progress event counts are never correlated across attempts.

Native pending totals remain unknown when any listed pending count is null, the inventory is truncated or its collection is unavailable. Known partial sums are labeled separately. An unavailable inventory is not counted as a confirmed untruncated inventory. Legacy captures without diagnostics keep their collection durations and error-code observations unknown. The JSON report's diagnostic_reason_code_samples counts only the three fixed reported reasons with compatible unavailable component/error states; missing or null reasons use not_recorded, and other or inconsistent values use other. These counts describe sampled reports, not authenticated cause attestations.

Each file must contain one exact state identity and newline-terminated JSONL records. The parser rejects mixed states, unsupported schemas, duplicate keys, malformed UTF-8/JSON, non-finite numbers, records over 2 MiB and inventories over 200 items. It streams one bounded record at a time and retains at most 16 examples of each episode category, with omitted counts. A rejected capture exits nonzero and emits no report or partial-input hash.

Only fixed aggregate fields enter the report: workspace paths, task/agent/trace identities, MACs, raw errors and unknown fields are omitted; unrecognized map labels and diagnostic codes use aggregate buckets. Original captures still contain sensitive operational metadata and remain private. Review even the filtered report before sharing it.

docs.title: Diagnose silence and interruption
docs.text:
For a managed headless turn, a fresh worker check-in with an unchanged native event count means the controller is reporting while no new adapter event has been observed. Some native tools run quietly. A stale check-in can reflect a stopped process, lost transport or an unavailable broker. Neither observation alone proves that a model is stalled or that side effects stopped.

Progress is metadata for one exact task attempt, fenced by recipient, credential instance/generation and execution lease. Heartbeats do not advance the native event timestamp or renew execution permission. Retry, cancellation and credential rotation cannot borrow the previous attempt's observations. Broker restart loses these ephemeral observations; missing progress means unknown, not zero activity. An expired unchanged attempt may retain its last observed progress beside effective uncertainty, but cannot refresh it.

For interactive sessions, inspect Native collaboration and the original native terminal. Adapter readiness and transport receipts remain separate. An adapter can stop reporting while its retained receipt still says running; the reporting warning does not convert that receipt into success or failure. External/manual bridges do not gain automatic delivery from being listed.

If delivery is uncertain, inspect the task's complete evidence and stop or fence its prior process before considering retry. Recovery is an explicit review of the exact current task/version. A retry can repeat side effects and spend another attempt's allowance. Expired runtime budgets can remove retry from the available actions. See recovery.

docs.title: Drill into retained evidence
docs.text:
Task output includes the native receipt and any trace summary. Receipt phase is transport evidence; owner task verification remains a separate action. For a completed opted-in managed trace, use the exact IDs and MAC anchor from that task:

amx managed trace verify --state STATE --agent AGENT_ID --id TRACE_ID --mac TASK_MAC
amx managed trace show --state STATE --agent AGENT_ID --id TRACE_ID --mac TASK_MAC

These trace commands also work with the broker offline. show contains sensitive task/tool content and emits verified JSONL; the live progress channel contains none of that raw content. The trace guide describes opt-in capacity limits, coverage exclusions and portable signed bundles. The workbench's trace summary is recorded metadata, not a fresh file verification.

Guided coding runs have their own retained evidence rather than this broker's task queue. Use amx work status and amx work show RUN_ID --open, or amx flow status RUN_DIRECTORY and amx flow explain RUN_DIRECTORY for advanced runs. See checked coding and advanced workflows. Research additionally exposes a separate runner heartbeat and reviewed phase barrier controls in Research.

docs.title: Validate the route you use
docs.text: Run the model-free observation regressions to check metadata fences, unavailable components and honest recovery state. Recorded protocol frames and local compatible-endpoint fixtures establish adapter behavior for those fixtures. Subscription login/startup establishes only acceptance of that configured route. Actual provider task and continuation checks must record the selected CLI version, authentication route and verified artifact separately. These are not interchangeable evidence of provider reliability, elapsed operational use or comparative task quality.

docs.title: Provider compatibility
docs.text: Agentmux launches installed provider CLIs or connects Pi to an explicitly configured inference endpoint. Install and authenticate the selected CLI first; Agentmux does not create provider accounts, log in or download model weights. Provider versions, accounts, models and optional tools can change compatibility.

docs.title: Choose a route
docs.text:
Route Interactive sessions Managed tasks and history Boundary Claude Code Native terminal with optional coordination context and delivery Fresh or persistent structured turns Trusted local execution or an explicit Bubblewrap profile; coding needs a native tool allowlist Codex CLI Native terminal with optional coordination context and delivery Fresh or persistent structured turns; custom endpoints use Responses Trusted local execution or Bubblewrap; external native sandbox policy requires an enforced outer boundary Pi Native terminal with optional coordination context and delivery Fresh or persistent RPC turns; compatible endpoints use Chat Completions Explicit runtime dependencies, endpoint/model metadata and selected authentication Native Antigravity --native-only, with normal native configuration/history Fresh trusted-local structured turns Native keyring/history stay on the host; direct isolated authentication and managed persistence are unsupported Antigravity inference through Pi Use Pi for the coordinated session Pi owns isolated tools and persistent history A separately managed trusted host bridge retains native Antigravity login Generic command harness Owner-selected command Fresh command tasks No inferred native history or provider identity

The original v1 pane launcher also supports additional launch aliases described in pane harnesses. Those aliases do not imply managed adapter or native delivery support.

docs.title: Configure and inspect
docs.text:
claude --version
codex --version
pi --version
amx doctor
amx managed setup --output team.yaml
amx managed doctor team.yaml

Run only the version commands for CLIs you intend to use. Complete their native login/startup prompts separately. Setup and doctor perform bounded capability, authentication/metadata and isolation checks without generating model responses. Unchecked authentication and endpoint capabilities remain visible as warnings. Review the generated paths, tool permissions, credentials, network policy and resource limits before launching. See managed setup.

For npm Pi, use the canonical Node executable and real package entrypoint with explicit read-only package dependencies. Mounting a launcher symlink alone can break package-relative resolution even if --version succeeds. Codex standalone installations can also need companion executables; setup discovers known layouts. Avoid mounting an entire provider home as a dependency.

Custom Codex endpoints must implement Responses. Pi endpoints must implement the selected Chat Completions contract. For Ollama/vLLM, configure the exact API base, model ID, real context limit and expected tool support. Missing metadata or an advertised capability does not establish actual model behavior. Use the Antigravity bridge guide for that separate lifecycle.

docs.title: Verify the selected integration
docs.text:
Check startup, inference, continuation and tools separately. A successful help or metadata request does not show that a model can answer; a text answer does not show that tools work; a continuation check does not establish the correctness of a review. Use a disposable workspace and explicit model/endpoint selections, finite deadlines and small turn budgets for provider checks.

Start with model-free coordination and isolation checks:

make build
python3 scripts/smoke-managed.py --binary bin/amx
python3 scripts/smoke-managed-interactive.py --binary bin/amx

These require the host capabilities documented by each script and make no model calls. The mixed-harness scenario and bounded autonomous workflow provide opt-in real tasks with independent artifact verification. The workflow validation guide covers amx work and amx flow; their isolation is configured separately from managed teams. Retain private reports for your own installation and inspect failures or uncertain outcomes before starting another attempt.

Local execution retains host filesystem authority. Requested Bubblewrap and resource boundaries must fail closed when unavailable. Model services outside worker sandboxes remain separately trusted, and native turns may contain several provider requests. Turn limits and reported usage are not hard billing caps. A successful bounded scenario establishes its configured path and task, not universal provider/tool compatibility, model quality or long-term reliability.

docs.title: Quality targets and evidence
docs.text:
Agentmux's next quality improvements focus on a reliable first result, maintainable controls and measured outcomes. Numerical ratings are judgments; these acceptance criteria make the evidence behind a future rating reviewable. An implemented feature or passing fixture does not earn a maturity or productivity score by itself.

Area Evidence required before arguing for 9/10 Technical capability The primary released workflow works from installation through inspected application; supported provider routes have recorded native task and continuation checks with independent artifact validation. Unsupported routes are clear. Safety design and assurance Boundary regressions pass with actual isolation; an independent adversarial review covers credentials, authorization, source application and recovery; material findings are resolved and retested. Regression testing Linux and macOS installed-artifact first runs pass; failure controls prove that wrong output, failed actors, timeouts, stale evidence and interrupted publication cannot become success; conditional provider/resource coverage is recorded explicitly. Maintainability Public entry points have focused responsibilities; changes to workflow state and authority have documented invariants and targeted regression coverage; another contributor can implement and review a representative change without maintainer intervention. File count alone is not a score. Onboarding and usability At least five first-time participants from the intended power-user audience install the release and complete the first-result journey unaided; at least four finish within five minutes after prerequisites, with no unsafe source mutation. Also observe resume, launch, delegation, inspection and recovery in daily use with declared timing/error criteria. Record failures, experience and assistance; repeat after fixing blockers. Operational maturity Record at least seven days of realistic supervised use on supported environments, including provider interruption, credential refresh, restart and storage growth. Preserve task outcomes and unresolved incidents; a fast fault soak does not substitute for elapsed operation. Productivity advantage Run the matched evaluation against a declared single-agent baseline and a relevant public alternative; retain failures, costs where actually available, blind artifact grading and uncertainty. Require a repeatable useful improvement with acceptable quality and overhead. A small pilot cannot establish a general advantage.

The first-result command and offline comparison controls validate infrastructure. They do not represent new-user observations, native model quality or a comparative benchmark. Keep real evaluation evidence private until its contents have been reviewed for publication.

docs.title: Recorded engineering evidence
docs.text:
The bounded command-worker soak records 60 verified turns, 61 audited tasks, 12 clean restarts and an in-flight broker crash. The interrupted attempt remained uncertain, its process stopped, and the owner resolved it as failed without automatic replay. Completed traces were verified after recovery. This took 66.66 seconds, made zero model calls, and used disposable fixtures. It is not evidence of seven days of native use.

The observability regressions cover large retained histories, complete counts, fair bounded attention and additive metadata-index migration. Query-plan checks reject reads of task bodies during operational counting/ranking. A separate read-only connection keeps slow queries and cancellation outside the worker's unchanged 500 ms lease monitor. Tests block the actual read path, retain the 250 ms query budget and check credential rotation and shutdown before publication. Worker check-ins remain separate from native events; unknown reporting never becomes a successful task outcome.

Agentmux v0.14.0 adds fixed diagnostic codes and local collection timings to schema-1 observations. The offline operational report summarizes sampled availability, gaps, retained-state/capacity gauges and storage changes, while preserving missing evidence as unknown. It omits source paths, task identities and raw errors, and records the complete input hash. Regression controls cover malformed captures, privacy and bounded memory; an optional actual-CLI integration exercises a live command-only task and a partial observation after shutdown. This prepares operational evidence collection; it does not supply seven days of native use or unaided user results.

The comparison summary keeps failures, incomplete/unstarted attempts and paired outcomes visible. Its timing summaries do not infer a winner, model quality or unknown provider usage. Deterministic fixture results validate that reporting route, rather than establishing a competitive advantage.

Fresh AI peer reviews added reproducible controls for escaped secret publication, ambiguous signed trace envelopes, concurrent trace changes and cancellation races. These are scoped code reviews and regressions, not an external human security audit. The subscription pilot has frozen contract graders and route guards; preparation and metadata checks alone are not measured model or competitor outcomes.

A subscription-route smoke completed a newly authored Go exercise in 86.541 seconds using Codex 0.166.0 with ChatGPT authentication and Claude Code 2.1.317 with first-party Pro subscription authentication. Four native CLI sessions ran. Controller checks and the frozen external grader passed; the confirmed patch applied only to the fixture and independently reproduced its final files. Observed process cleanup was clean. The record identifies the source build, rather than claiming that a later release archive was used.

Both model reviews approved without findings and reported not running tests. Their approvals are separate from controller and external test evidence. The preceding duplicate-flag setup failure remains recorded. The workflow's sonnet profile was overridden by the pinned claude-sonnet-5-5 request; the provider's resolved model and inference-request count remain unknown. This small route check establishes no comparative productivity or long-term reliability result.

Guided work in v0.14.0 addresses the redundant-turn case identified by that smoke. After independently passing implementation checks, an initial fresh-context approval of the exact same revision can skip the response and second-review phases. Retained reports mark those phases skipped with their reason, rather than recording imaginary model turns. Final acceptance checks still run, and source/result freshness plus explicit application guards remain. With one implementation attempt, the clean path uses two native CLI turns; retries increase that count and requested changes keep the full review loop. Legacy plans without the declared policy retain their previous behavior. Model-free controls establish those branches and rejection behavior.

A November 4 subscription smoke exercised that clean path in 69.093 seconds with exactly two native CLI sessions: Codex implementation and Claude review. The original approval, both skipped phases, final checks, full retained-report load, external grader and confirmed fixture-only application were verified. Its generic final files and grader contract reproduce without models. This used the clean bf3a578 source build labeled 0.14.0-pre, not a published release archive. The separate November 3 and November 4 records establish no speedup or competitive advantage.

A private exploratory subscription pilot ran three selected historical repository tasks once with a native Codex baseline and once through the actual published v0.14.0 Codex/Claude workflow. The baseline passed 3/3, while Agentmux passed 1/3. Two Agentmux implementations hit an implicit 180-second profile limit before review/application, despite a longer overall deadline. The outer guard separately rejected observed background processes and cleaned its tracked identities. These are undelivered-workflow failures, not correctness scores for completed patches.

The first four admissions were invalidated by a cumulative process-tracker limit and are retained separately. The corrected frozen study used seven native CLI admissions, with eleven across both studies. Grader/artifact integrity and the independent evidence audit passed. Raw source, logs and local paths remain private; the linked aggregate contains only reviewed metadata. Unequal workflow and turn allowances, one repeat, selected historical tasks, trusted-local access and unknown served-model revisions prevent a general speed, quality or competitive claim.

The v0.15.0 budget and bounded process-diagnostic changes address the concrete engineering findings. A separate regression record covers only the two failed cases: both passed 2/2 using the clean 0.15.0-rc1 source build, not a published binary. Fresh review, mandatory final checks, the same frozen external graders and fixture-only application passed. One extra package race-test command hit four native-sandbox Unix-socket permission errors; focused checks and the frozen contracts passed. This is not a full-suite success claim. The original native 3/3 versus Agentmux 1/3 remains unchanged, with no baseline rerun or pooled pass rate. Requested model aliases still do not verify served revisions, and these targeted rechecks establish no speedup or competitive advantage.

Use workflow validation for engineering checks, evaluation for usability and comparative task studies, and release verification for the bytes delivered to users.

docs.title: Agentmux Recipes
docs.text:
This guide shows concrete starting points for common Agentmux workflows.

These recipes use the original YAML layout mode (init / load) and raw pane controls. For everyday Claude/Codex conversations, begin with amx start and the work-session guide. That workflow provides the authenticated coordination broker, collaboration groups and live permissions.

Use the recipes below when you want custom tmux pane layouts and commands.

If you want the fastest copy-and-tweak path, start from one of these files:

  • docs/recipes/coding-starter.yaml: edit 3 fields and launch a coding workspace
  • docs/recipes/review-starter.yaml: edit 3 fields and launch a review workspace

docs.title: Coding Session
docs.text:
Use this when you want one session for editing, tests, git, and an AI helper pane.

Best starter:

./bin/amx init coding-starter coding.yaml

Fuller starter:

./bin/amx init default coding.yaml

coding-starter is the fastest path when you want a small file to tweak.
