Native/provider hidden state, internal prompts, undeclared file reads and unreported tool/network activity are outside this adapter's coverage. A native CLI may condense or omit event details. The prepared input is exact for that turn; this is not a claim of full hidden-model context or every filesystem read.

docs.title: Credentials, interruption and upgrades
docs.text:
Managed workers reload the selected, filtered native credential source between turns. An external native login/refresh can atomically update the owner's source file; the next turn sees it without restarting a healthy worker. Snapshots remain read-only in sandboxes. Automatic provider OAuth renewal and writes back from an agent are not performed. A missing/invalid source stops new claims. An interactive native process retains its prepared snapshot until exit; relaunch it when a refreshed source must be loaded.

With a running v0.13.0-or-newer broker, use direct owner inspection:

amx tasks --status running --state STATE
amx task TASK_ID --state STATE
amx task TASK_ID --open --state STATE

--open pins the exact task in the workbench, including older tasks and retired recipients. It shows recorded delivery, current recovery evidence and the explicit task/version review; opening never retries or resolves the task. These shortcuts have been available since v0.13.0. Trace verification and bundle inspection above also work without a running broker.

The lower-level managed activity, managed status, task.list, task.get and conversation.status remain available for inspecting state. Delivery uncertainty is preserved after a broker crash or transport loss. Stop old workers before any owner resolution:

amx managed down --state STATE
# In one terminal, run the broker in the foreground:
amx managed serve --state STATE --sandbox bubblewrap

If managed down or the shutdown stage of managed restart fails, keep the JSON fault and follow the exact-state recovery commands printed to stderr. Inspect status, open affected owned native terminals with amx attach --state STATE, and finish or exit their native CLIs normally. Detaching or closing an observer leaves those processes running. Retry managed down and confirm it succeeds before restarting a broker or resolving uncertain delivery. Broker and terminal availability remain unconfirmed until inspected.

In another terminal, inspect the exact task and resolve its current version:

amx managed call task.get --credential-file STATE/owner.json \
  --json '{"id":"TASK_ID"}'
amx managed call task.resolve --credential-file STATE/owner.json \
  --json '{"id":"TASK_ID","version":CURRENT_VERSION,"resolution":"fail"}'

Replace TASK_ID and CURRENT_VERSION with the returned task identity/version.

Use resolution: retry only after checking side effects and deciding to execute again. It is a new charged attempt. Workers validate the exact current lease before native launch, during monitoring and before completion; an old worker cannot borrow the replacement attempt's running state. A periodic check cannot undo side effects already in progress, so stopping the old process is still required before retry. Upgrade every worker, including SSH workers: a new broker does not add these observation checks to an older worker executable. Persistent native conversations can remain blocked after interrupted execution; conversation.reset explicitly starts a new generation after task delivery is resolved. Old history is retained, not silently resumed as confirmed work.

For an exited workspace-owned interactive terminal, amx relaunch AGENT_ID --state STATE keeps its identity and healthy peers, and starts a fresh native conversation by default. Select --resume last, --resume picker, or a native conversation ID explicitly when supported by that harness. This does not retry a broker task, reset a managed conversation fence, renew runtime, or revive a revoked agent. A live terminal must exit before relaunch. See work sessions for the CLI and dashboard workflow.

Disk capsule quarantine has separate owner inspection and digest-fenced recovery controls; see hardening. Do not remove journals or partially published workspace/history trees by hand.

For an upgrade, stop workers and broker, back up the complete private state (including SQLite/WAL consistency, credentials, history, trace key and anchors), then install an explicitly selected release and run managed doctor before restart. Preserve the original deadline and native conversation generations. Never replace a running executable in place. The release installer checks published SHA256 and uses an atomic destination replacement with explicit --replace; checksum verification is not an independent publisher signature. Restore a matching binary plus complete state backup together if rollback is needed. No live schema migration or zero-downtime upgrade guarantee is made. Older collaboration records remain readable but require an explicit owner legacy_policy choice before group edits; see live permissions. Keep recovery digests and their matching records together. Removing lifecycle or live-resource records is not a supported way to clear a pause or budget.

docs.title: Everyday control center
docs.text:
Agentmux keeps each native conversation interactive. The terminal is the main work surface; the local black/purple web app provides observation and reviewed control. Both surfaces identify actions by stable session ID.

The shortcuts below are included in v0.15.0. They retain the same explicit permissions, delivery policies and recovery reviews.

docs.title: Upgrade an existing workspace
docs.text: make install updates the amx executable. New workspaces use the new controller. Existing workspaces keep their pinned controller and native conversations. A new amx attach -s NAME upgrades the observer without restarting those agents; backend features such as retirement, memory patches and complete task counts require the updated controller. An older controller reports unsupported operations; it does not silently substitute a weaker edit. An unavailable complete-history API stays local to Board/Events: the roster and owner controls remain connected, with recent snapshots labeled as partial. Use a fresh workspace for the complete feature set, or stop and reopen an old one only after its conversations are finished.

docs.title: Find and act
docs.text:
• Ctrl+P finds a session by title, ID, provider, project or original terminal. Enter opens its native terminal; Tab selects it in the current workbench.
  • Ctrl+K opens searchable Actions. Search for rename, budget, delivery, attention, disconnect, archive or recovery. Each action shows its target and explains unavailable actions. Tasks for selected session opens that exact recipient's retained history and clears old search, state and attention filters. Later replies from a previous selection cannot replace the new history.
  • Shift+N creates another session using the selected provider and project. Enter an optional task title and review the launch, including the provider's default model and trusted local host execution. Advanced settings remain available through Actions.
  • F1 returns from a native terminal to that attachment's workbench. Focus follows the exact native session; editing drafts keep their original target.
  • Ctrl+W opens the workspace chooser while retaining an editor or review. The chooser owns the keyboard immediately while inventory loads; Esc cancels late results and returns to the unchanged draft or review. Interactive handoff uses the outer attachment, preserving previous dashboards and other clients. A standalone observer shows an exact attach command.

Press / or Ctrl+F in the running-workspace chooser to search names, exact state paths and status. With a search active, ordinary letters are search text; use arrows or Ctrl+N/P to navigate, Ctrl+U to clear and Esc to cancel. amx context explains the workspace an ordinary CLI command selects, with exact attach/inspect commands.

The web Actions menu invokes the same kinds of session operations. Sessions, Existing terminals and Connections use the same meaning across surfaces. In terminal Connections, [ focuses Sender and ] focuses Recipient; Tab or Shift+Tab switches between them. Up/Down changes only the highlighted identity. Changing focus preserves both selected identities and permissions; Left/Right still changes views. Connections has graph and searchable list representations. The list pages 50 entries at a time, distinguishes loaded permissions from uninspected sessions, and reveals keyboard focus. Explicit selection reveals its roster entry; background refreshes preserve your current focus. Attention filters show recorded review, delivery blockage, uncertainty and failure; they do not infer whether a model is thinking or waiting at an unreported native prompt.

The web graph automatically groups enabled connections and shared-access links. Drag or Shift+Arrow pins a node; local pins survive connection changes for that workspace/study attempt. Auto arrange releases pins and refits, while Fit preserves them. An unchanged visible topology stays still through polling, title changes and selection. Denied preview edges do not influence grouping, and arranging nodes changes no permissions. Use List view to inspect exact directions or work beyond the graph's 40-session display limit.

docs.title: Connect and disconnect precisely
docs.text:
amx link claude codex -s work
amx allow claude codex commands -s work
amx mode codex review -s work
amx unlink claude codex -s work

unlink disables only the exact pair/group contribution. Select a particular group with amx disconnect --group GROUP_ID -s work. Other groups and explicit permissions can still allow access; inspect the effective explanation. Reconnect preserves the group's saved instruction setting. A saved group can still be disabled after an original member has been revoked or retired.

amx isolate claude -s work disconnects Claude from all peer coordination. Workbench and web isolation controls review affected groups, scopes and teams. Isolation also dissolves teams owned by the selected session for every member, removes its memberships, and withdraws pending invitations. These team changes are permanent: reconnecting does not restore the original team. Reviews list and version-check the exact team effects, including an initially empty set. Already accepted tasks need separate cancellation, and previously returned information remains known. Permission to send and native delivery are separate: note/ping subscriptions can leave an allowed message in the inbox. The controls show the receiver's mode, readiness reason and known pending coverage. In terminal Connections, Shift+D configures the displayed recipient and Shift+A reviews its inbox without changing the selected sender. Ctrl+K exposes the same recipient-targeted actions. In Sessions, these keys target the selected session. Enabling Commands queues instructions; Manual delivery does not start a native turn. Auto is an explicit owner choice that can also dispatch existing eligible queue items. Its confirmation previews bounded queue metadata; choose Review to inspect and approve one exact item first.

docs.title: Recover without guessing
docs.text:
Stopping or revoking a session in a dashboard reviews the exact session and descendants first. Detaching keeps them running. Native Manual pauses future peer admission; human-steered turns continue until they settle or the human interrupts them explicitly. Untouched Codex peer turns cancel using their original thread and turn IDs, including after a conversation switch.

Uncertain task recovery reviews the exact task/version and allowed fail/retry choice. Expired execution leases also appear in owner recovery and attention, while recorded delivery state remains unchanged. Expired cancellation permits fail resolution only; deadlines can also rule out retry. Use amx task TASK_ID -s NAME to read those distinct fields from the CLI, or amx task TASK_ID --open -s NAME to open the exact task in the workbench's Tasks view. This uses its stable ID directly, including for old tasks and retired recipients. Opening never retries or resolves it; review its evidence and the current task/version before explicitly confirming a recovery action. The printed open command retains the exact workspace selector. --open cannot be combined with --json. Web attention summaries link to the exact recipient's tasks, even after the recipient leaves the active roster. Opening history never resolves anything. A retry is another execution and can repeat side effects. The web retains an unconfirmed submission's identity across reconnect so checking/replaying the same submission does not silently create a second instruction. Editing a draft creates a distinct intent only after the previous uncertainty is handled.

Existing external bridges keep their original terminal location. Their helper can read the broker inbox after the native agent receives the setup; it does not retrofit automatic delivery into the existing process. Known ownership in another authenticated workspace is displayed before preparing another bridge.

docs.title: Keep history and retire finished sessions
docs.text:
Board/inbox history is filtered at the broker before pagination. Task history has recipient/state filters. Reading an older event keeps that identity until Home explicitly returns to live activity.

After an owned session is stopped and its worker exits:

amx retire SESSION_ID -s work
amx ls --archived -s work

Retirement releases the active definition slot while preserving the immutable ID, attribution and history. A retired ID cannot be reused or revived. External bridges can be revoked and retired without closing their original terminals. Value-only editing of live memory preserves sources, tags and absolute expiry. After reviewing a deleted or expired entry, saving deliberately creates a new live value using the exact reviewed CAS version. Concurrent import changes report a conflict rather than claiming the archive was already present. The exposure ledger distinguishes current access from authenticated retrieval of a specific version; retrieval does not prove understanding. Ledger retention is bounded to 10,000 receipt records and absence is not proof of no prior exposure.

docs.title: Follow a study
docs.text:
amx research watch PRIVATE_OUTPUT --follow
amx research study PRIVATE_OUTPUT
amx research history PRIVATE_OUTPUT --type team.join --limit 100

Study watching continues across completed attempts and gaps between trials. Status and archived history verify the saved trial plan against the frozen manifest; inconsistent plans are rejected rather than changing the observed completion count or omitting archived trials. The terminal research details expose trial, admitted population, deadline and phase tasks. Web Follow study observes later trials; mutations retain an exact attempt fence and old reviews cannot apply to a new trial. Archived coordination and retrieval evidence can be searched and paged after shutdown. A stop accepted during the last phase prevents the next trial. At trial transitions, pause and a consumed step keep the next attempt paused. Without --start-paused, an unused step permits exactly one phase; --start-paused takes precedence and pauses every new attempt. Carried controls are audited interventions.

Behavior CSV schema 2 preserves decision choices, partners, received escrow, reward pools, lineage and phase-task IDs without exporting prompts. Dynamic population analysis includes trajectories and labels baselines as using the initial fixed population, with a comparability warning when composition changes.

For a multi-session CLI setup, specify the project on every addition; selecting a workspace does not inherit its project directory:

amx up -s daily -p /path/to/project -d
amx new reviewer --harness codex -p /path/to/project -s daily
amx new investigator --harness claude -p /path/to/project -s daily

docs.title: Agentmux visual workflow guide
docs.text:
Use Agentmux for a checked coding request, several native agent sessions, bounded automation or controlled multiagent studies. The terminal is the place to work directly with agents; the web app provides a larger view of relationships, shared context and evidence. Coding workflows also retain private offline HTML reports without requiring a running work-session broker or web app.

The managed runtime and workbench are experimental. This guide follows current main, including the power-user shortcuts and exact-task recovery navigation. The base amx work and amx flow journeys are also available in v0.13.0, including the inspection and workspace shortcuts shown here. For a first checked fixture without provider setup, start with amx demo. Native providers must be installed and authenticated separately. A new installation does not replace an existing workspace's pinned controller; use a fresh workspace for all current features, or upgrade deliberately.

Screenshots were captured on 2026-11-04 from source d5265d3c152d, using amx 0.15.0, in disposable command-only workspaces and a scripted research trial with explicitly trusted local execution. They show real current controls; they measure neither model quality nor isolation. Terminal images render live tmux captures with trailing empty rows cropped. Capture provenance records source, fixture conditions and image hashes. Open any image at full size.

docs.title: Choose a workflow
docs.text: What you want Start here Keep control through One coding change with implementation, review and checks Checked coding change Preview, finite turns, fresh review, report and explicit apply Compare alternative implementations or build a custom mission Advanced workflow plans Pinned snapshots, external checks, retained patches and freshness Several independent Claude or Codex conversations Everyday sessions Native terminals, titles, session switcher Ten sessions with just a few collaborating pairs Temporary collaboration Exact groups, directional permissions, receiver modes A concrete end-to-end collaboration example Write a poem together Review delivery, Tasks, Board, native terminals Reusable team knowledge Private and shared memory Exact namespaces, versions and retrieval evidence A team working from an initial goal Managed and autonomous work Task outcomes, wake subscriptions and finite limits Agents recruiting or forming their own teams Dynamic teams and recruitment Approved templates, invitations, consent, capacity Cooperation versus competition experiments Research and competition Frozen design, phase controls, objective outcomes More agents or another machine Scale and remote workers Admission limits, scoped views, explicit SSH placement

docs.title: Ask for a checked coding change
docs.text:
From a Git project with an initial commit and the selected native CLIs installed, preview your request:

amx work "Fix the login redirect" -- go test ./...

The preview shows the check, phases, provider profiles, deadline, maximum turns and private result location. It starts no models and creates no run files. Replace go test ./... with the executable and arguments that verify your task. The text after -- is literal argv; use an owner-maintained script for shell logic.

This is a real report from the deterministic amx demo fixture, with no model calls. The practical sequence for your own task is preview → run → inspect → explicitly apply; the report keeps the checked content and outcome visible.

When the preview is suitable, explicitly permit provider execution:

amx work "Fix the login redirect" --allow-models -- go test ./...
amx work status
amx work show latest

Trusted-local setup selects installed native CLIs and shows both profiles in the preview. With Codex and Claude installed, Codex implements and Claude reviews. A lone CLI uses separate fresh contexts for both roles. --coder and --reviewer pin your choices; isolated profiles retain their explicit credential defaults. Each review starts a fresh native session with the task, acceptance criteria and current files, excluding implementation chat and earlier review conclusions. A final explicit approval and successful checks are required before application. A failed check, tool denial, malformed review or uncertain transport remains visible in the retained outcome.

In v0.13.0, copy a stable run ID from amx work list --limit 10 and use amx work show RUN_ID --open to generate and open a fresh private report. The command stays bound to that selected run. In v0.12.0, open the saved report.html path printed by show. Reports are separate from the live owner app launched by amx web; inspection starts no models. After reviewing the patch and evidence, apply deliberately:

amx work apply latest

Application rechecks the source, checked revision, final approval and patch. It refuses stale results and leaves committing or pushing to you. After an interrupted application, inspect amx work status and use amx work recover latest to resolve the journal against exact source content; recovery does not replay the patch. Interrupted provider work is never automatically replayed.

Private Git snapshots separate retained data; the default trusted local tools still have host filesystem and network authority. On Linux, --isolation bubblewrap additionally requires filesystem, PID and network namespaces with no weaker fallback. Tools see the assigned worktree and selected runtime dependencies; reviewer workspaces are read-only. Checks get no provider credentials or network. Native inference needs exact allowed origins and explicit selected credentials; isolated Antigravity uses host inference with Pi tools inside the capsule. See work on a task for a complete isolated command, provider prerequisites, budgets and operational boundaries.

docs.title: Compare alternatives or build a mission
docs.text:
Use amx flow when you need an owner-authored plan rather than the default coding journey. Start with the complete command-only example in a disposable Git project. It runs real local commands without model calls, checks two independent candidates and retains an offline report.

Workflow Result to inspect flow run Alternatives from the same snapshot with separate worktrees and checks flow mission Bounded dependency steps, configured review gates and final acceptance checks flow check Verification pinned to the checked content; keep its sibling .git fingerprint store flow watch A bounded review for each eligible changed snapshot; unchanged content does not retrigger flow lab Repetitions against one starting snapshot with rotated candidate order flow explain Saved inputs, patch integrity and current freshness flow handoff A private Markdown brief; saved-brief delivery respects receiver permissions and mode

Command plans and checks execute owner-selected code even without --allow-models; that flag admits provider turns. Keep output directories outside the source and retain the worktrees, selection manifests and evidence stores together. flow apply is always a separate source mutation; flow recover resolves an interrupted application without replay. See advanced workflows for strict plan fields, isolated execution and exact saved-brief delivery.

docs.title: Navigate the terminal and web app
docs.text:
The left column selects a session. Tab moves focus between the sidebar and content; the focused header is purple. Its task title can change; its Agentmux ID stays stable. The top row selects a view of that session or workspace. You do not need to unselect a session before choosing another one.

Action Terminal control Select a different session Tab to the session sidebar, then Up/Down Navigate messages, tasks, memory or teams Tab to content, then Up/Down; Enter reads a selected item Find a task, provider, project or ID Ctrl+P, type a query, then Up/Down Enter the selected native CLI Enter with the session sidebar focused, or from Ctrl+P; F1 returns Select a search result without entering its CLI Tab in the session switcher Leave a search, editor or review Esc Change views Left/Right or 1–8 outside an editor Find an action without remembering its key Ctrl+K Add a session or change its title or role Shift+N, Shift+L, Shift+V Choose another workspace Ctrl+W or Shift+W See help for the current context ?; Ctrl+G while editing or reviewing Open the board from a native terminal Ctrl+b, release, then b Detach while keeping sessions alive Ctrl+b, release, then d

Uppercase shortcuts mean hold Shift. In an editor, letters and arrows edit the draft; cancel or save it before using workbench navigation. The footer always describes the current context. In Connections, [ focuses SENDER in the sidebar and ] focuses RECIPIENT. Tab or Shift+Tab switches between them; Up/Down changes only the focused identity. Its label is purple and shows the arrow hint. Focus changes preserve both selections and permissions. h/l or Alt+Left/Right also chooses a recipient. Left/Right still changes views.

Search results show titles, IDs, projects and providers. Enter opens a workspace-owned native terminal; an external observation opens its details. Tab keeps you in the current workbench view and changes its selected session.

Use Ctrl+K when unsure what to press. Actions opens the appropriate editor or review, with the target and unavailable reasons shown before a change. Tasks for selected session clears previous task filters and opens that recipient's retained history. Attention enables the attention view; the ! shortcut toggles it.

Open the web control center with:

amx web -s daily --open

The web sidebar selects a session; the main tabs expose its controls and the workspace's records. Board filters communication, Connections controls relationships, Memory edits shared knowledge, and Tasks shows deliveries and outcomes. Session detail exposes role, native delivery and capacity. Groups & teams distinguishes owner groups from consented teams. Research appears when observing a research attempt. Focus in tmux returns native work to the terminal. The web owner view can inspect records that an individual participant is not authorized to read.

For project folders, shell splits, multiple agents in one tmux window and amx a reattachment, see terminal workflow.

docs.title: Everyday sessions
docs.text:
Start from an existing project directory, with Claude Code and Codex logged in:

amx up -s daily -p "$PWD" -d
amx name claude "Fix login redirect" -s daily
amx name codex "Review authentication changes" -s daily
amx a -s daily

The default coding workspace starts native Claude and Codex sessions. Select one and press Enter, then use its normal prompt, tools, approvals, skills and MCPs. F1 returns to the workbench. Peer collaboration and automatic delivery start off.

Add a new conversation for a new problem, without disturbing the others:

amx new billing --harness claude -p /path/to/billing \
  --title "Investigate retry failures" -s daily
amx new --harness codex -p /path/to/api \
  --title "Review cache invalidation" -s daily
amx ls -s daily

Omitting the name generates a stable ID. Copy that ID from the output for later commands. Shift+N is the quick terminal flow and inherits the selected provider and project. Its review also shows the provider-default model and trusted local host execution; model overrides and sandboxes are not copied. A title identifies the human task; a role supplies agent instructions and grants no permissions.

One workspace can hold unrelated projects. Two terminal windows can each run amx a SESSION_ID -s daily: they have independent navigation and drafts while sharing the underlying native conversations. Ctrl+W switches workspaces from an owned attachment and preserves its previous dashboard. Switching workspaces does not connect their brokers or share their data.

docs.title: Bring in a session started elsewhere
docs.text:
amx ls -s daily
amx connect OBSERVATION_ID --title "Existing API investigation" -s daily

Choose an observed terminal ID from the inventory, then paste the printed helper setup into that original conversation. Discovery does not read prompts or send input. Registration prepares coordination; it does not prove the agent has read the setup. External terminals stay in their original window and use a manual bridge rather than receiving a retrofitted native delivery adapter. Some wrapper processes cannot be discovered reliably; use amx new for those cases.

The easiest arrangement for several collaborating pairs is one coordination workspace containing those sessions or bridges. link takes IDs from that workspace; it is not a cross-workspace broker federation command.

docs.title: Choose harness and isolation
docs.text:
Session choice Setup path Claude Code or Codex Native local launch preserves the installed CLI's normal configuration and history Pi with a hosted provider Select the provider, model and authentication through managed setup Pi with Ollama or vLLM Configure the exact compatible endpoint and model; verify context and tool support Native Antigravity Use --harness antigravity --native-only; coordination remains manual A prompt-free native session --native-only omits Agentmux context and injected role; broker access can still be used manually An isolated worker or terminal Select Bubblewrap and explicitly provision the required dependencies and credentials

For local model endpoints, start with the Pi setup specification and endpoint setup guide. Edit the endpoint and exact model to match your server. A successful metadata preflight is not a successful tool or inference test. Sandbox configuration and native approvals are separate; choosing a local model does not provide isolation by itself.

docs.title: Temporary collaboration
docs.text:
Suppose api, api-review, poet and editor are registered session IDs:

amx link api api-review -s daily
amx link poet editor -s daily

Each exact member set gets a dedicated board and shared-memory namespace. Save the printed Group, Board and Memory values. The API pair does not gain access to the poem pair's scope. With several groups, target one explicitly:

amx board "The API proposal is ready." --group GROUP_ID -s daily
amx send api-review "Read the proposal when useful." --mode note -s daily

A board post is visible to that board's authorized readers. A direct note has explicit recipients. An everyone-readable board is possible when configured with that audience; linking a pair does not create a workspace-wide public board. A session belonging to two groups can carry information between them, so avoid overlapping membership when testing independent information boundaries. In web Board, choose Shared boards, select the exact board and click Search to apply that scope.

Use Connections → List view to search an exact pair when the graph is busy; the list pages 50 entries at a time and supports arrows and Enter. Inspect the direction shown in the controls before changing it. The graph offers an overview of effective permissions; permission explanations remain the authority.

Enabled session connections and enabled shared-access links automatically group connected nodes. Denied preview edges do not affect placement. Drag a node, or focus it and use Shift+Arrow, to pin its position. Pins persist in this browser for the selected workspace and study attempt, and stay in place when connections change. Other nodes arrange around the pins after you finish dragging. Auto arrange releases all pins and fits the new layout; Fit changes the viewport without releasing them. Selection, title changes and ordinary refreshes preserve the layout when the visible topology is unchanged. Placement never changes permissions. Direction arrows still identify sender and recipient; proximity does not establish that agents actually cooperated.

The graph shows at most 40 active sessions. Use the roster and paginated List view for larger workspaces. Automatic grouping and Auto arrange are also available in v0.12.0.

docs.title: Separate permission from delivery
docs.text:
Control What it allows What it does not imply Messages A note in the recipient's inbox A native turn will start Pings An authorized notification The receiver subscribes to pings Commands Creation of an instruction task in this direction Receiver approval, readiness or native execution Board or memory access Read or write the exact namespace Access to another scope or permission to command a peer Receiver Manual Human-led use and manual inbox reads Automatic native dispatch Receiver Review Approval of each exact eligible candidate Approval of every future message Receiver Auto Eligible turns within configured limits Unlimited turns or a hard provider billing cap

For example, to let poet request work from editor:

amx allow poet editor commands -s daily
amx mode editor review -s daily

Integrated Claude, Codex and Pi sessions support verified native delivery paths. The screenshot's command-only fixture correctly reports that it has no native adapter. Native Antigravity and external bridges retain manual coordination; use the Pi bridge for the supported Antigravity integration path. Consult the native delivery matrix for provider-specific limits.

Notes, pings, board changes and memory changes have separate subscriptions. Enabling a subscription never grants namespace access. Roles and boundary changes reach eligible Review/Auto receivers as attributed notices; an initial boundary synchronization can be the first pending candidate.

docs.title: End just the intended collaboration
docs.text:
amx mode editor manual -s daily
amx deny poet editor commands -s daily
amx unlink poet editor -s daily

unlink removes that exact group's contribution. Other groups or explicit grants may still allow communication. Make independent / amx isolate editor revokes that session's peer coordination more broadly and leaves native input running. Isolation also permanently removes consented memberships and dissolves teams that session owns, affecting their other members; review the listed effects. Cancel already accepted tasks separately. Previously received context remains known.

docs.title: Write a poem together
docs.text:
This example uses two ordinary native sessions and owner-reviewed delivery. Choose a fresh workspace name and run from an existing project directory:

amx up -s poem-guide -p "$PWD" -d
amx name codex "Poem: writer and editor" -s poem-guide
amx name claude "Poem: second stanza" -s poem-guide
amx link codex claude -s poem-guide
amx allow codex claude commands -s poem-guide
amx mode claude review --max-turns 6 --max-hops 4 -s poem-guide
amx mode codex review --max-turns 6 --max-hops 4 -s poem-guide
amx a codex -s poem-guide
  1. In Codex, enter: “Use your authenticated Agentmux tools to collaborate with Claude on a poem called The Second Cup. Write an opening stanza about an evening window and rain. Post the draft to our shared board, then use instruct to ask agent claude for an original four-line second stanza. Keep attribution. Assemble the poem after its result arrives.”
  2. Press F1. In 2 Sessions, select Claude, use Shift+A to read the exact pending candidate and review its approval. Approve the intended instruction; a boundary notice may appear first. Web Session detail offers the same inbox review. Commands alone would leave this waiting in Review mode.
  3. Enter Claude's native terminal to watch or interact. The adapter starts an attributed peer turn when ready; it does not insert tmux keystrokes or send your unsent draft. Tasks should advance beyond pending once the native transport accepts it.
  4. When Claude settles, review the correlated result notice for Codex too. Results are subscribed by default, but Codex's Review mode still requires approval. Return to Codex to see it assemble the poem. The result does not grant Claude permission to command Codex.
  5. Inspect the board, the task's result and both native conversations. A transport receipt alone is not the finished poem or owner verification of its quality.

From a separate owner shell, amx mode claude -j -s poem-guide lists status and pending candidates. After reading one, approve its exact ID with amx mode claude --approve CANDIDATE_ID -s poem-guide. Repeat for Codex's result candidate. If you prefer automatic eligible deliveries after trying Review, explicitly change both receivers to Auto with suitable finite limits.

When finished, set both receivers to Manual and unlink the pair. Both native conversations remain available. amx down -s poem-guide instead stops the workspace's owned processes and retains their saved data.

docs.title: Private and shared memory
docs.text:
Private memory belongs to one authenticated agent. Shared memory belongs to an explicit namespace with separate read/write access. Neither is an automatic copy of a native transcript. Linking sessions gives them a shared scope; they still need to write useful entries and read them through their tools.

In the web app, select the session, open Memory, choose the group's namespace, then Load and select a key. Review its value and version before saving. In the terminal, 4 Memory exposes shared boundaries and o opens the selected scope. Value-only edits of live entries preserve metadata and expiry; conflicting edits retain the draft until you explicitly review the latest version.

A useful handoff is a short agreed-plan entry containing decisions, remaining checks and artifact locations. Ask the agents to cite the source messages or tasks when writing it. Agents use namespace private with their own credential for personal notes. The owner's private namespace is separate from theirs.

Who received context? shows retained authenticated retrieval evidence. It records which version was returned, not understanding or use. TTL, deletion, export/import, provenance and optional semantic search are described in memory lifecycle. Removing access does not erase a copy already received in a native conversation.

docs.title: Read the evidence
docs.text:
Surface What it establishes Native terminal The provider conversation you can directly read, steer or interrupt Board and replies Broker-visible content, authors, audiences and reply ancestry Connections Current effective permissions and their sources, rather than what an agent remembers Tasks and attention Recorded delivery, results, failures, approvals and uncertainty Memory and exposure Explicit stored versions and authenticated retrieval receipts Groups, teams and capacity Membership, pending consent, parentage, effective access and remaining admissions Research and archives Protocol state, phase controls, population, interventions and retained study evidence

These views do not reveal hidden model reasoning or all provider-side activity. The graph describes permissions, not a claim that two agents cooperated. Task settlement is distinct from owner verification, and a retrieved memory is distinct from understanding it. For configured managed turns, trace inspection adds adapter-visible execution evidence; it is not a complete recording of everything a model or remote service did.

docs.title: Open the exact task before recovery
docs.text:
v0.13.0 prints a copyable open command after amx task TASK_ID:

amx task TASK_ID --open -s daily

The view reads that exact record, including older tasks and retired recipients; it never substitutes a newer task that mentions the ID. Inspect the instruction, result and delivery evidence. Ctrl+K exposes available recovery actions; each action reviews the exact task/version before confirmation. Opening the view does not retry or resolve anything. Check the prior process and side effects before choosing retry.

In terminal or web Actions, Tasks for selected session goes directly to a recipient's retained history. Web attention rows also have Inspect tasks, including historical recipients outside the active roster. Reading history changes no recovery decision.

docs.title: Managed and autonomous work
docs.text:
Choose native interactive sessions when you want to type throughout the day. Choose managed workers for queued task turns, persistent managed conversations and bounded wakeups. Managed worker output is observable, but it is not an always-open provider TUI. These modes can share the same broker and policy.

Use the setup wizard to review a role preset before launching:

amx managed setup --preset reviewer-pair --session review-team \
  --output review-team.yaml
amx start --config review-team.yaml -s review-team -d
amx ls -s review-team
amx send TARGET_ID "Review the implementation and report specific findings." \
  --mode instruction -s review-team

Replace TARGET_ID with the registered ID shown by setup or ls. The research-team role preset is a coordinator/analyst/critic starting point, not an experimental design. Presets do not automatically enable wakeups, spawning or permission to form teams.

For ongoing autonomy, explicitly configure conversation persistence, permitted command edges, and wake subscriptions to selected boards, notes or pings. Set finite turn, hop, backlog, concurrency and runtime limits. A message-triggered observation is attributed data, not a new owner instruction. See persistent workflows for the configuration.

Observe Tasks for complete retained counts, attention filters, exact recipients, results and adapter evidence. Search or load older pages rather than assuming the visible rows are the complete history. Human-only native turns are not broker tasks. A paused worker stops future launches; inspect or cancel an already running task separately.

docs.title: Dynamic teams and recruitment
docs.text:
Two mechanisms serve different purposes:

Mechanism Who decides membership Use it for Owner collaboration group You select the exact session IDs with link Effortless temporary pairs or owner-arranged teams Consented agent team An authorized creator invites; each participant accepts Agent self-organization and observable team formation

Teams are off unless configured. Joining creates access to that team's board and current shared memory, not permission to instruct its members. Pending invitations grant no access. Since-join board history is the default; current memory can include material written before a participant joined.

From a source checkout, start this finite, model-free fixture to try the team operations below. It uses an isolated broker, isolated workers lead and peer, and a permitted helper template. Working Linux Bubblewrap is required:

./bin/amx managed up examples/managed/bounded-teams.yaml \
  --state /tmp/amx-team-demo --broker-sandbox bubblewrap
./bin/amx dashboard --state /tmp/amx-team-demo

The owner can create a team and invite participants:

amx team create "API investigation" --state /tmp/amx-team-demo
amx team invite TEAM_ID lead --state /tmp/amx-team-demo
amx team invite TEAM_ID peer --state /tmp/amx-team-demo

Replace TEAM_ID with the ID returned by team create. Each participant separately consents through its own tools and credential. The owner console does not accept invitations on an agent's behalf. Teams can be renamed, dissolved, or transferred through a proposal plus the new owner's acceptance. An invited non-owner member can consent to an atomic move between teams. Reviews retain exact IDs and versions.

Recruitment is another explicit permission. An agent can request only approved spawn templates and delegate a bounded subset of its own rights. Children get new identities and isolated workspaces; parent, depth and remaining capacity stay visible. A role called “leader” cannot grant itself these powers.

The fixture's command agents do not independently recruit or accept invitations. Follow dynamic teams and bounded spawning for the authenticated spawn/invite/join calls or replace the fixtures with provisioned model harnesses. The ordinary indefinite interactive preset disables delegated spawning; use an explicit finite managed configuration for this workflow.

docs.title: Research and competition
docs.text: Use the research runner to study how behavior changes under information, incentives, team permission and population policies. It supplies private observations, phase barriers and objective mechanics for public-goods-v1 and trust-exchange-v1.

docs.title: Inspect the protocol before using models
docs.text:
From the source checkout, with supported Linux Bubblewrap and Python 3:

amx research plan examples/research/public-goods.yaml
amx research run examples/research/public-goods.yaml \
  --output /tmp/amx-study-demo --start-paused

Choose a new output path. plan starts no participants and reports the matrix and task count. This bundled run uses scripted command participants and makes no model calls. run stays in its terminal; observe it from another terminal:

amx research watch /tmp/amx-study-demo --follow
amx research study /tmp/amx-study-demo
# Use the exact STATE printed by the runner:
amx dashboard --state STATE --view research
amx web --state STATE --open

The bundled smoke has short deadlines, so prepare the observer terminal first. For slower exploration, make a separate manifest and team with explicitly larger trial, phase and runtime limits; use a new output path. Pausing does not extend any of those deadlines.

The research screenshots show a one-condition demo. The bundled public-goods smoke plans six trials across its conditions and seeds.

The console shows trial/condition, phase, admitted population, task outcomes, deadlines, runner heartbeat and requested versus acknowledged controls. Web Follow this study across trials tracks the next attempt. Terminal 8 Events contains research controls and study details. Overall study status and archived history remain inspectable after individual brokers stop.

Read the current control version before an intervention:

amx research status /tmp/amx-study-demo
amx research step /tmp/amx-study-demo --version CONTROL_VERSION \
  --reason "Inspect team formation after one phase"

Replace CONTROL_VERSION with result.research.control.version; read it again before another change. Step admits one phase. Pause and Stop take effect at phase barriers; already admitted work may finish. Resume releases a live pause, not a terminated runner. --start-paused pauses every new attempt; it also takes precedence over a carried unused step. Deadlines and budgets keep counting while paused.

docs.title: Design cooperation and competition comparisons
docs.text:
Treatment Relevant design choice Shared success versus individual incentives reward_mode: shared, individual or winner Available communication visibility: isolated, board or direct Permission to form private teams teams: true in a direct condition Voluntary team reward pooling team_rewards: pool; eligible members must independently choose the pool Role or behavioral prompt treatments Named role_assignments and personality_profiles Changing population through recruitment Explicit population.mode: dynamic and approved bounded templates

Use roles-personality.yaml to inspect a declared role/profile design, and dynamic-population.yaml for bounded recruitment. Dynamic children become research participants only at the next-round boundary with the required entry-credit transfer. Team formation and population growth are separate controls.

Hold the population, tools, models and other conditions constant when testing one factor, or declare a complete factorial design and balanced order. The public-goods smoke changes several factors to test mechanics; it cannot isolate their causal effects. Prompt profiles are treatments, not established personality traits. One trajectory cannot establish a stable cooperative or competitive characteristic.

For native model studies, provision a separate team, review the planned turn count, declare preregistration and a positive model-task budget, then explicitly use --allow-models. Supported limits count admissions or native tasks, not a hard external dollar cap. See research design and analysis.

The demo above exercises actual invitation, acceptance and namespace access. Its Alice/Bob coalition is scripted; measuring model self-organization requires model participants making those decisions themselves under the declared policy.

docs.title: Observe freely and record steering
docs.text:
Read-only inspection does not mark a trial assisted. Phase controls and owner changes to messages, memory, permissions, teams or tasks are recorded as interventions. Default estimates exclude those assisted runs. You can still interact deliberately; keep that exploratory trajectory distinct from an unassisted comparison.

amx research history /tmp/amx-study-demo --type team.join --limit 100
amx research analyze /tmp/amx-study-demo \
  --csv /tmp/amx-study-summary.csv \
  --behavior-csv /tmp/amx-study-behavior.csv

Use new CSV paths. The private archive preserves messages, membership changes, tasks, memory and retrieval evidence. Behavior CSV exposes objective decision fields without raw prompts. Analysis reports incomplete blocks, invalid actions, execution failures and other quality limits. Repeated worlds, counterbalancing and adequate independent blocks matter more than an attractive single run.

docs.title: Scale and remote workers
docs.text:
For a busy workday, keep clear titles and project identities, use Ctrl+P or web search, and create small scopes instead of one everyone-to-everyone channel. Use Tasks attention filters and connection List view as the roster grows. Remove exited sessions deliberately; retire revoked IDs to release active definition slots while preserving attribution and history. amx archive ID is the short name for retirement; it does not stop an active session first.

Choose isolated profiles when filesystem boundaries matter. Trusted local sessions preserve normal host tools, skills and MCPs. Bubblewrap uses private homes, selected credentials and explicit dependencies; arbitrary host configuration is not inherited. An isolated broker can still communicate with separate agent sandboxes through its authenticated socket. Isolation failures do not fall back to trusted local execution.

Managed remote workers use explicit trusted Linux SSH placement:

amx managed remote --state STATE --agent WORKER_ID --host SSH_ALIAS \
  --remote-dir /tmp/amx-unique-remote-worker --once

Provision the remote harness, dependencies and selected credentials separately. The command forwards authenticated broker access, not the owner's credentials or source tree. It is not an automatic cluster scheduler or host-failure migration service. See SSH workers and broker scale.

Current validation includes larger registries and broker actor workloads; those are not measurements of hundreds of simultaneous native model sessions. Small teams remain the primary deployment target. Explicit concurrency, lifetime spawn/team, runtime and resource limits apply as you grow.

docs.title: Diagnose a stalled workflow
docs.text:
What you see Check next Commands allowed, nothing appears in the native CLI Receiver Manual/Review mode, pending approval, adapter support, readiness and limits in Session detail A note or ping stays in the inbox Its subscription and receiver mode; permission alone does not wake a session A task says submitted Inspect native settlement and its result; transport acceptance is not completion Delivery is uncertain or its lease expired Open amx task TASK_ID --open -s NAME, inspect the old process and task evidence, then review an exact fail/retry decision Unlinking leaves an edge allowed Inspect other active groups and explicit owner overrides A provider updated and exited Inspect final output; use Shift+U or amx relaunch ID with an explicit native resume choice Complete history is unavailable on an old controller The roster can remain usable with partial snapshots; use a fresh current workspace for full backend features Broker or runner health is unknown Inspect evidence and logs; a responsive broker does not prove a runner or model is active

Use the control center reference, optional verification walkthrough and trace and recovery guide for exact recovery steps. Closing an observer leaves work running. amx remove ID revokes and closes an owned session; removing an external bridge leaves its original terminal alone. amx down -s NAME stops the workspace's owned processes and retains saved data.

docs.title: Interactive work sessions
docs.text:
Start with amx start from your project directory after installing and logging in to Claude Code and Codex. It opens a workbench for the default workspace work; select a session and press Enter to type into its native CLI. F1 returns to the workbench. A workspace contains sessions and an owner coordination service (the broker).

For a coding request that runs through implementation, fresh reviews and checks without a persistent terminal workspace, use amx work. Its saved patch is applied explicitly. amx flow provides advanced comparisons, missions and handoffs; those runs do not join this workspace or inherit its permissions automatically.

Use interaction: interactive per agent for a native terminal; omit it for managed task execution. Both modes share the coordination broker and its permissions. Each agent has one terminal/worker lock. Changing interaction mode requires a new launch definition/run rather than a second process sharing a conversation.

v0.15.0 includes amx context, amx task / tasks, exact task opening with task ID --open, amx observe, the searchable running-workspace chooser and direct session task history in Actions. See installation and explicitly upgrade an older workspace controller before using its new controls.

docs.title: Inspect running work
docs.text:
amx observe --session work
amx observe --session work --watch --json
amx task TASK_ID --open --session work

The operational view separates broker availability, ownership-checked worker panes, live leases, worker check-ins, native event metadata and adapter readiness. Counts include all retained tasks; bounded attention keeps old failures and uncertain attempts visible. Silence alone leaves model progress unknown. Use the printed exact task command for results, native receipts, traces and reviewed recovery. See observability for freshness, JSONL, partial observations and the separate evidence used by coding runs and research.

docs.title: Recognize sessions throughout the day
docs.text:
Use a task title such as “Fix login redirect” to recognize a conversation. Titles are editable and may repeat; the permanent session ID remains visible and is used for every attach, message, permission and collaboration operation.

amx add --harness claude --project ~/projects/api --title "Fix login redirect"
# The command prints a generated stable ID; choosing a name is optional.
amx label SESSION_ID "Investigate expired login cookie"
amx label SESSION_ID ""  # Clear the title without changing the session.
amx sessions

The workbench and web app show title, project, provider and ID. Session details also distinguish workspace sessions from connected external terminals and show creation/start times and tmux/TTY locations when available. Untitled sessions use a project/provider fallback. No task description is inferred from prompts or transcripts. Two sessions with the same title remain separate identities.

In the terminal press Ctrl+P (or /) to find a session by task, project, provider, ID or terminal location. Enter opens the exact native terminal; Tab selects it in the workbench; Esc cancels. Discovered terminals open details for their original terminal instead. L edits the selected task title. N asks for an optional title and reviews a new generated ID using the selected session's provider, project and coordinated/native-only choice. In the web app use Find a session, Rename, and Sessions. Titles are labels, not role instructions; editing one never restarts the native conversation. When adding a session, --harness selects Claude Code, Codex, Pi or prompt-free native Antigravity; --title labels the human task, while --role supplies optional instructions to the agent at launch.

For a pristine native launch, use amx add --harness claude --native-only. This appends no Agentmux prompt or role and preserves the native CLI's local configuration. Broker credentials remain available for coordination you request manually; listing/attaching works normally. It cannot be combined with --role. Native Antigravity is available with --harness antigravity --native-only; its direct CLI does not expose a verified appended-system-role interface. Use the Pi bridge when you want injected Agentmux context with that provider.

Change a coordinated session's role with amx role SESSION_ID "New role", or press V in the terminal workbench. The role editor uses version checking and preserves a failed draft. Ctrl-R reviews the latest role; Enter adopts only the reviewed version before a separate save. Managed workers capture the current role when claiming the next task. Native conversations stay running and receive an informational inbox notice; managed call identity returns the current role and role_version. Manual mode leaves it in the broker inbox; Review/Auto can deliver an attributed role/boundary notice through the native adapter. Roles grant no broker permissions. In the quick N flow, Ctrl+O opens advanced provider, project, coordinated/native-only and role settings; Actions also exposes Advanced new session. The quick review explicitly shows the provider-default model and trusted local host execution. It does not copy an existing model override or sandbox; use explicit CLI launch flags for those choices.

Name or ID Where to use it Workspace name, such as work --session work selects the team and saved state Registered session ID, such as claude or an ID printed by add/connect attach, send, label, role, relaunch, collaborate, isolate, remove Observed terminal ID from sessions connect registers that live external terminal Group ID printed by collaborate board --group ID selects its shared board

Provider-native conversation IDs belong to the provider's own history UI; they are not Agentmux session IDs. Uppercase placeholders in examples below must be replaced with the IDs or paths from your own workspace.

docs.title: Start and attach
docs.text:
With Claude Code and Codex installed and logged in:

amx start --project /path/to/project
# In another terminal:
amx attach claude
amx attach codex
amx dashboard
amx web --open

start --detach starts without attachment. Commands accept --session NAME or --state DIRECTORY. Inside an owned tmux attachment, an omitted selector uses that verified workspace; outside, ordinary commands default to work. start always defaults to work when no selector is given. These are alternative selectors for existing workspaces: supplying both is rejected. start may combine them to name a workspace stored in a custom directory. Do not reuse a saved session for a different project or definition. down stops owned agents and broker in order, retaining their data. Detaching or closing a dashboard leaves them running. Running the same start command again, including --config FILE, attaches to the running workspace only if the configuration still matches its saved definition. Each attachment has its own dashboard process, selection and drafts. Only the underlying agent terminals are shared; attaching twice to the same agent still shows the same native conversation. Runtime service windows stay out of normal navigation. Ctrl-b, release, then Shift+D opens read-only service logs. An explicit --sandbox must also match the running broker's mode; reopening never changes that mode. A mismatch is rejected without restarting the workspace. Use managed restart --state DIRECTORY for explicit whole-workspace restart.

Use amx relaunch AGENT_ID to restart one exited workspace-owned native session under the same ID while its healthy peers keep their processes. It starts a fresh native conversation by default. --resume picker, --resume last or --resume NATIVE_ID makes the native history choice explicit; it does not renew deadlines or revive revoked identities. The dashboard offers the same flow with U. A controller started before this feature needs one explicit workspace restart after upgrading; it is never silently replaced. Antigravity accepts --resume last or an explicit conversation ID; it has no picker mapping. External bridges, revoked agents and still-running native CLIs cannot be relaunched through this command.

Native updates may exit successfully and ask you to restart. Agentmux retains the final output and marks that CLI exited; it never restarts it automatically. New trusted-local interactive setups save the selected public launcher, so a normal symlink-based native update is used on the next explicit relaunch. Managed and sandboxed definitions retain their frozen executable dependencies. If an older local definition directly invokes a removed or outdated native binary, select its installed public launcher for this one invocation:

amx relaunch codex --native-launcher "$(command -v codex)"

This requires an updated running controller and an absolute executable path. It applies only to trusted-local interactive sessions, preserves trailing arguments, and does not rewrite the saved definition or change sandbox mounts. It does not repair interpreter-plus-script definitions such as node /old/package/cli.js: their script argument is preserved too. Review those definitions explicitly, or create a new session with the updated setup. An older controller rejects this option with upgrade guidance; it is never silently ignored. Add the workspace's --session NAME or --state DIR selector when it is not the default workspace.

amx workspaces lists named workspaces and remembered custom state paths. Use --json for structured inventory or --register DIR to add an older custom location. Ctrl+W (also Shift+W) opens the workspace chooser. From an interactive attachment, Enter hands off to that workspace while preserving the previous workbench and drafts. A standalone observer shows an exact attach command when native input needs a different tmux server. The web Sessions view lists workspace commands. Identical names remain distinct by state path. A failed or exhausted live check reports unknown instead of inventing a stopped process; opening an unknown workspace attempts observation without starting agents.

The current directory does not select a workspace for later commands. Outside an owned attachment, if you used start --session api, keep using --session api, including on add, sessions, connect, attach, web and down. For a second workspace:

amx start --session billing --project /path/to/billing
# Later, from any directory:
amx attach codex --session billing
amx dashboard --session billing

amx context --session billing explains the target, selection source and runtime status without attaching or starting agents. Bare amx / amx a outside an attachment uses a sole running workspace or offers a running-workspace chooser. In that chooser, / or Ctrl+F starts a name/path/status filter, arrows or Ctrl+N/P choose a result, Ctrl+U clears and Enter opens its exact state path. This selection does not change the default for later ID-based commands in an unrelated shell.

If start reports a different saved project, use attach --session NAME to reopen that workspace, or choose a fresh name for the new project. If you only detached, attach again; no restart is needed. After down, running the original start command launches the saved definition again. Choose prior conversations through each provider's native history controls; relaunching does not promise automatic conversation resumption. See recovery for broker/task uncertainty and upgrades.

For project directories, shell splits, multiple agents in one tmux window, normal tmux keys and last-session reattachment, see terminal folders and layouts. Tab switches sidebar/content focus; ↑/↓ navigates that focused area and ←/→ changes views. In Connections, [ focuses Sender and ] focuses Recipient directly. Tab or Shift+Tab switches between them. Up/Down changes only the focused identity; changing focus preserves the other selection and never changes permissions.

Tasks in both consoles browse complete retained broker history. In the terminal, PgDn loads older records, PgUp returns toward newer records and f searches instructions, results or IDs; an empty search clears the filter. Web Tasks offers search, recipient/state filters and Load older. These pages do not include human turns typed only into a native provider's own conversation UI.

Direct CLI inspection is also available:

amx tasks --to codex --query "login" --limit 25 --session billing
amx task TASK_ID --session billing
amx task TASK_ID --open --session billing

tasks pages retained history newest first; its More command preserves the workspace and filters. task --open loads the exact task directly, even when it is older than the first page or its recipient is retired. It shows the current task/version, instruction, result and delivery/recovery evidence. Ctrl+K opens recovery actions when available; confirmation keeps the exact task/version. Opening never retries, resolves, cancels or approves a task. Terminal/web Actions offers Tasks for selected session to reset old filters and open that recipient's history. Web attention rows also offer Inspect tasks.

The coding preset preserves the normal local Claude/Codex environment, tools, skills, MCP configuration, native approval prompts, login and history. It does not enable Claude safe mode or suppress Pi customizations. Codex keeps the native sandbox policy from your configuration. This is trusted host execution: broker ACLs control coordination APIs, but do not isolate local files or same-user credentials. Choose a sandbox when those boundaries are required.

start --sandbox bubblewrap uses selected credential snapshots, private homes, separate native history, and an isolated broker. It cannot transparently inherit arbitrary host skills/MCPs or their filesystem/network authority. Codex then explicitly relies on the outer sandbox, while retaining native approvals. No host policy is changed. A sandbox failure never falls back to local execution.

The preset creates the team/project namespaces with no agent access, denies peer coordination, and disables automatic wakeups. It sets interactive_workspace: true, so ordinary native terminals run until you close them instead of expiring after a workday. This mode requires every initial agent to be interactive and delegated spawning disabled. Managed automation/research retains positive runtime budgets and durable deadlines. An explicit existing deadline is still honored. Saved configurations are never silently migrated. The controller is always checksum-pinned outside writable projects before launch, including projects added later.

amx add backend --harness claude --project ~/projects/backend
amx add review --harness codex --project ~/projects/frontend --role "Review changes"
amx collaborate backend review
amx board "Use the group's API proposal as context."
amx isolate review
amx remove backend

One workspace can contain sessions from unrelated projects. add starts another native session with a stable name/ID, normal local configuration by default, and no peer authority. remove closes its owned terminal and revokes its bridge, retaining native history. Names are not silently reused for different identities. For an isolated addition use --sandbox bubblewrap; Pi also requires an explicit --auth-file and --auth-provider. Dynamic additions require an owner broker able to inspect the selected host project and authentication boundaries. An isolated broker fails closed when those paths are unavailable; configure such teams before launch instead of exposing host paths to the broker.

collaborate A B enables notes/pings and creates a dedicated owner-managed group with its own board and memory. The exact member set reuses its stable group and history after reconnect/restart. Other groups do not gain access. A notes-only group contributes no command authority; pre-existing configuration or explicit owner command grants still apply. Inspect effective Connections permissions. board selects the only active group automatically; with multiple groups use --group ID or --board NAMESPACE. isolate A revokes both directions of peer coordination, shared scopes and group membership, and fences future delegated spawning/team formation. It leaves native input running. It does not cancel already accepted tasks or erase previous context. These owner-managed groups are distinct from consent-based agent-created research teams; neither operation bypasses those teams' membership rules.

For several independent groups, save the Group, Board, and Memory values printed by each collaborate call. The web app lists them in Groups & teams → Owner collaboration groups; select the exact board in the Board view or the exact memory namespace in Memory.

# Assume api, api-review, billing and billing-review are registered IDs.
amx collaborate api api-review
amx collaborate billing billing-review
# Replace GROUP_ID with the first command's printed Group value:
amx board "API proposal ready for review" --group GROUP_ID

Repeating collaborate with the same complete member set reuses its group and restores current membership in its retained history; explicit owner scope denies remain effective until reset. A different member set creates another group. A session in two groups can read both authorized contexts; it can carry that information between them. isolate api-review removes that session from all its groups and revokes peer coordination in both directions, not just the board currently displayed. It leaves other members running.

Collaboration groups contribute permissions independently. Disabling one group removes its note/ping/optional command contribution and its own scoped access; another active overlapping group keeps its grants. Explicit owner edge/scope overrides take precedence, including denies. Notes-only does not revoke a configured command relationship. Connections shows each effective grant's source; Memory distinguishes stored owner intent from effective read/write permission.

Isolation adds labeled suspension overlays without overwriting existing owner intent. Reconnecting selected sessions removes their pair's isolation overlays, restores their configured static scope intent, and rejoins the selected group. Unrelated isolated relationships remain blocked. Explicit denies survive reconnect. Use Connections M/P/I or Memory R to reset an exact override to underlying policy. Already-read knowledge and accepted tasks are never erased.

Older saved groups have no contribution version and require an explicit migration choice before a group edit; no changes are made by default. Review the historical pair grants, then choose --legacy-policy preserve to keep them as direct owner intent, or --legacy-policy group to remove untagged pair allows while retaining all denies and unrelated controls. Connections c provides an explicit 1/2 review for a legacy pair; larger groups can use the CLI or web. A reviewed/new group contributes permissions independently. See live permissions and resource controls for exact migration and reset semantics.

Each attach opens an independent tmux client view. You can keep Claude in one terminal window and Codex in another; switching one does not move the other. Detaching removes that view, not the agent. Session IDs remain distinct from the workspace name, tmux panes, and provider-native conversation IDs.

To review/edit a configured team before launch:

amx managed setup --preset coding --output team.yaml
amx start --config team.yaml --session my-team

For an idle managed review team, select --preset reviewer-pair; for coordinator, analyst and critic roles select --preset research-team. These preserve explicit authentication and sandbox choices, provide a shared board/memory, and queue no initial tasks. They do not enable automatic wakeups, spawning or dynamic-team authority. Use the research runner for a bounded experimental study and its preregistration/analysis rather than treating a role preset as a research design.

docs.title: Existing sessions
docs.text:
These commands use an already running Agentmux workspace. If you have none, start one first with amx start --detach. The independently started native terminal remains in its original window throughout discovery and connection.

amx sessions
amx connect OBSERVATION_ID --title "Review login changes"
# Optional: --name existing-review chooses the stable ID explicitly.

Discovery inspects current-user live TTY process names and the default tmux server. It reads no prompts, transcripts, command arguments, target environments or authentication files. Observation IDs include process lifetime identity so PID reuse does not attach an old identity to a new process. Generic node wrappers, non-TTY clients and some platform metadata cannot be identified reliably.

Connecting prepares a private per-agent helper and prints a short setup to paste into the existing native conversation. There is no automatic input injection, restart, model request or claim that the agent consumed the setup. The helper pins its assigned credential and broker socket; it cannot act as the owner. The session can then read permissions/inbox and use authorized coordination tools through its normal shell capability. Native tool access must permit that helper path.

A bridge does not retrofit process/filesystem isolation into an existing terminal. Disconnecting it revokes broker access and leaves the external process alone. Use amx remove REGISTERED_ID to disconnect that bridge; isolate keeps the bridge available but disables its peer collaboration. attach cannot move an external session into the workspace; return to its original terminal. Transport failures never trigger automatic registration retries. Explicit reconnect with the same name safely recovers an uncertain registration and preserves identity. If an observation is no longer live, run sessions again and select the new observation; an exited process cannot be reconnected by its old observation ID. If a terminal is absent from discovery, use add for a new supported native session instead of guessing an ID.

Without --project, preset setup creates separate workspaces. JSON setup specs accept interaction and optional workdir per agent. Pi interactive sessions support configured compatible endpoints and selected authentication. Native Antigravity is available with --native-only; use its Pi bridge for injected coordination context. See provider compatibility for supported routes and separate startup, inference and tool checks.

docs.title: Terminal dashboard
docs.text:
Keys are case-sensitive: N, L, V, and P mean Shift plus that letter. For Ctrl-b b, press Ctrl-b, release both keys, then press b. The same two-step prefix applies to the other Ctrl-b bindings. Shortcuts below depend on the active view and selected record; the footer shows the actions available there. Use Left/Right or a view number to switch between all eight views. Tab changes sidebar/content focus. Up/Down navigates the focused area. In Connections, [ focuses the sender and ] focuses the recipient; only the focused identity shows the arrow hint and purple highlight. Connections and Teams use h/l or Alt-Left/Alt-Right for their recipient/target. Below 100 columns, the terminal labels Connections as Links and Existing terminals as Existing; their view numbers and controls stay the same. In an editor, printable characters are text; use Ctrl-G for help and Esc to cancel before using navigation shortcuts.

Key Action ↑/↓ or j/k Navigate the focused sidebar or content Enter Open the focused native terminal or content reader; an exited native CLI opens a same-ID relaunch review. Outside tmux, open an independent attachment Ctrl+P or / Find by task, project, provider, ID or terminal location; Enter opens native, Tab selects here, Esc cancels Shift+L Edit the selected session's human task title; empty clears Shift+V Edit its coordinated role with CAS; prompt-free native sessions reject injected roles Ctrl+K Search and invoke Actions with exact targets and unavailable reasons Shift+N Quick new session using selected provider/project/profile; optional title, then review model default and host execution; Ctrl+O opens advanced settings Ctrl+W / Shift+W Choose another workspace; an attachment hands off interactively and retains prior drafts Shift+U Deliberately relaunch the selected exited owned native session ? / Ctrl-G Open context help outside an editor / while editing or reviewing F1 / Ctrl-b g in a native session Return to the workbench Ctrl-b, then b / Shift+P / m / t in a native session Open Board / Connections / Memory / Tasks in a popup Ctrl-b, then Shift+D Choose read-only Broker or Supervisor logs without leaving the current terminal Tab / Shift-Tab Focus sidebar or content 1–8 Select Board, Sessions, Connections, Memory, Tasks, Existing terminals, Teams, Events ←/→ or Ctrl+←/→ in every view Switch views; editors, readers and reviews keep their own arrow keys [ / ] in Teams; h/l or Alt+←/→ Choose a team; choose an exact agent for a membership action i / r / d in Teams Review invite / remove or revoke invitation / dissolve with the current version; hints follow target membership e / t in Teams Edit team name/mission / propose the selected member as owner; acceptance is separate b / v in Teams Compose to its board / inspect its shared memory as owner [ / ] in Events; Home Inspect an event; return to following the newest event PgDn / PgUp / Shift+F in Board or Events Page older / newer retained broker history / search within its scope g in Events Toggle all events versus the selected session's events P / R / S / T in Events Research pause / resume / one phase / stop, each with a reason and separate review x Revoke the selected session and descendants after review; owned shutdown is requested s / b Compose a direct message/instruction or selected shared-board note + / − in Board Select an allowed board namespace Enter / Esc in composer Submit / cancel; Alt-Enter inserts a newline Ctrl-T in a direct-message/reply composer Switch the frozen draft's note/instruction intent without changing its text or recipient ←/→ / Home / End in composer Edit the draft without changing its recipient f in Board Filter all coordination, team board, or selected agent inbox [ / ] then r in Board Select a message and reply h/l or Alt+←/→ in Connections Select the recipient for the selected sender [ / ] in Connections Focus sender / recipient, then Up/Down chooses that identity; focus changes preserve both selections and permissions c / d in Connections Connect selected sender/recipient in a group / make sender independent c in Existing terminals Prepare a bridge for the selected observed terminal; paste setup manually m / p / i in Connections Toggle messages / pings / commands Shift+M / Shift+P / Shift+I in Connections Reset the selected explicit override to the underlying effective policy [ / ] in Memory Select a board or memory namespace r / w in Memory Toggle read / write Shift+R in Memory Reset the selected explicit scope override; membership remains authoritative v in Memory Inspect shared entries; [ / ] selects an entry e / n in memory entries Edit an existing entry / create a key and value [ / ] in Tasks Select a task in the loaded history page PgDn / PgUp / f in Tasks Load older / newer history pages / search all task instructions, results or IDs y / z in Tasks Toggle recipient / cycle state;
