an explicit filter leaves a CLI-opened exact-task view r / c in Tasks Follow up / cancel o in Board, Sessions, Memory, Tasks, Existing terminals, Teams or Events Open the selected loaded content in a frozen, read-only reader ↑/↓ or j/k in the reader Scroll one line PgUp / PgDn; Home / End in the reader Scroll a page; jump to the start / end Esc / q / o in the reader Return to the previous view while keeping the observer open Ctrl-R outside a composer Restore the last failed message, board, memory, role or new-session draft for review Ctrl-R inside a memory/role editor Review the latest saved value/version alongside the retained draft; adopting a version does not save Shift+B in Board or Sessions Review four agent admission-budget fields, then confirm with the current resource version a Pause/resume configured autonomy; does not stop in-flight work q Detach from the persistent workbench, or close a popup/standalone view; team stays running

The Teams view is for consent-based teams created by permitted agents. An empty Teams view does not mean your native sessions are missing. For everyday pairing, press 3 for Connections, choose a recipient with h/l or Alt+←/→, then c. Those owner collaboration groups share a scoped board and memory.

The roster keeps process state visible even with long project names. A native CLI marked exited can still have an active coordination identity; it does not necessarily mean the CLI failed. Enter or Shift+U opens a deliberate relaunch review. Nothing restarts until you confirm; retained output is labeled as last output instead of live output.

Ctrl+W (also Shift+W) opens the workspace chooser even while a draft or review is open. An interactive amx attach hands off between tmux servers using its outer client; other attachments remain where they are, and returning restores the previous workbench and draft. A standalone observer instead shows an exact attach command for native input in another server.

Use o when a preview is too short. The reader keeps the selected record and its loaded text fixed while activity refreshes, so scrolling cannot switch to a different result. Tasks show the result first, followed by the instruction and provenance/reported trace. The Sessions view shows session details and a loaded terminal preview or unconfirmed external-bridge setup. Memory shows the selected entry, destination author and asserted source claims, or full boundary details; Existing terminals can show loaded bridge setup, and Teams/Events show full record details. Previously loaded content remains readable offline. The reader does not fetch older history; close and reopen it to read a refreshed record. Control and mutation keys are inactive while reading.

After a failed send/reply, board post, memory/role save or new-session setup, inspect current delivery/state before retrying: a lost response may follow a successful write. Close any newer composer with Esc, then press Ctrl-R to review the retained draft. It restores the original recipient, intent, reply reference or namespace/key; memory/role edits retain their original version check, and new-session drafts retain provider, project, prompt-free/coordinated profile and role. Nothing is sent automatically. Failed title edits are restored separately with L on their original session.

For a memory or role version conflict, press Ctrl-R inside that editor. This loads a frozen comparison of the current saved value/version and your retained draft. Enter in that reader adopts only the displayed version and returns to the editor; it does not save. Esc/q/o returns with the original version and draft. After reviewing or editing your draft, a separate Enter in the editor saves with the adopted version check. A later concurrent change still conflicts. Offline or failed reviews retain the draft without adopting a new version.

Human input goes directly to the native CLI, including its normal approval prompts. Broker messages do not inject keystrokes or impersonate user input. In the default Manual mode, ask an interactive agent to read its broker inbox. For integrated Claude, Codex and Pi sessions, choose Review or Auto in terminal Sessions or web Session detail, or use amx delivery ID review|auto to enable attributed native turns. Sender Commands permission and receiver delivery mode are separate. See native delivery for approvals, subscriptions, lifecycle evidence, limits and provider-specific capabilities.

amx send codex "Please read the proposed API on the team board."
amx board "Proposal: keep parsing and persistence separate."
amx inbox
amx reply TASK_OR_MESSAGE_ID "Please also check error handling."
amx reply MESSAGE_ID "A note, no task." --mode note
amx reply BOARD_MESSAGE_ID "For this board." --board BOARD_NAMESPACE
amx reply BOARD_MESSAGE_ID "Private follow-up." --to codex --mode note

send/reply default to --mode auto: a note for interactive agents and an instruction task for managed workers. Choose --mode note for information or --mode instruction for a task explicitly. An instruction to a native terminal stays queued in Manual mode; Review/Auto can deliver it through the native adapter. Both forms print the record ID. They never automatically retry writes; a transport failure can leave delivery uncertain. The lower-level managed call API exposes explicit request IDs for durable retries.

reply accepts direct messages and tasks. Messages and instruction tasks retain broker-validated reply_to and a stable thread_id instead of changing the text to simulate ancestry. A shared board post has several possible audiences, so choose reply ID "Follow-up" --board NAMESPACE to retain the same board, or reply ID "Follow-up" --to AGENT_ID for a private follow-up to an existing reader. Reply references cannot widen a private conversation or move a thread to a different board. Every direct recipient must already be able to read the referenced message; replies grant no history access. To share something with a new audience, compose a new message explicitly rather than attaching a private reference. Board replies are informational notes, never instruction tasks. Empty replies are rejected before creating any message or task.

docs.title: Web app
docs.text:
amx web --open opens a local full-screen app; without --open, it prints a private link. --port NUMBER selects a loopback port; by default one is allocated. Ctrl-C stops the web process independently of the team. Never give its private owner link to agents.

The app offers agent selection, read-only terminal previews, recent messages, follow-ups with explicit intent, searchable retained message/event/task history, cancellation, shared-memory inspection and versioned editing, role/profile setup, autonomy and admission controls, and the same live permission switches as the terminal dashboard. Board is the main focus pane. Connections shows directional message/ping/command connections and shared board/memory access; select a connection to adjust it. Since v0.13.0, enabled connections automatically group connected nodes. Denied preview edges do not affect arrangement. Dragging or Shift+Arrow pins a node; its position persists locally for that workspace and study attempt, including after topology changes. Unpinned nodes arrange around pins after a drag. Auto arrange releases pins and refits; Fit only adjusts the viewport. Ordinary refreshes, title changes and selection do not rearrange an unchanged visible topology. Arrangement does not write permissions or establish cooperation. Fit and zoom controls work by keyboard and on narrow screens; native terminal input remains in tmux. Spawned agents retain inherited delegation limits; live overlay edits currently apply to configured agents and owner-added native/bridged sessions. The graph displays at most 40 active agents, keeping selected identities visible; the roster reads every broker registry page. Recent activity snapshots are bounded to 40 records per category; Board, Events and Tasks separately search/page retained broker history. Actions opens the selected session's task history, and attention rows offer Inspect tasks for historical recipients too. Copy the attach command or focus an existing tmux window for native input. Terminal emulation remains in tmux.

No external scripts, fonts, services or analytics are loaded. APIs require a random bearer capability and validate Host/Origin. A restrictive content policy and text-only rendering protect the owner interface from agent-authored output. This is not a remote collaboration server.

docs.title: Live boundaries
docs.text:
Owner-only control.update overlays immutable launch configuration, with version checks, durable request receipts and audited events. Agents cannot edit controls or inspect another agent's permissions. Shared namespace edits cannot expose private memory or bypass team consent. Coordinated native sessions initially receive role, broker usage and effective-boundary context; --native-only appends none of that prompt. Managed workers fetch a fresh boundary snapshot and capture the current owner role at each task claim.

Agents query managed call boundaries.get; identity and inbox listings also report boundaries_version. Interactive models receive no automatic model turn or replacement system prompt after an owner edit. They must recheck live permissions before coordinating; broker enforcement applies regardless of stale context.

Removing instruction authority prevents new tasks; cancel accepted tasks separately. Removing read access stops future board/shared-memory reads but cannot remove information already present in history. Provider networking and project filesystem sharing are separate process boundaries.

From a workspace-native agent's shell, the authenticated bridge is:

"$AGENTMUX_CLI" managed call identity --json '{}'
"$AGENTMUX_CLI" managed call boundaries.get --json '{}'
"$AGENTMUX_CLI" managed call message.list --json '{}'
"$AGENTMUX_CLI" managed call task.list --json '{}'

The native process receives its own credential/socket through its environment; the agent should not print or locate credential contents. If the owner's native shell policy filters out the bridge variables, report that rather than searching owner state. These are agent-credential checks. The human's send, board and dashboard use owner authority, so a successful owner send does not prove a peer is permitted to send. Check the exact shared namespaces returned by boundaries.get or printed by collaborate; the coding preset's configured team and project names remain unshared until explicitly granted. After isolation, test future reads of the old explicit board/memory namespace: an unfiltered inbox may still contain the agent's own authored/direct receipts.

docs.title: Consented teams and capacity
docs.text:
Owner collaboration groups and consented dynamic teams have separate lifecycles. The coding preset leaves dynamic teams and spawning disabled. A configured managed team can enable and delegate them; amx team --help documents create/list, metadata edits, invitations, removal/dissolution, ownership proposals, participant acceptance and atomic invited moves. Team name/mission edits retain the same namespace identities. An ownership proposal changes no authority until the proposed owner accepts with its own credential. A participant move requires its pending destination invitation and both current team versions.

capacity.get {} and identity.capacity report the caller's remaining lifetime spawns/teams, depth, team slots, templates and admission reasons; the owner can inspect a selected agent. A snapshot reserves no capacity. Shift+B in Board/Sessions reviews the selected agent's four admission-budget fields; the web uses the same CAS broker rules. Lower-level owner capacity.update can edit complete agent or session admission-budget objects and shorten the admission deadline. It cannot refund permanently charged attempts, extend the original process deadline or change enforced launch resource caps. These are conservative broker admissions, not hard external provider billing limits. See live permissions and resources and dynamic teams.

docs.title: Limits and verification
docs.text:
Isolated native history is stored per agent. After restart, choose an exact prior conversation through the native UI; uncertain managed turns are never silently resumed. Credential snapshots are read-only: refresh externally, exit and deliberately relaunch the affected native session if its login needs renewal. Managed workers reload selected authentication between turns.

Interactive mode currently rejects managed conversation leases, automatic wakeups, structured turn traces, disk capsules and allowlist egress rather than skipping their guarantees. Bubblewrap host/none networking and process resource limits remain available. Managed workers retain existing hardening features. Native tool output in terminal/history is not a complete immutable broker trace.

Dashboards page the agent registry, retained message/event/task history and memory entries. Board/Event searches and pages are scoped at the broker before pagination. An older controller without those history APIs exposes only a labeled partial recent snapshot, never a complete search or older page. Retained broker history is not a native-provider transcript or an unlimited archive of external activity. The owner-added registry is limited to 200 definitions, and owner collaboration groups to 128 lifetime groups. Permission overlays are limited to 4,096 explicit edge/scope overrides. Switches edit configured and owner-managed agents/shared namespaces; dynamic children retain bounded inherited capabilities and dynamic teams retain consent operations.

python3 scripts/smoke-managed-interactive.py checks real tmux input/focus, two independent terminal clients, popup composition and detach/cleanup, isolated terminal fixtures and broker, message/input separation, live grant revocation/restoration and authenticated web controls. It makes no model calls. Native model behavior requires separate provider validation.

python3 scripts/smoke-managed-workspace.py exercises ten live model-free terminals in separate projects: dynamic additions, three disjoint pairs, overlapping groups, private/shared data checks through assigned credentials, isolation without losing native input, stable reconnects and closing one session while nine remain usable. Research and dynamic workflows use the same observability surfaces. Agent-created teams remain distinct from owner collaboration groups: an invitation grants no context until the participant accepts. Team namespace access follows actual membership, including parent-delegation and revocation fences. Membership changes invalidate displayed permission versions immediately.

Terminal Sessions and web Session detail distinguish automatic admission state from accepted work still executing, report pending/used turn counts and persistent-history fences, and show parent/template/children for spawned workers. Events report observed actor, subject and membership changes rather than inventing an agent's intent.

Research and legacy experiment workers run headlessly. Their consoles expose tasks, results, reported traces and lifecycle information; they do not offer a native tmux pane. Research adds reviewed phase-barrier controls and a separate runner heartbeat. See live research and the single-task pilot.

The control center guide describes reviewed shutdown, scoped history, attention, exact group disconnect, retirement, exposure receipts and continuous study observation. Existing --view agents and --view sessions names remain compatible for registered-session detail and discovered terminals respectively.

docs.title: Validate workflows
docs.text: Use these checks to validate an Agentmux build and the workflow features you intend to use. Model-free checks exercise process control, private Git storage, verification and recovery without loading provider credentials.

docs.title: Build and regression checks
docs.text:
Run from a source checkout with Go 1.24 or newer, Python 3, Git and Node.js. Terminal integration tests also require tmux.

make build
go test -race -count=1 -timeout=20m ./...
go vet ./...
node cmd/agentmux/workweb/app.test.cjs
python3 scripts/test-validate-workflows.py
python3 scripts/test-soak-workflows.py
python3 scripts/test-workflow-review-evidence.py

Conditional integrations report skips when their prerequisites are absent. A passing default suite does not establish that those integrations ran. When testing a binary outside bin/amx, set both AGENTMUX_TEST_BINARY (terminal journeys) and AGENTMUX_INTEGRATION_BINARY (workflow/report integrations) to its absolute path. Otherwise terminal journeys use the checkout's last built binary.

docs.title: Observation and reporting
docs.text:
The v0.15.0 source includes model-free regressions for owner observation, task progress and native readiness:

go test -race ./internal/managed -run 'TestObservation|TestTaskProgress|TestNativeReadiness|TestOperationalRead|TestNativeSummary' -count=1
go test -race ./cmd/agentmux -run 'TestObserve|TestNativeObservation' -count=1
node --test cmd/agentmux/workweb/app.test.cjs
python3 scripts/test-summarize-observations.py
AGENTMUX_INTEGRATION_BINARY="$PWD/bin/amx" python3 scripts/test-summarize-observations.py
python3 scripts/test-summarize-comparison.py

These check bounded full-history summaries, exact attempt/credential fences, separate event and worker timestamps, restart-unknown progress, unavailable components and read-only inspection. Operational-read controls keep a blocked diagnostic connection outside the unchanged 500 ms lease monitor and verify one-slot admission, read-only SQL, shutdown cancellation and credential rotation. Native-summary controls cover unknown admission, authorization and pagination. Structured-diagnostic controls distinguish credential, authorization, local timeout/cancellation, transport, protocol and storage failures without guessing from prose. They check acquisition/decoding durations and explicit null timing for unattempted native reads; existing completion and human output stay intact. The offline reporter rejects malformed, mixed-state and oversized captures, omits injected private fields and keeps legacy/missing timings unknown. Its memory and episode bounds do not grow with capture length. Setting AGENTMUX_INTEGRATION_BINARY runs a real command-only managed workspace through live, completed and stopped-broker captures, checks source/task preservation and offline-report privacy, and confirms shutdown of that exact fixture runtime. Without the variable, that integration reports a skip; the other reporter controls still run. Comparison-summary controls additionally exercise the actual deterministic actor/check failure harness and contradictory records. They make no model calls. They do not prove provider acceptance, useful model progress or elapsed production use. See observability for operational commands and interpretation.

docs.title: Exact initial approval and final acceptance
docs.text:
Guided work in v0.14.0 declares review_policy: early-approval-v1. Its clean path runs an implementation, independent checks and a fresh read-only review. Only an untruncated approval of that exact checked revision can mark address-review and final-review as skipped. Their retained evidence records the skip reason and zero execution attempts. The original approval is retained; it is not replaced by a fabricated final review. final-check always executes the configured acceptance commands against the final revision.

go test -race ./internal/workflow -run 'TestEarlyApproval' -count=1
python3 scripts/test-workflow-review-evidence.py

The minimum clean path uses two native CLI turns; retries can increase that count. Requested changes retain the coder response and fresh final review. Legacy plans with no review policy retain their full loop. Controls reject missing/forged approval identity, changed dependencies, synthetic execution or usage evidence, stale source/results, altered checked revisions, invalid reviews and failed or canceled final checks. Readiness for application still requires fresh passing evidence, and application remains explicit. These command-only controls do not measure model quality or prove a native-provider speedup.

docs.title: Model-free workflow journeys
docs.text:
Choose a new output directory for each run. The validator creates disposable repositories and checks source preservation, durable reports, verification and explicit application behavior.

validation_root=$(mktemp -d)
python3 scripts/validate-workflows.py --binary bin/amx --output "$validation_root/flow"
python3 scripts/validate-workflows.py --binary bin/amx --output "$validation_root/work" --guided

Inspect validation.json: its completion state and case results are the run authority. diagnostic.json describes case progress and is not a substitute for successful finalization. An interrupted process or missing final record does not establish success.

Use --storage shared only to check explicit legacy compatibility. New workflows should use the default private stores.

docs.title: Required Linux isolation
docs.text:
Full workflow isolation requires Linux, Bubblewrap with capped tmpfs support, and working user/PID namespaces. Requested isolation fails closed when the host cannot provide it. Process-group tests alone do not validate filesystem or network isolation.

make test-sandbox

isolation_root=$(mktemp -d)
python3 scripts/validate-workflows.py --binary bin/amx --output "$isolation_root/flow" \
  --storage private --isolation bubblewrap --containment pid-namespace
python3 scripts/validate-workflows.py --binary bin/amx --output "$isolation_root/work" \
  --guided --storage private --isolation bubblewrap --containment pid-namespace

The workflow oracle and cleanup regressions also have an explicit real-CLI isolation mode. A private evidence parent retains integration records for every outcome:

evidence_root=$(mktemp -d)
AGENTMUX_SANDBOX_INTEGRATION=1 \
AGENTMUX_INTEGRATION_BINARY="$PWD/bin/amx" \
AGENTMUX_WORKFLOW_TEST_EVIDENCE_ROOT="$evidence_root" \
  python3 scripts/test-soak-workflows.py

Keep evidence private: it can contain repository contents, patches, task instructions and process details. Review artifacts before sharing them.

docs.title: Fault and recovery soak
docs.text:
The model-free soak checks interrupted turns, verification failures, uncertain application and recovery, source/staging preservation, cleanup and evidence publication. By default each iteration exercises every scenario class.

soak_root=$(mktemp -d)
python3 scripts/soak-workflows.py --binary bin/amx --output "$soak_root/run" \
  --iterations 10 --duration-seconds 1800 \
  --storage private --isolation bubblewrap --containment pid-namespace

Inspect soak.json for state, completed, iteration counts, assertions and coverage exclusions. A selected scenario subset validates only that subset. Cleanup observations cover the recorded process trees. Worker containment also depends on the required namespaces; unrelated host services remain outside that boundary.

docs.title: Live provider checks
docs.text:
Provider tests require an explicit profile, selected authentication, a disposable repository and bounded execution. Review the validator's --help before using --native or a native comparison: these options can make billable requests. Run only the provider routes you have configured and intend to use.

Recorded protocol fixtures establish parser behavior for those frames. Native CLI startup establishes startup behavior. An actual verified tool task supplies stronger evidence for that profile, version and task; none guarantees future provider compatibility or arbitrary task correctness.

See provider compatibility, guided coding, and advanced workflows for setup.

docs.title: Interpret the boundaries
docs.text:
• The Go controller and any selected host inference adapter remain trusted.
  • Private Git stores isolate run evidence; explicit shared storage retains legacy source-store behavior.
  • Bubblewrap constrains selected workers and checks. Independent host writers and services remain outside its authority.
  • Selection bounds are not a hard workspace disk quota. Native deadlines and admission limits do not guarantee a monetary cap; use provider-side controls.
  • Recovery resolves existing application evidence. It does not replay a patch or infer a missing outcome.
  • Exact revision checks and fresh reviews provide task-specific evidence. They do not prove universal correctness.

Use the security model and hardening guide when selecting the boundaries for a deployment.

docs.title: Compare, verify and hand over work
docs.text:
amx flow provides seven owner-driven workflows: independent alternatives, revision-bound checks, cross-provider handoff briefs, bounded snapshot review, missions with dependencies, evidence explanations and repeated comparisons. It complements native tmux sessions and the managed broker. It does not replace their identity, permission, delivery or recovery controls.

These commands are included in Agentmux v0.15.0. For a first checked fixture with no provider configuration, run amx demo. For one coding request with defaults for implementation, fresh reviews and acceptance checks, start with amx work. For a visual map of execution and explicit source application, see the illustrated journey.

Workflow file handling is supported on the published Linux/macOS platforms. Input reads reject symlinks and special files, use bounded nofollow/nonblocking opens, and reject changed-file reads. Other platforms refuse workflow input until a platform-safe opener has been implemented and validated.

Every plan explicitly chooses "execution": "local". Without full isolation, commands, checks and native provider tools execute with trusted host authority; a separate Git worktree does not restrict filesystem or network access. Workflows do not inherit a managed worker's Bubblewrap configuration. Select full workflow isolation explicitly when required. Use trusted owner-authored plans. Provider turns require --allow-models; command plans and checks can execute owner-selected code without that flag, within the selected isolation policy.

docs.title: Try the complete journey without model calls
docs.text:
Build amx, then create a small separate repository. Run these from your Agentmux checkout; use fresh temporary paths if any already exist:

mkdir /tmp/amx-flow-project
git -C /tmp/amx-flow-project init
python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('/tmp/amx-flow-project/README').write_text('Workflow fixture' + chr(10))"
git -C /tmp/amx-flow-project add README
git -C /tmp/amx-flow-project -c user.name='Workflow demo' -c user.email=demo@example.invalid commit -m 'Initial fixture'

amx flow run examples/workflows/compare.json --repo /tmp/amx-flow-project --output /tmp/amx-comparison
amx flow status /tmp/amx-comparison
amx flow explain /tmp/amx-comparison
amx flow handoff /tmp/amx-comparison --candidate calculated --output /tmp/amx-handoff.md

The two candidates start from the same captured content and work separately. Comparisons run up to two candidates concurrently by default; max_parallel can select 1–4 concurrent candidate turns within the plan's overall deadline. Each writes answer.txt in its own worktree. Both undergo the same exact-content check. The source repository is unchanged. The JSON envelope names each retained worktree, patch, result and verification. Open /tmp/amx-comparison/report.html in your browser for an offline review of the results. It is generated after a CLI comparison or mission; flow report RUN --output FILE.html creates another exclusive report copy. Reports execute no model calls and contain private task and code content.

For an actual provider-backed coding task, the native comparison example asks Antigravity and Codex to implement normalize_tags in separate worktrees. External Python assertions check normalization, error behavior, generators, fresh outputs and nonmutation. Installed authenticated CLIs are required. Opt in explicitly:

amx flow run examples/workflows/native-compare.json --repo /tmp/amx-flow-project --output /tmp/amx-native-comparison --allow-models

Provider startup, tool approvals and successful execution depend on the selected native configuration. The model-free validation does not establish that this provider-backed task will complete on a particular account or CLI version. The Antigravity example selects a session-only accept-edits profile and asks for native file tools; it does not grant terminal-command permission. A denied tool is a failed turn even when Antigravity's terminal record says SUCCESS. Actual native events and their digests are retained beside each attempt. The examples explicitly select gemini-3.8-flash-low for Antigravity and gpt-6.1-sol for Codex; update those model selections deliberately when needed.

After inspection, explicitly select the result to bring back:

amx flow apply /tmp/amx-comparison --candidate calculated

Applying is a separate mutation. It checks the retained patch and source state, and refuses stale or incompatible work instead of choosing a winner or merging conflicts automatically. It neither commits nor pushes changes. Inspect the returned result and your source diff before continuing.

docs.title: Independent checks and freshness
docs.text:
A check is an owner-configured executable argv, not shell text:

[
  {"name": "unit-tests", "command": ["go", "test", "./..."], "timeout_seconds": 60}
]

Run checks against a candidate's retained worktree or a selected repository:

amx flow check --repo /tmp/amx-flow-project --checks examples/workflows/checks.json --output /tmp/amx-checks.json

Save verification outside the verified repository. Starting and ending Git content trees bind the result to the checked tracked and nonignored untracked files. A check that changes that content invalidates its result. Ignored build outputs do not affect the content fingerprint. Later edits make the recorded verification stale; flow explain RUN recomputes candidate freshness. Missing worktrees produce an unknown freshness result, not a fresh approval.

Passing means these declared checks passed against that content. It is not a proof of general correctness or an independent security assessment. Checks are owner-controlled and should exercise meaningful acceptance criteria. Each check runs in a separate process. A candidate can modify test files in its own worktree, so tests stored there are not independent of its edits. For a stronger acceptance gate, use an owner-maintained external verifier or explicit assertions in the configured check argv, as the command-only examples do.

docs.title: Handoff to another native agent
docs.text:
flow handoff creates a private Markdown brief with the objective, pinned revision, selected result, patch digest, checks and remaining uncertainty. It does not copy native transcripts, login caches or provider-internal state. Artifact paths in a brief are references; they are not uploaded attachments. A remote recipient needs a separately transferred artifact.

Inspect the saved brief, then send its exact bytes through an existing broker:

amx flow handoff /tmp/amx-comparison --brief /tmp/amx-handoff.md --state /absolute/workspace/state --to reviewer --request-id review-login-fix-1

The owner credential queues an instruct operation. Existing receiver Manual/Review/Auto settings remain authoritative; accepting a broker task does not prove a native turn started or completed. The brief grants no permissions.

Keep the request ID. On an uncertain transport outcome, repeat the same --brief, recipient and request ID to recover the original receipt. Changed payloads under that ID are rejected. Do not regenerate a handoff for the retry: its freshness description may have changed. Saved briefs must be regular files, not symlinks, and at most 512 KiB. Outputs are mode 0600 and never overwrite an existing destination. Handoff output must be outside the source and candidate worktrees. Otherwise saving a brief could invalidate the very revision its freshness statement describes. Saved briefs must contain nonempty valid UTF-8 text; invalid bytes are rejected rather than silently changed during JSON delivery.

docs.title: Bounded missions
docs.text:
amx flow mission examples/workflows/mission.json --repo /tmp/amx-flow-project --output /tmp/amx-mission

A mission's named steps reference candidates and explicit depends_on IDs. A step with "verify": true and no candidate runs the declared checks. Combined with a candidate, it runs that turn and checks the result before successors; max_attempts permits bounded corrections after a completed turn fails checks. Missing dependencies, duplicate IDs and cycles are rejected before execution. Steps run in dependency order in one mission worktree. Implementation steps receive preceding result summaries as context. Structured review steps receive the task, criteria and current files without predecessor narratives or earlier reviews. The declared final checks run before the mission can finish successfully. The original project stays separate until explicit application.

timeout_seconds bounds the plan; candidate timeouts can shorten individual turns. max_attempts is finite and bounded. Failed acceptance checks may allow a configured correction attempt; an uncertain or failed native transport is never automatically replayed. Ctrl+C cancels the active run and preserves its recorded partial outcome. This initial workflow has no automatic resume of an interrupted mission and does not infer that external side effects were undone.

docs.title: Quiet review of changed snapshots
docs.text:
amx flow watch examples/workflows/shadow.json --repo /tmp/amx-flow-project --output /tmp/amx-watch --interval 2s --max-runs 2 --duration 30s

Watch polls the selected source and reviews stable changed content once per eligible revision, using separate retained worktrees. The source is not edited by the orchestration engine. Without full isolation, trusted local reviewer tools retain their normal host authority. Configure review commands and checks accordingly. Repeated unchanged content does not start another reviewer turn. Each run keeps its own findings and verification; a later revision supersedes earlier evidence.

The poll interval is 1 second to 1 hour, the duration is at most 24 hours, and max-runs is 1–100. These limits bound admission to reviews, not monetary provider billing. Closing the foreground command ends the watch; it is not an installed background service or a native terminal input injector. watch.json links to individual run reports.

docs.title: Repeated comparisons
docs.text:
amx flow lab examples/workflows/compare.json --repo /tmp/amx-flow-project --output /tmp/amx-lab --repetitions 3

Lab repeats the comparison against one pinned starting snapshot and rotates candidate order. lab.json reports recorded outcomes, duration and usage rather than selecting a universal winner. Repetitions are 1–20 and the plan deadline bounds the entire collection. Lab forces sequential candidate execution to make the rotated order meaningful; ordinary comparisons can run concurrently.

The scripted example establishes mechanics only. Meaningful team comparisons need representative tasks, appropriate acceptance checks, human assessment, comparable budgets and enough repetitions. Reported provider usage may be absent or have provider-specific meanings; it is not an inferred bill. The existing research runner supplies separate controlled-study capabilities.

docs.title: Private storage and full isolation
docs.text:
New plans default to "storage": "private". The run has its own snapshot Git store, and candidates have independent object stores with no source alternates or shared hardlinks. Source objects, refs, configuration and index remain unchanged while collecting and running work. Explicit application may leave its coordination file .git/agentmux-apply.lock; it preserves the source index and Git objects. "storage": "shared" opts into legacy source-object retention. Older saved reports retain their recorded behavior. Private selection uses exact case-sensitive paths and raw file contents, overriding mutable Git path settings. Verification binds selected files; untracked ignored build artifacts are neither included nor applied. Private snapshots and verifications pin a content-addressed path manifest, so worker commits, index changes or ignore changes cannot hide starting or checked paths. Missing or damaged private selection evidence is refused. Keep each fork's sibling <worktree>.selection.json with its run: standalone checks use it to restore the controller's starting path set. Private records require selection_sha256; shared legacy records keep their existing format. The cumulative manifest is limited to 200,000 paths and 32 MiB of path names; current selected contents remain limited to 100,000 files and 512 MiB. Private preparation refuses partial-clone and promisor repositories before reading objects. Use a complete local repository; capture never downloads missing objects into the source or starts a remote transport. Native workflow profiles cannot select saved sessions. Non-Codex -c and -r are reserved as session controls; compact short-option forms are also refused. Use long options and script files for interpreter wrappers. Owner-selected wrappers remain trusted to honor the fresh-session contract.

For full Linux isolation, add these fields to a private plan:

{
  "storage": "private",
  "isolation": {
    "mode": "bubblewrap",
    "network": "none",
    "read_only_paths": ["/opt/selected-runtime"],
    "home_bytes": 67108864,
    "temp_bytes": 67108864
  }
}

This is a plan fragment, not a complete executable plan. Full isolation requires working Bubblewrap user/PID/mount/network namespaces and capped private tmpfs; there is no weaker fallback. Tools can write their candidate workspace. Review workspaces are read-only. Acceptance checks may create build output in their assigned worktree but cannot change selected content without failing verification; they receive no credentials or network. System runtime files and explicitly selected read-only dependencies are exposed; the original home, source project and unrelated host files are absent from native tool access. The trusted Go controller reads the original source and grants its own Git helper source writes only during explicit admitted apply. Original sources may be linked Git worktrees. Only trusted controller Git receives their exact read-only admin/common directories; tools and checks do not receive those directories. Sources, Git metadata and private run state that overlap a default system runtime mount are refused, since that mount would expose them. Read-only runtime dependencies must also stay outside original source/input trees. Source paths cannot be used to bypass snapshot selection.

Native inference can use "network": "allowlist" with "allow": [{"origin": "https://inference.example"}]. Origins are exact scheme, host and port. DNS resolves once at startup, rejects non-public addresses unless explicitly pinned with "ips", and the relay enforces the selected destination. Proxy settings alone are insufficient: direct networking is denied by the namespace. HTTPS uses a trusted per-turn inspecting proxy with an ephemeral CA. Every HTTP/1.1 Host and HTTP/2 authority must match the granted origin; upstream TLS hostname and certificate verification remains enabled. Only the public CA is mounted read-only, and standard client trust variables (including CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE, SSL_CERT_FILE, Node, requests, curl and Git variables) point to it. The CA signing key stays in memory. Certificate-pinned, mutual-TLS and clients with incompatible custom trust fail closed; opaque tunnels and HTTP upgrades are refused. Forwarded requests have a ten-minute total lifetime, including uploads and streamed responses; shorter run deadlines still apply. Existing managed-mode networking retains its separately documented CONNECT/SNI destination boundary. Checks have neither egress nor provider auth even when a native candidate has grants. Runtime HOME/tmp sizes are enforceable; workspace growth does not have a hard disk quota.

Select native credentials explicitly per candidate:

{
  "auth": {
    "coder": {"file": "/private/codex-auth.json"},
    "reviewer": {"file": "/private/pi-auth.json", "provider": "selected-provider"}
  }
}

auth belongs inside isolation. It accepts supported filtered Codex, Claude or Pi credentials and hands them to only the selected candidate through sealed anonymous data mounted read-only. The source and exposed runtime dependencies cannot contain the selected original login. No original host login directory or ambient provider environment is implicitly imported.

Selected credential values are pinned before snapshots and evidence are created. Diagnostics can be redacted, but identifiers, schema fields and verification results keep their meaning. If a selected value collides with those fields or with final JSON/HTML bytes, publication fails closed. Very short values can make even a fixed diagnostic unsafe, so a nonzero exit may have no printable error. The isolated CLI defers stdout and diagnostics until the operation finishes so it can check credentials selected by later child turns too. This buffer is limited to 64 MiB; exceeding it cancels execution and refuses publication. Retained run evidence remains available during execution.

Direct Antigravity’s native tools are unavailable in full isolation. Select "harness": "antigravity-bridge" and an explicit gemini-… model instead. Pi tools then run inside the capsule; a host adapter supplies inference only using its existing Antigravity login. It receives no workspace tool authority. The plan must select allowlist networking for this bridge. Its private bridge endpoint is granted by the controller; bridge_max_requests defaults to 32 and is bounded to 1–10,000. Retained bridge_usage records admission and rejections. bridge_command and relay_executable can explicitly select trusted adapter/relay executables. They are owner configuration, not model tool permissions. A request count is not a monetary cap.

docs.title: Evidence and limits
docs.text:
Plans may set "process_containment": "pid-namespace" to require the Linux Bubblewrap lifetime boundary for native tools, checks and Git helpers, including watcher and laboratory snapshots. The default is "process-group". Required PID containment is probed before execution and never silently downgraded. It preserves trusted host filesystem/network authority unless isolation is also selected. Standalone verification accepts --containment pid-namespace too. The standalone flow check defaults to --storage private and retains its independent fingerprint store beside the requested output at OUTPUT.git. Keep that store with the verification record for later freshness checks. --storage shared explicitly selects legacy source-object behavior. The standalone check command provides process containment; use a full isolated plan with acceptance checks to require filesystem and network isolation as well.

amx flow recover RUN_DIR --candidate ID inspects and resolves an interrupted application's durable journal against exact source HEAD/content. It does not replay a patch. Omit --candidate for a mission or an unambiguous single result. Unresolved or damaged application history blocks a new application. See the everyday guide for recovery details and boundary requirements.

flow status RUN reads the stored report. flow explain RUN connects recorded inputs, dependencies, candidate results, revisions, patch digests and check evidence; it verifies retained patch integrity and checks current freshness. It reports observable records, not hidden model reasoning or every external filesystem/network action. Owner-editable local evidence is not provider attestation.

The validation guide provides reproducible checks and explains the limits of command fixtures, provider checks and isolation tests.

Plans and checks use strict JSON with unknown fields rejected. Repository paths are relative to the shell's working directory; --repo explicitly overrides the plan path. The repository needs an initial Git commit. Dirty tracked files and nonignored untracked files are captured without changing the source index or working files. Ignored files are excluded, so provide required ignored build dependencies through your own environment or reproducible setup.

Put the new private run directory outside the source repository. Retained worktrees and Git snapshot objects are intentional evidence and consume disk; this version does not delete them automatically. Keep them for review or remove owned run directories deliberately after preserving needed results. Legacy shared runs may also retain source Git worktree registrations and snapshot refs; manage those with Git rather than deleting arbitrary source metadata. No workflow automatically commits, pushes, publishes, spends additional turns after its limits, or grants an agent broader broker authority.

docs.title: Ask for work, inspect the result, apply it
docs.text:
amx work turns one request into a checked coding-and-review journey. A coding provider implements the change and a fresh review context examines the checked files. If the review requests changes, the coder addresses them and a fresh review examines the final revision. Final acceptance checks always run. You receive a saved report and a patch in a separate Git worktree. Agentmux does not integrate that patch into your project until you explicitly apply it.

The clean-approval shortcut, introduced in v0.14.0, is included in Agentmux v0.15.0. v0.13.0 always executes the response and second review. To inspect a checked fixture before configuring providers, start with amx demo.

The report above comes from amx demo, a deterministic fixture with no model calls. For your own task, the daily sequence is:

Step Command What happens Preview amx work "Change" -- CHECK Review the plan without starting models Run Add --allow-models before -- Implement, review and check in a retained worktree Inspect amx work show RUN_ID --open Read fresh report evidence and the patch Apply amx work apply RUN_ID Recheck and apply the selected result explicitly

v0.13.0 includes run-ID listing and report opening. The base journey also works in v0.12.0; see inspection for the older report route.

All five phases remain in the report. A clean initial approval marks the response and second review as skipped, with the original review and exact checked revision retained as evidence. Failed or uncertain work remains available to inspect; it does not become an approved application.

docs.title: Preview your first request
docs.text:
From an existing Git project with an initial commit:

amx work "Fix the login redirect" -- go test ./...

This is a preview. It explains the five phases, exact check command, deadline, planned native turns and private result location. It does not start models, create worktrees or write a run catalog. Go projects can omit the command to use go test ./...; npm projects with an existing test script can use npm test. If both apply or no supported check can be identified, choose the check explicitly after --.

The check is literal executable argv, not a shell command. For example:

amx work "Correct the parser" -- python3 -m pytest tests/test_parser.py
amx work "Handle empty input" -- npm test

Pipes, redirects and && are ordinary arguments after --; they are never silently interpreted by a shell. Use an owner-maintained check script when a check needs several commands.

Preflight checks the Git project, executable availability, check selection and output paths. It cannot establish that provider accounts are signed in. Install and sign in to the selected native CLIs before executing a request. Trusted-local setup discovers installed Codex, Claude Code or Antigravity tools without launching them; executable discovery does not check subscription login.

docs.title: One deadline, visible turn limits
docs.text:
From v0.15.0, an implicit Codex or Claude turn can use the chosen overall --timeout, up to the existing ten-minute per-turn ceiling. All turns and acceptance checks share that overall budget; their limits do not add together, and time is not reserved for a later review. Explicit role limits remain saved. Antigravity print/bridge requests retain their own shorter limits, which the preview displays separately.

For example, --timeout 435s gives implicit Codex/Claude profiles a maximum of 7m15s each within one shared 7m15s run, rather than a hidden three-minute cutoff. The agent is encouraged to run targeted checks and finish started commands; that guidance does not guarantee completion. Controller acceptance checks and explicit application remain mandatory. See process containment for the difference between process groups and Linux namespace containment.

docs.title: Start the work
docs.text:
Add --allow-models before --:

amx work "Fix the login redirect" --allow-models -- go test ./...

Without full isolation, the command prints the result location immediately and reports phase changes as they are recorded. Isolated CLI runs defer stdout and stderr until completion so selected credentials can be checked before publication. Use an explicit --output path to locate retained evidence during such a run. The usual path is:

  1. Implement the requested change and run the declared check.
  2. Review the implementation without changing its checked content.
  3. If changes are requested, address the findings and check the changes.
  4. If findings were addressed, review the exact final revision in fresh context.
  5. Run final acceptance checks and retain the patch.

A fresh review must explicitly approve the exact final checked revision. A clean first review can supply that approval only while the checked content remains unchanged; it never replaces final acceptance checks. An empty review, malformed review, review edits, remaining requested changes or failed acceptance checks stop the journey and remain visible in the result. A model saying “finished” does not replace review approval and executable checks.

From v0.15.0, trusted-local defaults select an installed CLI: Codex first for coding, then Claude for review when available. A different installed provider is preferred for review; a single installed CLI uses separate fresh contexts for both roles. The preview names and pins both profiles in its suggested run command. --coder and --reviewer remain authoritative; failures never switch providers. Isolated defaults remain Codex and the Antigravity bridge because their selected credentials and network/runtime boundaries are explicit. Availability depends on your account and CLI versions. Each review starts a new native session with the owner’s task, acceptance criteria and current files. Implementation narrative, earlier review findings and earlier approvals are excluded from that review’s input. Workflow profiles that request native resume, continue or transcript selection are rejected before admission. Codex workflow turns also use ephemeral sessions.

In v0.14.0, a clean first review uses two native turns when implementation checks pass on the first attempt: implementation and independent review. Requested changes normally use four turns. Completed coding-check failures can use up to six with the default two attempts per coding phase; the preview shows the full 2–6 range. In v0.13.0 the range is 4–6. Native turns can contain multiple provider requests, so these counts do not measure inference requests or subscription usage. Transport failures and uncertain turns are not automatically replayed.

Useful controls are:

amx work "Fix the redirect" --timeout 8m --check-timeout 2m --attempts 2 --allow-models -- go test ./...
amx work "Fix the redirect" --dry-run --allow-models -- go test ./...
amx work "Fix the redirect" --repo /path/to/project --output /private/new-run --allow-models -- go test ./...
amx work "Fix the redirect" --containment pid-namespace --allow-models -- go test ./...

The overall deadline is 1 second to 24 hours. Per-check deadlines are 1 second to 10 minutes. --attempts is 1–5 and applies separately to the two coding phases. --dry-run always previews, including when --allow-models is present.

docs.title: Require process containment
docs.text:
On Linux, --containment pid-namespace requires Bubblewrap and a working user/PID namespace boundary. Execution probes that boundary before starting workflow work; an unavailable boundary fails without falling back. Native tools, checks, Git filters, integration and freshness checks inherit the recorded requirement. A descendant that creates another session or process group remains in the PID namespace and is terminated with it. The default process-group policy retains the ordinary process-group cleanup behavior.

This option alone preserves host filesystem, network, devices and native authentication access. Requests to independent host services are outside its process-descendant boundary. Use the full isolation option below to restrict filesystem and network authority too.

Preview also shows selected file and byte counts. Snapshot admission is bounded to 100,000 existing selected files and 512 MiB, checked before raw working-content snapshot objects are written and checked again while fingerprinting. These are protective selection bounds; trusted filters and unrelated writers are not a disk quota.

docs.title: Private snapshots and full isolation
docs.text:
New runs default to --storage private. Snapshot objects live in the private run directory, and every candidate has an independent Git object store without alternates or shared hardlinks. Capturing and running a task leaves the source’s index, objects, refs and Git configuration unchanged. Explicit application uses a persistent .git/agentmux-apply.lock coordination file while preserving the source index, objects, refs and configuration. --storage shared explicitly selects the legacy source-object-store behavior; full isolation requires private storage. Deleting a private run removes its retained copies, but cannot erase filesystem backups or independently copied evidence.

On Linux, --isolation bubblewrap requires real user, PID, mount and network namespaces and capped private HOME and temporary filesystems. Required probes fail closed. Native tools see their selected candidate workspace, system runtime files and explicit --read-only-path dependencies. Reviewer workspaces are read-only. Checks can create build output in their assigned worktree, receive no provider credentials or network, and fail verification if selected files change. The default network policy is none; provider turns need the exact inference origins you deliberately grant:

amx work "Fix the redirect" --isolation bubblewrap --network allowlist \
  --coder codex --reviewer claude \
  --allow-origin https://YOUR-CODEX-INFERENCE-ORIGIN \
  --allow-origin https://YOUR-CLAUDE-INFERENCE-ORIGIN \
  --auth coder=/private/codex-auth.json --auth reviewer=/private/claude-auth.json \
  --read-only-path /opt/selected-native-runtime --allow-models -- /usr/bin/python3 -m unittest

Replace the origin placeholders with the actual origins needed by your selected profiles. Grants match exact scheme, host and port; redirects to another origin need their own grant. HTTPS is inspected by a trusted per-turn proxy: an ephemeral public CA is mounted read-only, each HTTP/1.1 Host or HTTP/2 authority is checked, and upstream certificates and hostnames are verified. The signing key stays in controller memory. Certificate-pinned, mutual-TLS or custom-trust clients may fail closed; opaque tunnels and HTTP upgrades are refused. Runtime directories and executable dependencies outside the system runtime must be selected explicitly. Do not grant a broad home or credential directory as a runtime dependency. Selected credential files must remain outside the source project and exposed dependencies. Supported fields are filtered into a sealed anonymous, read-only handoff for that candidate; the original login file and ambient login directories are not mounted. This selection does not establish that a provider account or endpoint is usable.

With full isolation the default Antigravity reviewer uses antigravity-bridge: an explicit Gemini model runs through a bounded host inference bridge, while Pi performs the model’s tools inside the isolated workspace. The host bridge does not execute model tools or export Antigravity login files. Its inference requests are counted and capped separately from native turns. See the advanced guide for plan fields and direct provider selection.

The Go controller remains trusted: it reads source inputs, runs the selected host inference adapter and admits explicit source application after its checks. Independent host services and unrelated host writers are outside its authority. HOME and temporary filesystems default to 64 MiB each. Workspace growth has no hard disk quota; selection bounds and post-run evidence limits do not provide one. Keep reports private because they contain task and code data.

docs.title: Inspect the result
docs.text:
amx work status
amx work show latest
amx work list --limit 10
amx work show RUN_ID --open

These commands use the current Git project. status explains the recorded phases, checks, accepted review, changed files and next action. show also prints the hash-checked patch preview and saved HTML report path. The preview is capped at 64 KiB, preserves code line breaks and escapes terminal control characters; truncated previews identify the full retained patch. Use the retained artifact or explicit apply command for integration, because displayed escapes are for inspection. Ordinary inspection starts no model and opens no browser. list shows stable run IDs for this project, newest first. Omit --limit to retain the full list; an explicit limit accepts 1–1024.

In v0.13.0, show RUN_ID --open renders a fresh private, script-free HTML report from the selected run's saved evidence and asks the system browser to open it. Use an explicit ID, directory or latest; it resolves that selector once and never starts another run. Existing report.html is not opened. The generated file path is printed and retained even if the browser cannot open it. --open and --json cannot be combined. Stable IDs and --limit are included in v0.13.0.

Use an explicit directory or run ID to inspect another recorded attempt:

amx work show /private/run-directory --repo /path/to/project
amx work status RUN_ID --repo /path/to/project

A run belonging to another project is refused. The catalog cannot redirect an application into a different repository.

By default, private run state lives under $XDG_STATE_HOME/agentmux/workflows, or ~/.local/state/agentmux/workflows. --catalog DIR selects another private catalog; use the same option to list or resolve its latest run. Explicit result directories are indexed too. Outputs never overwrite an existing run. For an explicit --output, its parent directory must already exist; omitting the option lets Agentmux prepare its private catalog hierarchy for you.

--json prints structured output on stdout. Phase progress remains on stderr:

amx work status latest --json
amx work "Fix the redirect" --json --allow-models -- go test ./...

docs.title: Apply only the result you inspected
docs.text:
amx work apply latest

Application is explicit. It rechecks the original source, final result, verification and patch, and refuses stale or incompatible work. It does not commit, push, publish or merge conflicts. Your staging remains unchanged; inspect your source diff before committing.

If unrelated work changed the source or candidate since the run, keep both results and reconcile deliberately. An application with uncertain effects reports whether changes may already be present; inspect before retrying.

docs.title: Recover an interrupted application
docs.text:
amx work status latest
amx work recover latest

Before admitting source mutation, Agentmux saves an uncertain application intent. After applying and checking the source, it finalizes that same record. Changed files and directory entries are synced before a confirmed receipt is saved. Unsupported directory durability fails closed. The application lock survives in an admitted Git writer if its controller dies, and releases when the writer exits. A stale coordination filename by itself does not hold the kernel lock.

Recovery takes the same lock and compares source HEAD and exact content with the recorded starting and final snapshots. An exact match can resolve the saved intent as not_applied or applied; divergent or uninspectable content remains uncertain. Recovery updates existing records, never reapplies a patch or undoes source files. Damaged history blocks application until inspected. Settle unrelated writers first; Agentmux's lock coordinates Agentmux operations, not every host application. Filesystem and hardware must honor their sync guarantees.

docs.title: Return after interruption
docs.text:
Ctrl+C cancels active work and retains its recorded partial outcome. A valid run is registered during execution and again after completion so it remains discoverable through status and list. The printed result directory provides a direct route if catalog registration was unavailable.

Recorded running is not proof that a process is still alive. After a hard process or machine interruption, inspect its evidence before starting a new attempt. This command does not automatically resume an uncertain provider turn or undo external side effects. A failed final review remains available for inspection; it is not silently treated as approval.

docs.title: Execution and evidence
docs.text:
v0.14.0 guided reports record the explicit early-approval-v1 review policy. The original review binds both the Git tree and selected raw content; skipped phases have no model attempts or invented review results. Complete structured review verdicts, including findings, remain available within the 128 KiB review limit. Inputs and check diagnostics can still be excerpts with retained evidence references. Reading a completed report compares its declared checks, candidate profiles and phase execution with the separately retained plan and actual attempt, skip and verification records. Candidate profile fingerprints exclude environment credentials and identify declared settings, not a provider's resolved model. These are owner-controlled records, not provider attestations or protection against an owner rewriting all evidence. Existing advanced plans without this policy retain their declared execution phases.

Failed or interrupted runs can retain only the checks reached before stopping. Those exact planned prefixes remain inspectable; they never authorize application. The guided policy requires successful completion and all final checks before apply.

Without --isolation bubblewrap, native tools and checks use trusted local execution with host authority. Private Git stores separate retained data; they do not themselves confine a process. With full isolation, the recorded policy is required again for inspection, verification, recovery and application helpers. Unavailable boundaries remain visible as failures. The trusted controller and owner-selected runtime dependencies are part of that boundary.

For individual comparisons, custom mission plans, exact handoff delivery, snapshot watchers and repeated trials, use the advanced workflow guide. The validation guide explains how to check your build, selected providers and isolation boundaries.

docs.title: Coordination primitives
docs.text:
For current interactive and managed teams, coordination goes through an authenticated broker: scoped messages/boards, queued instructions, private and shared memory, versioned permissions and consented teams. Start with work sessions, live permissions and the managed runtime. Those controls are independent of native tool approvals and filesystem sandboxing.

The remainder of this page describes the original v1 layout mode's tmux KV, output polling and raw pane scaling. These remain available, but do not enforce the broker's agent identities, hierarchy or per-agent access rules. They do not create process/filesystem isolation.

docs.title: 1. The Blackboard (KV-Store)
docs.text:
If five agents are working in five different tmux panes, they need a "Shared Brain" to store state (e.g., "What is the current sub-task?").

Instead of running a Redis or SQLite database, Agentmux uses Tmux Session Options.

Any pane can run amx kv-set my-session key "value" to write, and any other pane can run amx kv-get my-session key to read.

  • Stateless: If Agentmux crashes, the data survives in tmux.
  • Inspectable: amx kv-list SESSION shows the values that participants explicitly stored, not their private reasoning.

docs.title: 2. Synchronization (Wait)
docs.text:
Agents often need to block until another agent finishes a task. Rather than complex webhooks, Agentmux uses the terminal itself as the messaging bus.

The amx wait command polls a target pane's output stream. When it detects a specific regex string, it unblocks and exits with code 0.

docs.title: 3. Dynamic Scaling
docs.text:
When an agentic team encounters a massive task, the manager might decide to parallelize the work.

The legacy scale SESSION AGENT COUNT command adds/removes panes using the original configuration and reapplies the window layout. Managed delegated spawning instead requires approved templates, admission limits and broker authority; see dynamic teams.

docs.title: 4. LLM Native Awareness
docs.text:
The legacy pane launcher provides these context-delivery mechanisms:

  1. Environment Injection: Every pane automatically receives $AGENTMUX_SESSION and $AGENTMUX_PANE environment variables.
  2. CLI Tool Bridge: Models call real coordination actions through amx tool-call, using --from-stdin, --from-file, or --from-json, which wraps the existing Agentmux CLI in a machine-stable JSON envelope.
  3. Native MCP Surface: Agentmux can expose the same coordination registry through amx mcp-server, allowing providers with verified MCP support to use the tools natively instead of shelling out.
  4. Schema Export For Compatibility: The amx tools command still generates provider-friendly JSON schemas (openai, codex, gemini, claude) for debugging or compatibility exports, but it is no longer the primary runtime contract.
  5. JIT Compilation: Using the provider, persona, and optional reasoning_effort fields, Agentmux compiles provider-specific CLI commands that deliver persona and operational coordination through the strongest real surfaces available, selecting native-mcp or cli-bridge per provider at launch time.

Persona delivery is intentionally provider-specific: - Claude appends the persona and coordination instructions to Claude Code's default system prompt. - Pi appends the persona and CLI bridge instructions to its default system prompt. - Antigravity uses an interactive bootstrap prompt through agy, with the CLI bridge. Agentmux does not modify shared Antigravity MCP configuration. - Gemini uses a native workspace context file via a session-scoped runtime artifact. - Codex and GPTMe currently use bootstrap prompt delivery.

docs.title: Layout compiler mental model
docs.text:
This page describes the legacy v1 workspace compiler (load, render, and raw tmux pane commands). Its declarative launch layer is stateless.

The v2 managed runtime is stateful: it keeps authenticated coordination, tasks, permissions, memory, and process ownership in a private store. For the terminal-first daily workflow, start with work sessions.

docs.title: The Core Concept
docs.text:
In this mode, Agentmux compiles declarative YAML into standard tmux CLI commands.

  • It does not run a background daemon.
  • It does not intercept your keys.
  • It does not have its own database.

Once the launch command exits, tmux owns the pane processes. Removing that launcher does not by itself stop them. This description does not apply to the managed broker/supervisor, which has persistent state and explicit lifecycle controls.

docs.title: The Hierarchy
docs.text:
A configuration breaks down into three core concepts:

  1. Agents (The "Who"): These are reusable execution templates. They define what runs (e.g., a Python script or an LLM CLI), the environment variables it needs, and how it behaves when it exits.
  2. Windows (The "Where"): These define the physical layout of your screen (e.g., even-horizontal). They provide shared context (like a working directory) for the panes inside them.
  3. Panes (The "What"): These are the actual, running processes. A pane instantiates an Agent. You can have five Panes all running the same "Researcher" Agent, and they will be five distinct shell processes.

docs.title: Injected Metadata
docs.text:
To manage these panes without a daemon, Agentmux injects state directly into the tmux processes using Tmux User Options (e.g., @agentmux_name, @agentmux_startup_command).

When you run amx status, Agentmux simply asks tmux to print these options. These options make legacy layout state inspectable without a separate database.

docs.title: Everyday commands
docs.text:
amx is the Agentmux command. amx alone opens the current terminal dashboard, the sole running workspace, or a workspace chooser when several are running; it starts no agents. amx a restores the last live native terminal in the selected workspace. If no terminal has been selected or it has closed, the workbench opens. With several running workspaces, choose one or pass -s NAME.

The searchable choosers, context, observe, task/tasks, exact-task workbench opening, bounded run lists and report opening below are included in v0.15.0.

docs.title: Daily power-user loop
docs.text:
Goal Short route Resume amx a; filter the workspace chooser by name, path or status Launch Shift+N inherits the selected provider and project; review before starting Peer delegation Shift+C in Connections reviews Commands, both delivery modes and returned results together Owner task amx send ID "Do this" --mode instruction -s NAME; copy its printed inspection command Inspect amx task TASK_ID -s NAME, or Ctrl+K → Tasks for selected session Observe amx observe -s NAME; add --watch for repeated fresh evidence Recover amx task TASK_ID --open -s NAME; inspect its evidence and review the exact task/version

Use amx context to see which workspace an ordinary command selects and why. It never starts or switches a workspace. Outside an attachment, bare amx and amx a offer running-workspace selection; commands with IDs still default to work unless you supply a selector. Keep -s NAME on scripts and copied commands.

Ctrl+W opens the same workspace filter inside the workbench without losing an open draft or review. Press / or Ctrl+F, then filter by name, path or status; arrows or Ctrl+N/P choose, Ctrl+U clears, Enter opens the exact displayed state, and Esc returns. While filtering, j, k and q are literal query text. Use amx send --help, amx attach --help or another command's help for focused options. amx help all retains the full reference.

In Connections, [ focuses Sender and ] focuses Recipient. Tab or Shift+Tab switches fields; Up/Down changes only the highlighted identity. Left/Right still changes views. Focus changes neither permissions nor the other field's selected identity.

amx observe separates broker connectivity, worker check-ins, native events, effective delivery uncertainty and retained outcomes. It counts complete task history and prints exact task inspection commands; quiet reporting alone does not establish a stalled or failed model.

docs.title: Ask for a checked coding change
docs.text:
The checked workflow, --limit and --open below are included in v0.15.0. For a first checked fixture with no provider setup, run amx demo. From a Git project with an initial commit and the selected native CLIs installed:

amx work "Fix the login redirect" -- go test ./...
amx work "Fix the login redirect" --allow-models -- go test ./...
amx work status
amx work show latest
amx work list --limit 10
amx work show RUN_ID --open
amx work apply latest

The first command previews without model calls or run files. The second starts bounded coding, fresh review and checks in a retained private worktree. Inspect status, show and the saved HTML report before choosing apply; application rechecks freshness and changes your project without committing or pushing it. After an interrupted application, inspect and use amx work recover latest to resolve its journal without replaying the patch. See work on a task for provider, isolation, deadlines and recovery details, or advanced workflows for command-only comparisons and custom plans.

A clean first review of the exact independently checked revision can finish with two native CLI turns, skipping the response and second review. Final acceptance checks still run; requested changes keep the full loop. Saved reports show skipped phases explicitly.

Copy a stable run ID from work list when following up on older work. --open requires an explicit ID, directory or latest; it renders a fresh private HTML report from saved evidence and opens it with the system browser. It prints and retains the generated file if the opener fails. It never starts another run.

work selects the Git project in the current directory (or --repo DIR). The interactive commands below select a running workspace with -s NAME; these are separate selectors.

docs.title: Open and manage sessions
docs.text:
amx up -s work -p /path/to/project -d
amx ui -s work
amx ls -s work
amx a claude -s work
amx new reviewer --harness codex -p /path/to/project -s work
amx name reviewer "Review login changes" -s work

Use stable session IDs from amx ls when attaching, naming, or connecting agents. Display names describe the task and can repeat. Select a workspace explicitly with -s NAME when switching between several workspaces; amx ws lists saved workspaces. Attaching opens the normal native terminal so you can keep typing, approve tools, and interrupt work yourself. Within an owned tmux attachment, an omitted workspace selector uses that exact attachment after checking its attempt identity. Outside, commands with an explicit agent ID default to work; there is no global last-used workspace setting. up / start always defaults to work when no selector is given, even inside another workspace. amx -s NAME ui also works.

In the workbench, Tab switches between the session sidebar and the current view’s content. The purple header shows focus; ↑/↓ navigates that area. Left/Right or 1–8 changes views. Esc returns focus to the sidebar after closing an open reader or editor. Ctrl+P finds sessions by task, stable ID, provider or project: Enter opens the native terminal, Tab selects it in the workbench, and Esc returns. In Connections (Links on narrow terminals), use the sidebar to choose the sender, then Tab to choose a recipient with ↑/↓; h/l also changes the recipient. F1 returns from a native terminal.

See terminal folders and layouts for scratch panes, multiple agents in one window and reattachment.

docs.title: Pair native agents for tasks
docs.text:
Task pairing requires v0.15.0 or later, including the workspace controller.

amx pair claude codex --delivery auto -s work
amx pair claude codex --delivery auto --apply -s work

The first command previews; each --apply invocation reads and prints the current review before making one atomic update. It grants Commands both ways, sets both receivers and enables returned results. In Connections, Shift+C opens one frozen review: 1 chooses Review, 2 chooses Auto, Enter applies.

Auto affects eligible existing queues and future work from all permitted senders, not just this pair. New grants/results can make previously ineligible items eligible. Limits and spent turns remain saved. Use --delivery review for exact item approval. Pairing leaves notes, pings, shared boards and memory alone. Older pinned controllers need an explicit upgrade or a fresh workspace.

docs.title: Share chat and memory, or edit one direction
docs.text:
amx link claude reviewer -s work
amx allow claude reviewer commands -s work
amx mode reviewer review -s work

link provides a shared board and memory scope. allow grants one direction of command permission. mode decides whether the receiver accepts a native turn: Manual stays human-led, Review needs approval of each exact item, and Auto delivers eligible turns within the configured limits.

amx send reviewer "Check the login proposal." --mode instruction -s work
amx mode reviewer -j -s work
amx mode reviewer --approve CANDIDATE_ID -s work
amx tasks --to reviewer -s work
amx task TASK_ID -s work
amx task TASK_ID --open -s work

Copy the exact pending candidate ID from the status. A queued or submitted item does not prove the model executed it; inspect its receipt and native terminal. Provider-specific guarantees are in native collaboration.

Start with the unfiltered recipient history above so pending approval and submitted results stay visible. Add --status running only when you want to limit the view to running tasks.

tasks searches retained history at the broker, newest first, with --query, --status, --to and --limit (1–200). Copy the printed More command for the next page, or add -j for JSON. task shows the exact instruction, result, version and available receipt/recovery evidence, then prints a command to open that exact task. task TASK_ID --open goes straight to its Tasks view without searching the history; old tasks and retired recipients remain addressable. Opening changes no task state. Any recovery action still reviews the exact task/version and requires explicit confirmation. --open applies only to task and cannot be combined with --json.

In the workbench or web app, Tasks for selected session clears prior filters and opens that recipient's complete paginated history. Web attention rows also offer Inspect tasks, including for a retired recipient.

amx mode reviewer manual -s work
amx deny claude reviewer commands -s work
amx unlink claude reviewer -s work

Manual pauses future native dispatch and requests cancellation of an active peer turn where the adapter supports it. Inspect the receipt and native terminal: the request does not confirm that work stopped, and it does not interrupt an unrelated human turn. deny removes the chosen directional permission. unlink disables only the exact selected pair/group; isolate ID disconnects that session from all peers. Other groups or explicit grants can still provide access; inspect active tasks separately because already read context and completed effects cannot be undone.

docs.title: Short names
docs.text:
Short command Full command up start a, open attach ui dashboard ls sessions ws workspaces new add link collaborate unlink disconnect name label mode delivery

Everyday commands accept -s for --session, -p for --project, -d for --detach, and -j for --json where that option applies. web and task also accept -o for --open. Text after a literal -- keeps its original meaning. Long commands and flags remain available. allow FROM TO commands|messages|pings and the matching deny change only the selected permission; they do not enable receiver delivery or grant new memory access.
