In terminal Connections, inspect the recipient's delivery summary and press Shift+D for its settings or Shift+A to review a pending item. amx delivery ID auto -s work can dispatch existing eligible queued items and preserves saved subscriptions and limits. Choose Review first to inspect an exact item. Results of your own instructions use the correlated task channel, without a reverse message grant; receiving them as native turns still needs your own Results subscription and delivery readiness. Use amx task TASK_ID to inspect the recorded result directly. See native collaboration and the complete command reference for advanced options.

docs.title: Your first checked result
docs.text:
Start with a deterministic fixture before configuring providers or using a real project. Install Agentmux v0.15.0, then run from any directory:

amx demo

After installation, this command needs Git and a POSIX shell. It needs no Python, tmux, provider CLI, account or API key and makes no model calls.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
The demo creates a new private temporary directory containing a disposable Git repository. It runs a deterministic candidate through Agentmux's workflow engine, checks the candidate independently, retains a patch and report, then applies the checked patch only to the generated repository. A final byte comparison verifies the fixture result. Your current project is not the target.

Success means the workflow check and fixture application verification passed. Look for:

Success: checked patch applied; fixture file independently verified.

The command prints the repository, report and patch locations. Retained files let you inspect what happened after the command exits.

This is a fixture, not an AI coding task. It demonstrates local workflow mechanics; it does not measure model quality or certify sandbox isolation.

docs.title: Inspect the evidence
docs.text:
Open the printed run/report.html in a browser and inspect the checked change. The report is a local file; no running web server is needed. The neighboring run/report.json retains machine-readable evidence. The command also prints the exact commands for reading the run from the terminal:

amx flow status /printed/demo-directory/run
amx flow explain /printed/demo-directory/run

Use the actual printed path in place of /printed/demo-directory. Confirm that the candidate passed its independent check, inspect the saved patch, and compare the resulting repository/hello.txt with that change. Its final contents are:

Agentmux demo: checked change applied.

Reading these records starts no models and applies no additional change.

Each amx demo invocation creates a fresh directory. To choose where to retain it, pass an absolute path that does not yet exist:

amx demo --output /path/to/new-agentmux-demo

Keep that directory while inspecting the evidence. Delete it when finished; it contains only this run's fixture and retained files.

If demo is unknown, check command -v amx and amx version, then follow the upgrade instructions. If Git or the shell is missing, install the named dependency and rerun. A failed demo is not a passing result: retain the printed diagnostics and files when reporting the failure.

docs.title: Move to a live coding task
docs.text:
Install and sign in to the native CLIs you want to use. Trusted-local setup selects installed tools and shows the coder/reviewer in its preview; Codex plus Claude is the usual pair when both are installed. In a Git project with an initial commit, preview a specific task with its executable acceptance check:

amx work "Fix the login redirect" -- go test ./...

Replace the request and go test ./... with your task and check. This preview starts no models and writes no run files. It shows the selected providers, phases, deadlines and result location.

When the preview is suitable, explicitly permit provider calls:

amx work "Fix the login redirect" --allow-models -- go test ./...
amx work status
amx work show latest

Provider calls can incur charges. Agentmux retains the implementation, fresh reviews, executable checks and patch in a separate worktree. Inspect the report and patch before choosing amx work apply latest; that command changes your project. A failed check or unapproved review does not become an accepted result.

See work on a task for provider choices, deadlines, failed or interrupted runs and optional Linux isolation. For several interactive native conversations instead, follow the short native-session quickstart.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Agentmux's CLI is amx. Published binaries need no Go toolchain. Python 3 runs the installer; the first amx demo needs only Git and a POSIX shell after installation. Native sessions additionally require tmux 3.2+ and separately installed, authenticated provider CLIs.

docs.title: Install a published binary (recommended)
docs.text:
Release v0.15.0 provides Linux and macOS 13+ binaries for x86-64 and ARM64. The macOS minimum follows the release toolchain. Agentmux uses MIT; dependency notices are bundled separately. It includes amx demo, checked work/flow journeys, native sessions, searchable workspace choosers, context, observe, retained task/tasks inspection and exact-task recovery navigation. It also includes explicit sender/recipient focus in Connections, structured observation diagnostics, offline operational/comparison reports, and a two-turn clean-review path with final checks. Task pairing configures mutual Commands, both native delivery modes and returned results in one atomic review. Trusted-local checked work selects installed native providers and shows the choices before execution. No Go toolchain is needed for these controls. The managed runtime and workbench remain experimental.

An existing workspace keeps its pinned controller and workers after installation. Inspect current work before explicitly upgrading/restarting that workspace; a new observer executable alone does not upgrade its controller. Earlier v0.12.0 archives remain unchanged.

For publicly accessible release assets, download the versioned installer from GitHub, inspect it, then run it with Python 3. These commands also require curl. The installer downloads the matching platform archive and checksum manifest from the selected release. For assets that require authentication, use the GitHub CLI route below.

mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
amx_release_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
curl --fail --location --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pagel-s/agentmux/v0.15.0/scripts/install-release.py \
  --output "$amx_release_dir/install-release.py"
# Read the downloaded installer before running it.
python3 "$amx_release_dir/install-release.py" --version v0.15.0 \
  --destination "$HOME/.local/bin/amx"
rm -r "$amx_release_dir"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
amx version
amx demo

For access-controlled releases, authenticate GitHub CLI with an account that has repository access (gh auth login if needed), then download the assets and versioned installer before installation:

mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
amx_release_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
gh release download v0.15.0 --repo pagel-s/agentmux \
  --dir "$amx_release_dir" --pattern 'agentmux_*.tar.gz' --pattern checksums.txt
gh api repos/pagel-s/agentmux/contents/scripts/install-release.py \
  --method GET -f ref=v0.15.0 --header 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json' \
  > "$amx_release_dir/install-release.py"
# Read the downloaded installer before running it.
python3 "$amx_release_dir/install-release.py" --version v0.15.0 \
  --artifact-dir "$amx_release_dir" --destination "$HOME/.local/bin/amx"
rm -r "$amx_release_dir"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
amx version
amx demo

Upgrading: add --replace to the python3 command. The installer verifies SHA256 and the executable version before atomically installing amx. A previous amx → agentmux shortcut is migrated to a real amx executable. Its exact old executable is retained as an amx.backup-* file; the recognized old agentmux path is retired. Unrecognized symlink destinations are refused. Replacing an existing regular executable requires the explicit --replace flag and retains its previous inode as a backup. A fresh installation creates only amx.

amx demo prints the location of its disposable repository and retained check, patch and report evidence. See your first checked result for what to inspect and how to move on to a live task. It starts no models and needs no provider login. Run amx help for everyday commands and amx help all for the full command reference.

Archives retain the agentmux_OS_ARCH.tar.gz project name and contain amx, docs, examples and scripts. The installer also accepts older archives whose executable is named agentmux. To use already downloaded release assets, add --artifact-dir /path/to/release-files; the directory must include the matching platform archive and checksums.txt. From a checkout, run python3 scripts/install-release.py with the same version and destination options.

A checksum checks consistency with the release manifest, not an independent signature. The direct HTTPS route works without a login when the release assets are publicly accessible. For access-controlled repositories, download the archive and checksum manifest using authenticated GitHub tooling, then use the checkout's installer with --artifact-dir as described above.

Installation does not restart native sessions or replace a workspace's pinned controller. Reattach with the new amx for its updated dashboard. Follow the recovery guide when deliberately upgrading a running controller; fresh workspaces use the current controller automatically. Existing external bridges that name a retired public executable may need their setup printed again with amx connect.

Strict Bubblewrap isolation requires Linux with working user namespaces and a supported Bubblewrap. macOS supports native tmux sessions and explicitly trusted local execution. A shell split beside an isolated agent is a host shell, not a new sandbox.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
Building needs Git, Make and Go 1.24+. Use Go 1.27.3 for a current maintained toolchain; 1.24 is retained as the source-compatibility minimum. Published distributions and installed-artifact checks use 1.27.3. make install also uses Python 3. The Makefile prefers a compatible repo-local toolchain under .tools/, then Go from PATH. Native sessions additionally need tmux 3.2+.

# Ubuntu/Debian: install Go 1.24+ separately if needed
sudo apt install git make python3

git clone https://github.com/pagel-s/agentmux.git
cd agentmux
make build
./bin/amx version
./bin/amx demo

In an existing clean checkout on main, run git pull --ff-only and make build. For a user-local installation:

make install
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
command -v amx
amx version

The installer does not edit shell configuration. Add the PATH export to your shell's startup file if needed, and check command -v amx in each new terminal. After later source updates, run make install again. Select another prefix with make install PREFIX=/your/prefix, or use BINDIR and optional DESTDIR for packaging. Existing executable replacements retain their original inode in a uniquely named backup.

Check the source workflow commands after installation:

amx demo
amx work --help
amx flow --help
amx task --help
amx context --help
amx observe --help

amx work "Describe the change" -- CHECK [ARG...] previews a checked coding journey without starting models or creating run files. Execution needs the selected installed and authenticated provider CLIs plus --allow-models. For a first model-free plan, use the separate temporary project in advanced workflows.

Remote go install github.com/pagel-s/agentmux/cmd/agentmux@latest is unsupported: go.mod declares module path agentmux, so Go rejects the GitHub module path. Use the published installer or build from the checkout.

docs.title: Check the native providers
docs.text:
For native terminal sessions, install tmux 3.2+ (brew install tmux on macOS or sudo apt install tmux on Ubuntu/Debian) as well as the selected provider CLIs.

claude --version
codex --version
amx doctor

Open each provider once directly and complete its normal login/startup prompts. Agentmux reuses those native logins in trusted local mode; it does not install a provider or sign you in. amx doctor CONFIG also checks configured native CLI compatibility.

For your first result, use the model-free demo. For native conversations, continue with the short native quickstart or terminal folders and layouts. The optional verification walkthrough covers collaboration, shared memory, revocation and web controls. From a checkout, Linux operators can verify model-free isolation with:

python3 scripts/smoke-managed.py
python3 scripts/smoke-managed-interactive.py

A missing Bubblewrap feature such as --size, or unavailable user namespaces, fails the isolation check; it does not silently select trusted local execution. For a configured team, use the managed setup wizard.

docs.title: Verify a native workspace step by step
docs.text:
This optional walkthrough checks boundaries and recovery. For ordinary setup, start with the short quickstart.

This journey tests the everyday workflow: two normal native conversations, readable session identities, opt-in communication and memory, then ending the collaboration while keeping both terminals usable. It uses a separate workspace named try-agentmux. Every owner command below selects that same workspace, regardless of the current directory.

For your first checked result without provider setup, use amx demo. For a live coding request with implementation, fresh review and acceptance checks, use work on a task. The walkthrough below covers native interactive sessions.

The walkthrough and its power-user controls are included in v0.15.0; upgrade older workspace controllers explicitly.

docs.title: 1. Install and check Agentmux
docs.text:
Install v0.15.0 using the published binary instructions for the amx command without a Go toolchain. Then skip the source-build commands below and continue with the native CLI checks in this step.

Alternatively, build from source with Git, Make, Python 3, tmux 3.2+ and Go 1.24+. On a new checkout:

git clone https://github.com/pagel-s/agentmux.git
cd agentmux
make build
./bin/amx version
./bin/amx doctor

For a user-local executable:

make install
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

Make that PATH setting available in each new terminal; see installation. Check command -v amx and amx version if another installed copy might be selected.

The default team needs both Claude Code and Codex installed and logged in:

claude --version
codex --version

Open each directly once and complete its normal login/startup prompts. If a CLI does not work outside Agentmux, resolve that before testing its Agentmux session. Other harnesses or a single-provider team can use the setup wizard with a custom configuration.

docs.title: 2. Create a disposable project and workspace
docs.text:
In a regular shell outside an existing tmux attachment:

amx_demo_project="$(mktemp -d "$HOME/agentmux-playground.XXXXXX")"
git -C "$amx_demo_project" init
printf '# Agentmux playground\n' > "$amx_demo_project/README.md"
printf 'Project: %s\n' "$amx_demo_project"

amx start --session try-agentmux --project "$amx_demo_project" --detach
amx sessions --session try-agentmux

Expected: two registered native sessions with stable IDs claude and codex. The native CLIs can still need their usual project-trust approval. This first workspace uses trusted local execution to preserve normal configuration, tools, skills, MCPs, native approval behavior and history. It does not isolate host files. Peer collaboration and autonomous wakeups start disabled.

This journey requires a fresh, unused workspace name. If try-agentmux already belongs to an earlier test, choose another name consistently in every command. Reopening an old workspace retains its permissions and memory, so it cannot establish the initial deny-by-default results below. A saved workspace is not silently repointed at a different project.

docs.title: 3. Use the terminal workbench
docs.text:
amx label claude "Explore the project" --session try-agentmux
amx label codex "Review the approach" --session try-agentmux
amx dashboard --session try-agentmux

Press Tab to focus the session sidebar, select a session with ↑/↓ and press Enter. Ask it to describe the playground without changing files. Handle native trust/tool prompts normally. Press F1 (or Ctrl-b, release, then g) to return to the workbench.

Try / to search, Shift+L to edit its title, Shift+V to edit its role, Shift+N to add a session, ? for context help, and ←/→ or 1–8 to change views. Tab switches sidebar/content focus; ↑/↓ navigates that focused area. Left/right works across all eight views. In Connections (Links on narrow terminals) and Teams, use h/l or Alt+←/→ to choose the recipient or action target. The footer follows the current view and selection; uppercase letters mean hold Shift. Titles can change or repeat; commands still use the stable IDs. A role update changes future managed turns and sends a native inbox notice. In the default Manual mode it does not start a native turn; Review/Auto can deliver updated role and boundary context.

On current main, Shift+N reviews the inherited provider, project and coordinated/native-only choice, the provider-default model and trusted local host execution. Ctrl+O in its title editor opens advanced settings. It does not copy an existing model override or sandbox.

For pairing existing sessions, use 3 Connections, choose a recipient with h/l or Alt+←/→, then c. 7 Teams is for consent-based teams created by agents with permission; an empty Teams view is normal for this everyday preset.

Detach with Ctrl-b, release, then d. The sessions keep running. Runtime services are separate from the agent windows. To inspect their logs, press Ctrl-b, release, then Shift+D. From an agent terminal, Ctrl-b b opens the Board popup; from the workbench, press 1 for Board directly.

docs.title: 4. Keep both native sessions open
docs.text:
In one terminal window:

amx attach claude --session try-agentmux

In another:

amx attach codex --session try-agentmux

Expected: both are normal native CLI conversations. Switching sessions in one attachment does not switch the other attachment. Each attachment also has its own dashboard selection and drafts. Keep a separate regular shell for owner commands in the following steps.

docs.title: 5. Verify the initial communication boundary
docs.text:
Paste this into Claude's native conversation, not the owner shell:

Use "$AGENTMUX_CLI" managed call boundaries.get to inspect your current
permissions. Then attempt message.send with JSON
{"to":["codex"],"text":"Initial boundary probe"}.
Report the broker result. Do not change policy or use files to communicate.

Expected: Claude's agent credential receives forbidden for the peer message. Use its normal shell tool and approve that specific call if the native CLI asks. The owner CLI has broader authority: running amx send as the owner does not test a peer's permission boundary.

docs.title: 6. Connect only this pair
docs.text:
In the owner shell:

amx collaborate claude codex --session try-agentmux
amx board "Test proposal: keep parsing separate from persistence." --session try-agentmux

Keep the printed Group, Board and Memory values. This creates a dedicated scope for this member set and enables peer notes/pings. It contributes no peer command authority. The original team and project namespaces do not become shared merely because this group exists.

Ask Claude:

Re-read your effective Agentmux boundaries using the authenticated CLI bridge.
Read the newly allowed group board. In its shared-memory namespace, save a new
key demo-greeting with value HELLO_FROM_CLAUDE using memory.put and version 0.
Send Codex a direct informational note telling it which namespace/key to read.
Use only the broker; do not edit files or change permissions.

Then ask Codex:

Read your current Agentmux boundaries and broker inbox. Read the group board
and the shared-memory key demo-greeting. Report the exact saved value and send
Claude a short informational acknowledgment through the broker.

Expected: Codex reports HELLO_FROM_CLAUDE; the board and acknowledgments appear in the workbench. Native sessions read coordination when asked; a note does not automatically type into or wake a native conversation.

docs.title: 7. Compare notes with queued instructions
docs.text:
In the owner shell:

amx send codex "Informational test note; no task requested." --mode note --session try-agentmux
amx send codex "Test task: summarize the board proposal." --mode instruction --session try-agentmux
amx inbox --session try-agentmux

Expected: the first creates a message; the second creates a task visible in Tasks. In the default Manual delivery mode, neither starts a native turn. Open the task with o, search with f, and use PgUp/PgDn for history. Return from the reader and cancel this demonstration task with c after inspection, so it does not remain pending across reopening. In a managed worker workflow, eligible queued tasks are claimed and executed instead.

Copy the exact inspection command printed by send, or use:

amx tasks --to codex --session try-agentmux
amx task TASK_ID --open --session try-agentmux

Replace TASK_ID with the queued task's ID. --open goes straight to that exact task in Tasks, including older records, and shows its current version and recovery evidence. Opening changes no task state. When recovery is available, Ctrl+K offers a separate review and confirmation against the exact task/version. Tasks for selected session in terminal/web Actions provides the recipient's complete paginated history.

docs.title: Try an approved native turn
docs.text:
New integrated sessions can also receive attributed instructions directly in their native conversation. In the owner shell:

amx delivery codex review --session try-agentmux
amx send codex "Reply with one sentence about the board proposal." --mode instruction --session try-agentmux
amx delivery codex --session try-agentmux

Copy the exact pending candidate ID, then approve it:

amx delivery codex --approve CANDIDATE_ID --session try-agentmux

Expected: Codex receives the attributed turn, and Tasks shows transport progress and a correlated result. A queued/submitted item is not yet proof of execution. 2 Sessions → Shift+D edits receiver delivery; Shift+A reviews an item. Auto removes per-item approval while retaining limits and permissions. Peer commands additionally require the sender's directional Commands grant. Return to Manual with amx delivery codex manual --session try-agentmux. See native collaboration for provider differences, subscriptions and upgrading a workspace whose controller predates this feature.

docs.title: 8. Use the web control center
docs.text:
Open an additional regular shell for the web server and keep that process open. Leave the original owner shell available for steps 9–10:

amx web --session try-agentmux --open

If your desktop does not open it, use the full private URL printed by the command. Try Connections for directional relationships and shared access, Groups & teams for the owner group's scope, Memory to inspect demo-greeting, and Tasks for instruction history. Select a session before changing its controls; review the exact sender, recipient and effective permission. Note, ping and instruction authority, and namespace read/write access, are separate controls.

Expected: a black/purple observation and control app. Native typing stays in tmux. Closing the browser does not stop the workspace; Ctrl-C stops this web server only.

docs.title: 9. End collaboration without ending the conversations
docs.text:
amx isolate codex --session try-agentmux

Ask Codex to retry memory.get using the same shared-memory namespace/key from step 6 and message.list explicitly filtered to that old board, then try a direct note to Claude. A generic inbox can still contain authored/direct receipts and is not the revoked-board test. Expected: the revoked operations are denied, while direct native conversation still works. Previously read information remains in its conversation; isolation cannot make it forget. Accepted tasks need separate cancellation.

Reconnect when wanted:

amx collaborate claude codex --session try-agentmux

The same member set reuses its group and saved history. Separate explicit owner denies survive reconnect; review/reset those in Connections/Memory if you added them during step 8. See live permissions.

docs.title: 10. Add a session and test individual recovery
docs.text:
In the original owner shell, which still has amx_demo_project set:

amx add review --harness claude --project "$amx_demo_project" \
  --title "Independent second review" --session try-agentmux
amx sessions --session try-agentmux

The new ID review starts independently. Repeat collaborate only for the IDs you want connected. Use --native-only on an addition for a prompt-free native launch; coordination then needs explicit manual setup/instructions.

Attach to the new review session with amx attach review --session try-agentmux, exit that native CLI normally, then detach with Ctrl-b, release, then d to return to the owner shell. The exited pane can retain its final output. Then test a deliberate same-ID relaunch:

In the workbench, an exited native CLI is marked exited; Enter or Shift+U opens its relaunch review. A clean exit does not mean a failure. You can use the owner shell instead:

amx relaunch review --session try-agentmux
amx attach review --session try-agentmux

The first command requires review to have exited; it refuses a live session. Expected: a fresh native conversation under the same Agentmux ID, with peers untouched. To choose native history deliberately use --resume picker or an exact native conversation ID instead. --resume last means the provider's latest applicable conversation, not an Agentmux title match.

A native CLI may exit normally after updating itself. Review and relaunch that session in the same way; a clean exit is not a crash. New local setups follow the selected public launcher on relaunch. For older saved definitions that freeze a versioned executable, see the explicit launcher recovery option in work sessions.

docs.title: 11. Test discovery or another workspace
docs.text:
To observe a native CLI started outside Agentmux:

amx sessions --session try-agentmux
amx connect OBSERVED_ID --title "Existing conversation" --session try-agentmux

Replace OBSERVED_ID with a currently observed entry. Paste its printed setup into that original native conversation; connecting does not inject it or move the external terminal. Some generic interpreter/non-TTY processes cannot be identified. Existing external conversations remain under your direct control.

amx workspaces lists named and remembered custom locations. Ctrl+W (also Shift+W) opens the chooser. An interactive attachment switches to the selected workspace and retains the previous workbench and drafts. A standalone observer shows an exact attach command when native input needs another server. For an older custom state location, use amx workspaces --register DIRECTORY.

Use amx context --session try-agentmux to explain the ordinary command target without attaching. Outside an attachment, bare amx / amx a selects a sole running workspace or offers a running-workspace chooser; press / or Ctrl+F there to filter by name, state path or status. Commands with an agent ID still default to workspace work outside an owned attachment, so retain the explicit selector used throughout this walkthrough.

docs.title: 12. Stop the test and try isolated/managed workflows
docs.text:
Stop the web process with Ctrl-C in its shell, then:

amx down --session try-agentmux

Expected: only the workspace's owned processes stop. Saved state/history and the playground directory are retained. External bridged terminals stay alive. You can reopen the original definition with the same start command/project; choose previous conversations explicitly through native history controls.

For model-free isolation checks, return to the repository checkout and run:

python3 scripts/smoke-managed.py
python3 scripts/smoke-managed-interactive.py

These require Linux, a supported Bubblewrap (including --size) and working user namespaces. They make no model calls and clean up their temporary runtimes. For a real isolated native workspace, use a fresh workspace name with start --sandbox bubblewrap; isolated credential snapshots and private homes have different customization boundaries from the local workflow above.

Continue with managed setup for role presets and selected providers, persistent/autonomous workflows for managed task execution, and research for observable, preregistered studies. The work-session guide and command reference cover the full controls.

docs.title: Existing workspace mode
docs.text: The following flow is a separate, optional tutorial for the original layout compiler. It creates tmux panes without the managed broker's authenticated board, memory or permissions.

docs.title: 1. Create a Configuration
docs.text:
Agentmux uses declarative YAML files to define your workspace. You can create one from scratch, but it's easier to use a built-in starter template.

# See available templates
amx templates

# Initialize a standard AI development workspace
amx init ai-dev my-workflow.yaml

docs.title: 2. Review the Plan
docs.text:
Before launching, you can ask Agentmux to show you exactly what it intends to do:

amx render my-workflow.yaml

You'll see a breakdown of the windows, panes, commands, and environment variables that will be created.

docs.title: 3. Launch the Session
docs.text:
To create the tmux session and attach to it:

amx load my-workflow.yaml

Welcome to your new workspace! You should see your editor on the left and a dedicated pane for your AI agent on the right.

docs.title: 4. Live Modifications
docs.text:
If you realize you want to change the layout or add a new pane, you don't need to kill the session.

  1. Detach from tmux (Prefix + d).
  2. Edit your configuration file (amx edit my-workflow).
  3. Reload the session non-destructively:
amx reload my-workflow.yaml

For supported changes, reload reconciles the layout and updates affected panes. Structural changes that cannot be reconciled in place can recreate the session and interrupt its processes; inspect the rendered configuration before reloading.

docs.title: Start a native work session
docs.text:
Use your existing Claude Code and Codex subscriptions. This page covers ordinary setup; the optional verification walkthrough tests every permission and recovery boundary in detail.

Task pairing and automatic installed-provider selection require Agentmux v0.15.0. An existing workspace retains its pinned controller until explicitly upgraded; a fresh workspace uses the installed binary.

docs.title: 1. Install and sign in once
docs.text:
Install Agentmux. Native sessions require tmux 3.2+ and the native CLIs you want to use. Open Claude Code and Codex directly and complete their normal subscription login and project-trust prompts.

You keep the native tools' configuration, skills, history and approval behavior. Ordinary sessions use trusted local execution. Strict Linux isolation is an explicit advanced option.

docs.title: 2. Start your project and pair for tasks
docs.text:
From the project directory:

amx start --detach
amx pair claude codex --delivery auto

The pairing command is a preview. It shows both identities, command permissions, delivery modes, returned results, existing queues and limits. --apply checks and prints the current review again before its atomic update:

amx pair claude codex --delivery auto --apply
amx attach claude

Ask Claude to delegate a specific task to Codex, for example running a check or reviewing a file. Instructions arrive as agent-attributed turns, and returned results need no separate reverse message permission.

Pairing enables mutual Commands and own-result delivery in one atomic update. It leaves message/ping grants, shared boards/memory and existing limits alone. Auto can start eligible existing queued work and future work from all permitted senders, not just this pair. Use --delivery review if you want to approve each exact queued item. Native readiness and limits still govern when turns run.

For another workspace, add -s NAME to every command. Existing workspaces keep their controller version; start a fresh name or follow deliberate upgrade/recovery.

docs.title: 3. Work and inspect
docs.text:
F1 returns to the workbench. Ctrl+P finds sessions and Ctrl+K finds actions. In Connections, [ chooses sender focus and ] chooses recipient focus; ↑/↓ changes that identity. Shift+C reviews task pairing, Shift+D reviews delivery settings and Shift+A approves an exact item.

From an owner shell:

amx observe
amx tasks
amx task TASK_ID

Tasks show what was queued, delivered and verified separately. Use the exact printed task ID; observability explains uncertainty and stale reporting. For a checked coding request in a separate worktree, use amx work; its preview selects installed providers without starting a model.

Detach with Ctrl-b, release, then d to keep the workspace running. amx down stops its owned processes and retains history. See everyday commands for adding and relaunching sessions.

docs.title: Existing workspace mode
docs.text: The original YAML layout compiler is a separate workflow. Its optional walkthrough covers templates, init, render, load and reload.

docs.title: Legacy layout handoff tutorial
docs.text:
For your first native Claude/Codex team with scoped communication, use the optional verification walkthrough. This separate tutorial demonstrates the original v1 layout compiler with two shell commands; it makes no model calls and provides no per-agent broker ACLs or sandboxes.

We will create a Planner agent that writes a task, and a Worker agent that waits for the task to be ready before starting.

docs.title: 1. The Configuration
docs.text:
Create a file named my-team.yaml with the following content:

version: 1
session: first-team

agents:
  planner:
    provider: command
    # The planner does some work, then updates the Blackboard
    command: |
      printf "Thinking about the architecture...\n"
      sleep 3
      printf "Plan complete.\n"
      amx kv-set first-team status "PLAN_READY"
      exec $SHELL

  worker:
    provider: command
    # The worker uses the 'wait' command to block until the planner is done
    command: |
      printf "Worker waiting for the plan...\n"
      # Block until the planner pane outputs the specific string
      amx wait first-team planner "Plan complete"

      # Now the worker can proceed safely
      printf "\n[STARTING] Executing the plan!\n"
      exec $SHELL

layout:
  - window: workflow
    layout: even-horizontal
    panes:
      - name: planner
        agent: planner
        title: "Agent: Planner"
      - name: worker
        agent: worker
        title: "Agent: Worker"

docs.title: 2. Launching the Team
docs.text:
Start the session:

amx load my-team.yaml

When tmux opens, you will see two panes side-by-side.

Watch closely: The Worker (on the right) will explicitly say "waiting for the plan..." and will pause. It will not continue until the Planner (on the left) prints "Plan complete."

docs.title: 3. Mission Control
docs.text:
Once the team is running, detach from tmux (Prefix + d) and open the Mission Control dashboard:

amx dashboard first-team

In the dashboard, you will see your two agents running. Look at the Blackboard (KV) section on the right. You should see status: PLAN_READY. This is the shared memory your planner agent created using kv-set!

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
You have coordinated two tmux pane processes using: 1. Synchronization (wait): Blocking execution based on another pane's output. 2. Shared Memory (kv-set): Storing state that outlives the script execution.

For bounded spawning, consented membership and permission-controlled shared knowledge, continue with dynamic teams. V1 KV and output polling do not establish those controls.

docs.title: Portable layout bundles
docs.text:
This page covers original v1 layout .amx files. It does not package managed credentials, a live coordination store or provider-native history. For portable managed evidence use trace bundles, and for reusable memory use memory export/import.

When you build a great agentic team, you will want to share it. However, if your agents rely on local Python scripts or text files for prompts, just sending the YAML configuration isn't enough.

Agentmux solves this with Portable Bundles (.amx files) and the {{config_dir}} variable.

docs.title: 1. Using {{config_dir}}
docs.text:
The {{config_dir}} variable is automatically injected by Agentmux during configuration load. It represents the absolute path to the directory containing your yaml file.

You should always use this variable when referencing local files.

Bad: 

agents:
  researcher:
    command: "python3 ./scripts/scrape.py" # Breaks if launched from another folder!

Good: 

agents:
  researcher:
    command: "python3 {{config_dir}}/scripts/scrape.py"

docs.title: 2. Packing a Bundle
docs.text:
Once you have organized your team into a folder (with the YAML and any scripts), you can create a self-contained bundle.

# Assuming you have a folder: my-team/session.yaml, my-team/script.sh
amx pack my-team/session.yaml session.amx

This creates session.amx in the current directory. Without the second path, the default name comes from the YAML's session, not its filename. The ZIP contains the YAML's directory tree, excluding root .git, .cache, .tmp, bin, other .amx files and the output itself. Review the directory before packing; the bundle contains the remaining files rather than a minimal dependency manifest.

docs.title: 3. Distributing the Bundle
docs.text:
You can now send session.amx to anyone. They don't need to extract it manually. Agentmux handles it transparently:

amx load session.amx

docs.title: Remote Loading
docs.text:
Because .amx files are self-contained, they are perfect for HTTP distribution. You can host them on GitHub Releases, S3, or your own server, and users can launch them with a single command:

amx load https://your-server.com/downloads/my-team.amx

Agentmux downloads/unpacks the bundle into a temporary directory and launches its configured commands, using {{config_dir}} to resolve local paths. Loading a bundle executes those commands; it is not a sandbox or a signature-verification workflow.
